rows.title: Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions - composition, functions, removal
sub: Group-II M1-B-49: Union and State Public Service Commissions - composition, functions and removal

secs.t: UPSC history — Acts and commissions → year

x: The Government of India Act, 1919 first provided for a Public Service Commission; the 1935 Act created the Federal PSC and provincial PSCs.
ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the
Montagu-Chelmsford reforms
Sir Ross Barker
was the first Chairman of the Public Service Commission set up on 1 October 1926 on the Lee Commission's advice.

secs.t: Articles 315-323 (Part XIV) → provisions

x: Article 318 covers regulations on conditions of service, Article 319 the bar on holding office after ceasing to be a member, and Article 322 expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund.
The correct sequence is Article 320 (functions), Article 321 (extension), Article 322 (expenses), and Article 323 (reports).
Article 317 deals with removal and suspension of members.

secs.t: Appointment, term and post-retirement bar — UPSC vs SPSC vs JSPSC (Art. 316, 319)

x: UPSC members retire at 65 years and SPSC members at 62 years, subject in both cases to the six-year term.
The Governor appoints SPSC members but only the President removes them.
At least half of the members must have held office under the Government of India or a State Government for a minimum of ten years.
A UPSC member may become Chairman of the UPSC or Chairman of an SPSC, but cannot take other government employment or serve a second term in the same office.

secs.t: Removal and suspension of members — Art. 317

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2019 - SPSC chairman
appointed by Governor, removed by President
Exam angle: "Governor appoints, President removes" for SPSC chairman is the favourite trap.
Misbehaviour includes
being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit
under Article 317(4).
During the Supreme Court inquiry, the President may suspend a UPSC member and the Governor may suspend an SPSC member.

secs.t: Functions — consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321) — Functions (Art. 320)

x: UPSC conducts examinations for appointment to All-India services, Central services and Group-A services.
The manner of reservation for SCs and STs is outside UPSC's consultation function.
Claims of SCs and STs, temporary appointments of less than one year, and Group B and C posts are excluded.
The President (Governor for an SPSC) may exclude posts by regulations.

secs.t: Functions — consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321) — Extension and nature of advice

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2022 - "manner of reservation" is
not
a UPSC function.
Under Article 321 functions are extended only by an Act of Parliament (State Legislature for an SPSC), not by executive order.
The disciplinary role is shared by UPSC and the Central Vigilance Commission.
The SPSC is described as the watchdog of the
merit system
in public services.

secs.t: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice (Art. 323)

x: The UPSC annual report is accompanied by a memorandum explaining cases in which its advice was not accepted.
Every case of non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by
the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
; an individual ministry cannot reject the advice on its own.
The UPSC report follows the President-Parliament route, while an SPSC report follows the Governor-State Legislature route.

secs.t: JSPSC and APPSC — bodies → features

x: The Joint State Public Service Commission submits its report to each concerned Governor, who lays it before the relevant State Legislature.
After bifurcation, APPSC continued for residuary Andhra Pradesh, Telangana constituted TSPSC, and the Governor appoints APPSC members.
The APPSC conducts recruitment examinations for State services and examinations for the lower judicial service under Article 234.
The Governor of AP appoints the APPSC Chairman and members, but only the President can remove them (Art 317), so C is right.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Paper leaks, flawed evaluation, delays and litigation are identified as major concerns, with the Telangana 2023 and Bihar 2024 examinations cited as examples.
Satyendranath Tagore was selected in 1863 and is recorded as the first Indian to clear the ICS in 1864.
Public Service Commissions are called the
watchdog of the merit system
because they ensure recruitment to civil services on merit.

rows.title: Finance Commission - composition, terms of reference, functions; 15th and 16th Finance Commission
sub: Group-II M1-B-47: Finance Commission - composition, functions and recent recommendations

secs.t: Finance Commission — Articles, Act, composition and status

x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the
Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951
, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
Special knowledge of Government finance and accounts, wide experience in financial matters and administration, and special knowledge of economics are prescribed areas.

secs.t: Finance Commissions → constitution, award period, members and FIRSTs

x: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, had constitution-based Terms of Reference, and was the first to use Contribution to GDP as a criterion.
Population based on the 2011 Census received a weight of
under the 16th Finance Commission, compared with 15% under the 15th Finance Commission.
T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda and Soumya Kanti Ghosh were members of the 16th FC.

secs.t: Devolution → vertical share and criteria data

x: The 14th Finance Commission made tax devolution the main route instead of grants and ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction.
The 15th Finance Commission added
demographic performance and tax effort
as new criteria.
Contribution to GDP
was introduced as a new criterion by the 16th Finance Commission with a weight of 10%.
Area and demographic performance received lower weights, forest and ecology remained unchanged, and tax and fiscal effort was dropped.

secs.t: Grants → local bodies, disaster and deficits data

x: Local-body grants were ₹2,87,436 crore under the 14th FC, ₹4.36 lakh crore under the 15th FC and ₹7.91 lakh crore under the 16th FC.

The 16th FC's ₹7.91 lakh crore local-body grants split into about ₹4.35 lakh crore (≈₹4.4 lakh crore) for rural and ₹3.56 lakh crore (≈₹3.6 lakh crore) for urban local bodies, the urban share being 45%.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh and the Finance Commission — grants, share, special category status

x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission allocation for Andhra Pradesh is ₹16,627 crore for rural local bodies, ₹12,158 crore for urban local bodies and ₹6,125 crore for disaster-related grants.
Andhra Pradesh's share was 4.305 per cent under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, 4.047 per cent under the Fifteenth, and 4.217 per cent under the Sixteenth.
Andhra Pradesh sought higher vertical devolution and criteria addressing capital-city and infrastructure costs resulting from post-bifurcation imbalances.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Cesses and surcharges are not generally part of the divisible pool, so their increasing use shrinks the pool available for devolution.
Andhra Pradesh was stated to have lost up to
₹38,000 crore
in Central grants after revenue deficit grants were dropped.
Kerala
was identified as facing fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission gave it neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants.

rows.title: Comptroller and Auditor General - appointment, duties, types of audit, audit reports and PAC linkage
sub: Group-II M1-B-50: Comptroller and Auditor General of India - appointment, duties and audit reports

secs.t: CAG — official name, Articles 148-151 and the 1971 Act

x: The CAG’s duties, powers and conditions of service are governed by the Comptroller and Auditor General’s Act of 1971, made under Articles 148 and 149.
Although Union accounts were separated from audit in 1976,
the CAG continues to keep most State accounts
The Act provides for
compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators

secs.t: CAG — appointment, term, removal, salary and independence

x: Exam angle: "whose term is longest - President, LS member, CAG, VP?" →
CAG
The CAG takes the oath before the President, in the form prescribed in the
Third Schedule
The CAG receives a salary equal to that of a Supreme Court judge.
Salary, leave, pension and retirement age cannot be varied to the CAG’s disadvantage after appointment.
No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament
The term is 6 years or age 65.

secs.t: Persons → CAG FIRSTs, titles and statements

x: V. Narahari Rao
was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
K. Sanjay Murthy
is mentioned as the CAG of India for 2026.
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the CAG as
the most important officer under the Constitution
Former CAG
Vinod Rai
authored “When Audit Matters.”.

secs.t: CAG duties and types of audit — Art. 149, limits — What he audits (Art. 149)

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2017 wrong statement - "CAG controls the entire financial system of the country".
The CAG audits public finances but does not control the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund.
The CAG cannot audit secret service expenditure and instead accepts a certificate from the competent authority.

secs.t: CAG duties and types of audit — Art. 149, limits — Types of audit

x: A legal and regulatory audit is obligatory and examines whether money was legally available and spent in accordance with applicable rules.
Financial attest audit is an obligatory audit concerned with the truthfulness of accounts and their conformity with the reporting framework.
Social audits feed into the CAG's performance audits, which test the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes; MGNREGA social audit standards were issued in 2016.

secs.t: Audit reports, Public Accounts Committee and landmark reports

x: Article 151
deals with the submission and laying of the CAG’s audit reports before the appropriate legislature.
Reports relating to public sector undertakings are referred to the
Committee on Public Undertakings
, while the PAC examines the other relevant CAG reports.
The CAG acts as the PAC’s
friend, philosopher and guide
by assisting it in examining audit findings.
The 2010 2G spectrum report, prepared during Vinod Rai's tenure, referred to a presumptive loss of
₹1.76 lakh crore

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The CAG was
auditing 101 cities for ease of living
, including urban-mobility concerns.
The 5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit hosted by India in 2026 was associated with the theme of
ease of living and urban mobility
The CAG is using AI/ML-based audits to detect fraud in welfare schemes and is expanding remote audits.

rows.title: Attorney General and Advocate General; Solicitor General
sub: Group-II M1-B-51: Attorney General of India and the Advocate General of the State

secs.t: Law officers — Articles, legal basis and order of precedence

x: The Attorney General is placed at 11, the Solicitor General at 23, and the Additional Solicitors General and Advocates General at 25 in the stated order of precedence.
Article 88 gives the AG the right to speak in Parliament, and Article 177 gives the Advocate General the same right in the State Legislature; neither can vote.

secs.t: Attorney General — Article 76, appointment, term, removal, duties — Status and appointment

x: Article 76 requires the Attorney General to satisfy the qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge, including the stated judicial, advocacy or eminent-jurist qualifications.

References concerning the Attorney General go through the Ministry of Law; law officers conventionally resign after a change of government; and only the Attorney General is constitutionally created, under Article 76.

secs.t: Attorney General — Article 76, appointment, term, removal, duties — Duties

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - "qualified to be an SC judge" and "advises GoI" are correct; a "fixed term" statement is wrong (LENS Oct 2025 practice question also tests "fixed five-year term" - false).
Exam angle: "Who is the highest law officer?" → AG (not CJI, not Law Minister).
References to the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law, and consultation is confined to
legal matters of real importance

secs.t: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General — status, appointment, role

x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, is appointed through the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, and has a three-year term.
The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General advise the government and represent the Government of India before courts.
Under the Advocates Act, 1961, the Attorney General and Solicitor General are ex officio members of the
Bar Council of India

secs.t: Advocate General — Article 165, duties, Art. 177

x: Article 165 requires the Advocate General to be qualified for appointment as a
Judge of a High Court
Under Article 177, the Advocate General may speak and participate in the Legislature and its committees when entitled to do so, but has no right to vote.
Article 194(4)
extends legislative privileges to the Advocate General in the State Legislature.

secs.t: Persons → Attorneys General, Solicitors General and Advocates General (FIRST and current)

x: M.C. Setalvad was the first, followed by Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal and R. Venkataramani in the sequence represented here.
K.K. Venugopal served as Attorney General of India from 2017 to 2022.
R. Venkataramani
is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026.
C.K. Daphtary
was the first Solicitor General of India.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The convention is criticised because the resignation of all law officers after a change of government can make the offices appear tied to the ruling party rather than being institutionally independent.
The Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to communicate directions to all Advocates General concerning
facilities for senior citizens

rows.title: National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B)
sub: Group-II M1-B-52: National Commissions for SCs, STs and Backward Classes; Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

secs.t: Articles, Amendments, Acts and cases → commissions — Evolution - Article / Amendment table

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2022 - NCBC got constitutional status by the
102nd
Amendment.
The
65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990
created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 338.
NCST was established on 19 February 2004 under
Article 338A
, inserted through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

secs.t: Articles, Amendments, Acts and cases → commissions — NCBC - case, Act and Amendments

x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
The direction in Indra Sawhney led to the NCBC Act, 1993 and the establishment of the statutory NCBC.
The 102nd Amendment removed backward classes from the purview of the NCSC while constitutionalising the NCBC under Article 338B.

secs.t: Commissions — composition

x: Each Commission has five members in all, appointed by the President by warrant, with service conditions and tenure fixed by the President.
The term of office of the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members is
three years
under the applicable rules.
The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.

secs.t: Functions and powers — NCSC, NCST, NCBC — Functions of NCSC / NCST

x: The Commissions investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on development; they do not function as criminal courts or award criminal punishment.
The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.
The reporting arrangement includes annual or need-based reports, transmission of State-related reports to the Governor and laying before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.

secs.t: Functions and powers — NCSC, NCST, NCBC — Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

x: Article 338
provides the constitutional basis for the powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
Proposals for de-reservation of posts must first be examined by the relevant NCSC, NCST or NCBC, depending on the category concerned.

secs.t: Persons → chairpersons (FIRST and current)

x: S.H. Ramdhan was the first chairperson of the combined commission (1992).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism identified is that recommendations are advisory only and that the National Commission for Minorities has experienced long vacancies, a matter noted by the Delhi High Court in 2026.
Niranjan Jyoti
was appointed Chairperson of the NCBC in 2026.
Harjit Singh Grewal
headed the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026.

rows.title: Statutory bodies - NHRC and SHRCs, National Commission for Women, NCPCR, National Commission for Minorities
sub: Group-II S3-46: Statutory commissions - NCSC, NCST, NCBC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NHRC and their state counterparts

secs.t: Commissions → Act, Article, status and year

x: Exam angle: match-the-Act-with-year pairs; "which of these is NOT a constitutional body".
Exam angle: a list-matching question on bodies and Articles; "NHRC is constitutional" is a trap.
The NCBC was statutory under the NCBC Act, 1993, became constitutional under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment, 2018, and the 89th Amendment, 2003 separated the NCSC and NCST.
The NHRC is a statutory body set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; calling it constitutional is a common trap.

secs.t: NCSK — Act, lapse and tenure extensions

x: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004, after which the NCSK continued as a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the NCSK for
three years beyond 31 March 2022
, taking the tenure up to 31 March 2025.
The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.

secs.t: Human rights conventions and child-rights Acts → year

x: The UDHR dates to 1948, the ICCPR and ICESCR to 1966, CEDAW to 1979 and the Convention against Torture to 1984.
Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December to commemorate the adoption of the
Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989, and India acceded to it in 1992.

secs.t: NHRC and SHRCs — composition, appointment, powers — NHRC establishment

x: The Paris Principles were adopted in October 1991, the Ordinance was promulgated on 28 September 1993, the NHRC was established on 12 October 1993, and UNGA endorsement followed on 20 December 1993.
For misbehaviour or incapacity, the President removes an NHRC member after the Supreme Court inquires into the charge.

secs.t: NHRC and SHRCs — composition, appointment, powers — Appointment

x: SHRCs are governed by the PHRA, the Centre can assign them certain UT functions, but Delhi remains with the NHRC.
The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, which includes the Union Home Minister and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
During inquiries, the NHRC has the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, calling for documents and receiving evidence on affidavit.

secs.t: NHRC and SHRCs — composition, appointment, powers — SHRC

x: The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to matters in the State List and Concurrent List, but it cannot inquire into a matter already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.

The Governor appoints SHRC members on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition (plus the Council Chairman and its LoP where a Council exists).

secs.t: NCW, NCPCR, NCM — composition and functions — Composition and appointment compared (Group-II table)

x: The National Commission for Women was constituted in
January 1992
under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
The Chairperson, five Members and Member-Secretary of the NCW are nominated by
the Central Government
The NCM is appointed by the Central Government, not by the President.

secs.t: NCW, NCPCR, NCM — composition and functions — NCW — functions (Section 10)

x: The NCW may review laws, suggest amendments, take suo motu notice and commission special studies.
The NCW may regulate its own procedure.
Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings conducted to hear and address women’s grievances.

secs.t: NCW, NCPCR, NCM — composition and functions — NCPCR and SCPCRs

x: Section
of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 concerns the 25 per cent reservation of seats for children in specified private unaided schools.
SCPCRs operate under the CPCR Act, 2005, alongside the NCPCR, and address child-rights directions including school menstrual-hygiene measures.
Six
communities are notified as minorities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis, with Jains added on 27 January 2014 as the latest notified minority.

secs.t: Persons → chairpersons of commissions (present and first)

x: Vijaya Rahatkar chairs NCW, Justice V. Ramasubramanian chairs NHRC, Kishor Makwana chairs NCSC and Antar Singh Arya chairs NCST.
Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson, Justice Ranganath Misra the first NHRC Chairperson, Suraj Bhan the first separate NCSC Chairperson and Kunwar Singh the first NCST Chairperson.
Harjit Singh Grewal
was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026.

secs.t: AP commissions → Act, place and 2026 work — AP State Commission for Women (Mahila Commission)

x: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission is a State Human Rights Commission established under the
Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Rayapati Sailaja
is the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women.
The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs was established under the 2003 Act and was reconstituted in 2016 through an amendment to that Act.

secs.t: AP commissions → Act, place and 2026 work — AP State Commission for SCs and STs

x: K.S. Jawahar
was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes while reviewing SC/ST welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore.
Reports of State commissions go to the Governor and are laid before the State Legislature.
Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: In August 2026, the
National Commission for Scheduled Castes
began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts.
The NHRC sought reports in connection with the alleged custodial death of
Gade Sai Krishna
A long vacancy affected the NCM, and an adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026; the NHRC was not dissolved.

rows.title: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - structure, jurisdiction, working; Central Vigilance Commission
sub: Group-II M1-B-57: Lokpal - evolution of the demand and the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013
Group-II M1-B-58: Lokpal - composition, jurisdiction, powers and working
Group-II M1-B-59: Lokayukta - state-level institutions; the Lokayukta in Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Ombudsman — terms, origin and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "first Lokpal Bill introduced in" =
Exam angle: the options mix 1968 (first introduced) with 1969 (first passed by the Lok Sabha) - read the verb.
The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by
Dr. L.M. Singhvi
Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.

secs.t: Committees and commissions → Lokpal recommendations

x: The First ARC recommended Lokpal at the Union level and Lokayukta in the States.
The First ARC was chaired by
Morarji Desai
during 1966–70.
The First ARC’s recommendation dates to 1966, the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007, and the Santhanam Committee operated during 1962–64.
The First Administrative Reforms Commission functioned from 1966 to 1970 and was chaired by Morarji Desai.

secs.t: Lokpal Bills and the 2013 Act → year and date — Bill history

x: The First Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
The correct order is introduction in 1968, passage by the Lok Sabha in 1969, re-introduction in 2008, and passage by Parliament in December 2013.
The Rajya Sabha debate remained unfinished and the Bill was sent to a Rajya Sabha Select Committee.

secs.t: Lokpal Bills and the 2013 Act → year and date — Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 — dates and nature

x: The President gave assent on 1 January 2014, while the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on
27 March 2019
after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.

secs.t: Lokpal Bills and the 2013 Act → year and date — Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Amendment) Act 2016 - asset declaration

x: The 2016 amendment provided that the form and manner would be prescribed by the Central Government; it did not place the prescription in the Constitution.

secs.t: Persons → roles in the Lokpal movement

x: India Against Corruption was led by
Anna Hazare
and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.
The fasts were held at Jantar Mantar in April 2011 and at Ramlila Maidan in August 2011.
All four statements correctly identify the chairpersons and members of the Government and civil society sides of the April 2011 Joint Drafting Committee.

secs.t: Lokpal — composition, eligibility, term and selection — Composition

x: A former Chief Justice of India, former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person with 25 years' relevant experience may qualify.
The term is five years or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier, and reappointment is not permitted.
The Chairperson is assisted by not more than eight members, and at least 50% of the members must be judicial.

secs.t: Lokpal — composition, eligibility, term and selection — Appointment and selection

x: The
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
The Search Committee is constituted by the Selection Committee, prepares a panel, has at least seven persons and must satisfy the specified representation requirement.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be a Member of Parliament or a Member of a Legislative Assembly.

secs.t: Lokpal — jurisdiction and time limits — Who is covered

x: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal.
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
The Prime Minister’s excluded areas include international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space.
The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the
Prevention of Corruption Act

secs.t: Lokpal — jurisdiction and time limits — Time limits

x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.
The Inquiry Wing is required to submit its report within
60 days
after a reference.
A preliminary inquiry ordinarily has a 90-day limit and may be extended by another 90 days.
The Special Court trial has a one-year limit extendable up to two years.

secs.t: Lokpal — powers and wings (Sections)

x: The Lokpal’s framework includes prosecution before the Special Court, specified CBI superintendence, civil-court powers and attachment or confiscation of tainted property during pending prosecution.
The Lokpal’s inquiry wing under Section 11 and its prosecution wing were reported as still not fully staffed.

secs.t: Persons → Lokpal chairpersons and bench

x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.
The Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019, Justice Ghose left office on 27 May 2022, and Justice Khanwilkar became Chairperson on 10 March 2024.
Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose
, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the first Lokpal in March 2019.

secs.t: Lokpal in office — issues, cases and criticism

x: The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal's 12 November 2025 order sanctioning a chargesheet in the Mahua Moitra matter and held that the law had been 'mutilated'.

secs.t: State Lokayuktas — States → Act year and the 2013 mandate

x: Lokayuktas are established under the respective State Acts, and there is no uniformity among States regarding jurisdiction, coverage of the Chief Minister or judicial qualifications.
The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under
Justice N. Santosh Hegde
The report led to the Chief Minister’s resignation, the arrest of former minister G. Janardhana Reddy, cancellation of mining leases and recovery of thousands of crores.

secs.t: State Lokayuktas — State-wise structure, appointment and jurisdiction

x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the
Governor
Lokayuktas generally rely on State investigating agencies, and their recommendations are advisory in many States.
Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta; Punjab has officials designated as Lokpal; Maharashtra has a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.
Rajasthan
cut its Lokayukta's tenure from eight to five years (APPSC G1 2018 key).
Section 7 of the Rajasthan Act keeps sexual harassment, caste discrimination and violence outside the Lokayukta's investigation subjects (RPSC 2024 key).

secs.t: AP Lokayukta — Act, holders, data and other anti-corruption bodies — Law and features

x: The 1983 Act was amended by the
Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta (Amendment) Act, 2024
The Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta have differentiated functions, and the stated coverage includes the Chief Minister and MLAs.
The AP Lokayukta offers informal procedure, easy access, almost free and prompt service, and independence from executive control.
The Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta constitute a statutory ombudsman institution under the 1983 Act.

secs.t: AP Lokayukta — Act, holders, data and other anti-corruption bodies — Holders

x: Justice A. Sambasiva Rao
was the first Lokayukta of the integrated State of Andhra Pradesh.
Governor S. Abdul Nazeer
appointed Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao under Section 3(1), on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.

secs.t: AP Lokayukta — Act, holders, data and other anti-corruption bodies — Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.
R. Jayalakshmi
headed the Andhra Pradesh Anti-Corruption Bureau at the Inspector General level as of April 2026.
Many Lokayuktas lack an independent investigating wing and therefore depend on the State police or the Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally.
The criticisms and debates have included a suggestion for constitutional status for the Lokayukta and the adoption of a model Lokayukta Act.
Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants.

rows.title: Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions; CBI and its legal basis
sub: Group-II M1-B-60: Central Vigilance Commission, CBI and the anti-corruption framework

secs.t: CIC, CBI and CVC — status, origin and FIRSTs

x: The Special Police Establishment originated in 1941, the DSPE Act was enacted in 1946, the CBI was set up in 1963, and the CVC was set up in 1964.
D.P. Kohli
was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC 2018 key); an annual memorial lecture is held in his name.

secs.t: Acts and Sections — RTI Act, DSPE Act, CVC Act

x: The 2019 Amendment lets the Centre fix tenure and salaries.
When the application concerns life or liberty, information must be provided within
48 hours
The ordinary response period is 30 days, while applicants belonging to the Below Poverty Line category are entitled to information free of cost.
Public Information Officers are designated by each public authority under Section 5.

secs.t: Committees and cases — Santhanam, Vineet Narain, Second ARC

x: The CBI was set up in 1963 following the recommendation of the
Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
, constituted during 1962–64.
The Supreme Court in Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997) quashed the Single Directive that required prior sanction to investigate senior officers.
The 1997 Vineet Narain judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and prescribed a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director.

secs.t: Appointing authority, composition and tenure → who picks whom

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025 keyed "CIC by President, SIC by Governor" as the correct pairs, and CM + LoP + CM-nominated minister for the SIC panel. The
Chief Justice is not a member

The President appoints the Lokpal Chairperson and members on the recommendation of a committee including the Prime Minister, Speaker, Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and an eminent jurist.

secs.t: Appointing authority, composition and tenure → who picks whom — CBI Director

x: The
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
amended the DSPE framework and introduced the present three-member selection committee.
In May 2026,
the Leader of Opposition recorded dissent over the selection
of the new CBI Director.
The 2021 amendments permit extension of the tenure of the CBI and ED Directors by one year at a time, subject to a maximum tenure of five years.

secs.t: Appointing authority, composition and tenure → who picks whom — Other CBI officers

x: All three statements correctly describe the special supervisory and prosecutorial arrangements associated with the CBI.
The Commission consists of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.

secs.t: Functions — CBI mandate, units and CVC role

x: OCSAE deals with online child sexual abuse material; BHARATPOL routes international assistance requests; the CBI is India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol; and the specified cells handle economic offences and bank securities and fraud.
The OCSAE Prevention/Investigation Unit was set up by the CBI in 2019 against online child sexual abuse material (APPSC 2018-style PYQ).

secs.t: Functions — CBI mandate, units and CVC role — CVC role

x: The CVC exercises specified superintendence and makes recommendations, but it does not conduct the trials of CBI corruption cases.
The CVC supervises the CBI in corruption cases and functions as the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act.

secs.t: Enforcement agencies → function and controlling ministry

x: The CBI also investigates economic and special crimes, apart from corruption cases.
The Director of the Enforcement Directorate may
attach property believed to be proceeds of crime
under the PMLA.
The ED is under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

secs.t: General consent and the RTI dilution debate — issues

x: The DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, thereby removing the earlier public-interest override.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 called for re-examination of the RTI Act and floated exemptions for confidential service records and draft policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — ACB, Vigilance Commission, CBI consent

x: The Andhra Pradesh ACB is a State police agency that deals with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
The State Vigilance Commission changed the SPSC's disciplinary role, but the SPSC continues as an independent body.
R. Jayalakshmi is a 2006-batch IPS officer who had previously served as CBI SP and DIG before serving as IGP, AP ACB.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Bench considered whether State Human Rights Commission chairpersons could act as Information Commissioners in States with few RTI appeals, in the context of vacancies.
The criticisms noted for the RTI framework are backlogs and vacancies in Information Commissions, misuse of Section 8 exemptions and attacks on RTI activists (over 100 killed).

rows.title: NITI Aayog - structure, functions, initiatives; contrast with the Planning Commission

secs.t: NITI bodies → composition and role

x: The Governing Council includes the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, Lieutenant Governors of other Union Territories, ex officio members, the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members and special invitees.
NITI Aayog assists States in setting up State Economic and Transformation Units, or SETUs, to prepare
State Vision@2047 plans

secs.t: Indices and reports → subject, edition and AP rank

x: The SDG India Index assesses the progress of States and Union Territories towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
GROW stands for
Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry
NITI Aayog
(earlier the Planning Commission) is the nodal agency for poverty estimation and also brings out the National MPI.
The 2023-24 edition (released July 2024) used 113 indicators; AP scored 74 and was a 'Front Runner'.

secs.t: Initiatives → launch year, coverage and design

x: The Aspirational Blocks Programme, launched in January 2023, covers
513 blocks in 329 districts across 27 States and 4 Union Territories
Sampoornata Abhiyan 2.0 seeks saturation of five key performance indicators in Aspirational Districts and six KPIs in Aspirational Blocks.
The Statement of Intent between NITI Aayog and UNICEF covers
health and nutrition
in aspirational districts and blocks.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — aspirational and backward districts

x: The original aspirational districts of Andhra Pradesh were
Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa
The current set mentioned is Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa.
The split is 4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal, not 3 + 4.
Alluri Sitarama Raju district had the lowest cited literacy rate, at 44.67%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Parliamentary Standing Committee sought
for 2026–27 while criticising the chronic under-use of funds by the Ministry of Planning and NITI Aayog.

The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister attended the 11th Governing Council meeting in June 2026, ASR district topped the Basic Infrastructure theme in March 2026, and Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in EPI 2024.

rows.title: Centralization vs decentralization - concepts, arguments and Indian experience
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-64

secs.t: Centralisation and decentralisation — definitions, forms and dimensions

x: Centralisation concentrates decisions at the apex, such as the Union, the State capital or the headquarters of a department.
Deconcentration remains within the same government, delegation involves semi-autonomous bodies, and devolution empowers elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue.
If the transferring authority can withdraw the power at will, the arrangement is delegation rather than devolution.

secs.t: Persons → views on village self-government

x: Gandhi advocated Gram Swaraj, conceived as
a republic of self-sufficient villages with decentralised economic and political power
The Gandhian Plan of 1944, associated with Sriman Narayan Agarwal, sought
self-contained villages, cottage industry, swadeshi, sarvodaya and trusteeship
Ambedkar criticised the village as a seat of caste domination and called it a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism on 4 November 1948.

secs.t: Articles, Amendments and Bills on local self-government

x: Article 40 represented a compromise: panchayats were named as an objective, reflecting the Gandhian position, but the provision was made non-justiciable, accommodating Ambedkar's reservations.
The 64th Bill passed the Lok Sabha in July 1989, was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989, a fresh Bill followed in 1990, and the 73rd Amendment came into force in 1993.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — subsidiarity and the 3Fs

x: Subsidiarity assigns a function to the lowest competent level and permits movement to a higher level only when the lower level cannot perform it adequately.
The Second Administrative Reforms Commission invoked subsidiarity for
dividing functions between the three tiers of government
Without adequate funds, functions and functionaries, Panchayati Raj Institutions remain implementing agencies instead of becoming effective planning units.

secs.t: Arguments and the Indian experience — issues and debates

x: Nation-building after Partition, along with the requirements of unity and security, was an argument for centralisation.

All three were arguments advanced in favour of centralisation: a single command for planned heavy industry and food security, weak local capacity, and the risk of elite capture by dominant local castes.
India transferred political power, some administrative power and the least fiscal power.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The call for a “structural reset” referred to addressing the increasing centralisation of power and reconsidering the working of federalism in Union-State relations.
The traditional 12-Ayagar village administration under the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara is cited as an example of historical village autonomy in the Andhra region.
Political decentralisation through elections is insufficient by itself.

rows.title: Democratic decentralisation - meaning, objectives and preconditions
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-64

secs.t: Democratic decentralisation — meaning, attributes and FIRSTs

x: Democratic decentralisation means transferring power to elected local bodies so that people participate in decisions affecting them.
Local bodies may have their own funds and taxing powers and enjoy autonomy within State law.
UPSC 2017 keyed '
democratic decentralisation
': power is transferred to elected local bodies.
Rajasthan inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959, and Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959.

secs.t: Committees → recommendations and preconditions

x: The recommended three-tier structure consisted of the
Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
Appointed January 1957 to review the CDP (1952) and NES (1953), it reported in November 1957, and the NDC accepted it in January 1958.
The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that development had become bureaucratised—described as “grass without roots”—and called for restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role.

secs.t: Objectives and outcomes of Panchayati Raj

x: PRIs brought
formal representation of weaker sections
in village governance and were adopted to decentralise democratic power.
People’s participation in development and democratic decentralisation were the fundamental objectives.
The needs identified are decentralisation of decision-making, of administrative powers and of the system as a whole.

secs.t: Articles, programmes and campaigns — Gram Swaraj to People's Plan

x: Gram Swaraj means
a self-reliant village republic
in the Gandhian conception.
The constitutional trace of Gram Swaraj is found in
Article 40
, a Directive Principle of State Policy concerning village panchayats.
The Abhiyan is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, began from 2018–19 and trains PRI members.
SVAMITVA was launched on
24 April 2020
(National Panchayati Raj Day).

secs.t: Global models of local government — Scandinavian and British

x: The Scandinavian model is characterised by strong municipalities, delivery of most welfare services and high local taxes; it is treated as a benchmark for fiscal decentralisation.
In the British model, local councils are creatures of Parliament and are subject to the ultra vires rule; the model also uses a committee system.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: SabhaSaar is an AI tool associated with Gram Sabha minutes.
The 1 July 2026 report highlighted
low participation in Gram Sabha meetings
The J&K DDCs’ term ended on 24 February 2026, and no fresh polls had taken place.

secs.t: Rural development programmes → person, place, year

x: The correct associations are Gurgaon experiment–F.L. Brayne, Sriniketan–Rabindranath Tagore, Marthandam–Spencer Hatch and Baroda–V.T. Krishnamachari.
Sevagram was associated with Mahatma Gandhi, Etawah with Albert Mayer, Nilokheri with S.K. Dey and Marthandam with Spencer Hatch.
The correct order is Gurgaon experiment (1920), Sriniketan (1921), Sevagram (1930s) and Etawah Pilot Project (1948).
CDP 1952, NES 1953, ICDS 1975, IRDP nationwide from 2 October 1980 (piloted 1978-79).

secs.t: Persons → role in community development and Panchayati Raj

x: S.K. Dey was associated with Nilokheri and the Union Ministry of Community Development; Albert Mayer with the Etawah Pilot Project; V.T. Krishnamachari chaired the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee; and Jawaharlal Nehru launched the CDP and inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur.
Balwant Rai Mehta
is popularly called the architect or father of Panchayati Raj because of his Committee’s recommendations on democratic decentralisation.

secs.t: Grow More Food Inquiry, CDP and NES — features and organisation — Grow More Food Inquiry Committee (1952)

x: The Committee found the campaign too narrow and recommended an integrated village-development approach supported by
a nationwide extension organisation
The programme began with 55 community projects functioning as pilot areas.
The CDP was launched on 2 October 1952 (Gandhi Jayanti) during the First Five Year Plan.

secs.t: Grow More Food Inquiry, CDP and NES — features and organisation — CDP — objectives and components

x: Exam angle: year asked directly (1952, not 1950/1957/1959); "aim = public participation" is the keyed option.
The programme was viewed as a step towards implementing Article 40 of the Constitution, which directs the State to organise village panchayats.
The Andhra State Plan was associated with 1953, had Kurnool as its capital and came under the First Five Year Plan; the Community Development Programme formed part of it.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: A Village Level Worker or Gram Sevak served as a
multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages
The
block
(about 100 villages) was the CDP's unit of planning and development, headed by the BDO with a team of extension officers.
Panchayats formed after 1977 on the lines of the Ashok Mehta recommendations are referred to as
Second Generation Panchayats

secs.t: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) → appointment, findings, recommendations — Appointment and report

x: The committee was appointed to examine the working of the Community Development Programme launched in 1952 and the National Extension Service launched in 1953, and to suggest improvements.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in
January 1957
to review the CDP (1952) and the NES (1953); it reported in November 1957.

secs.t: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) → appointment, findings, recommendations — Recommendations

x: Exam angle: "two-tier" and "direct elections to both village panchayat and Zila Parishad" are false. "All planning and development activities entrusted to these bodies" and "Collector as ZP chairman" are true. Keyed answer: c and d. Nyaya Panchayat is NOT one of the three tiers.
The Panchayat Samiti was recommended as the executive body, whereas the Zila Parishad was assigned advisory, coordinating and supervisory functions.

secs.t: FIRSTs, state patterns and phases of Panchayati Raj

x: Exam angle: "first state" = Rajasthan. "First implemented across the entire state in 1959" = Andhra Pradesh.
Andhra Pradesh, the second State to adopt the system, introduced three-tier Panchayati Raj at Shadnagar on
1 November 1959
The NDC did not insist on one rigid pattern for all States; however, the basic principles of Panchayati Raj were to be the same everywhere.

secs.t: Specialist committees of the 1960s-70s → subject; causes of decline

x: The Fifth Plan Working Group on Panchayati Raj, constituted in 1972, was chaired by
N. Ramakrishnayya
Poor finances, irregular elections and supersession, and weak devolution of functions and staff were identified as causes.
Although its name may suggest a statistical body outside the Panchayati Raj field, the V.R. Rao Committee was associated with
Panchayat Statistics
and was a Panchayati Raj committee.

secs.t: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) → appointment, two tiers, recommendations — Appointment and report

x: Exam angle: APPSC (2023, 2025) asked Ashok Mehta = "
two-tier system with four years of term
Exam angle (UPPSC 2023, key "only (1)"): "three-tier replaced by two-tier" is correct. The second statement, about the block, is the trap: Ashok Mehta made the
district
, not the block, the unit.
The Zila Parishad was the district-level executive body; the Mandal Panchayat covered a group of villages; the report came in August 1978; and the committee was appointed in December 1977.

secs.t: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) → appointment, two tiers, recommendations — Other recommendations

x: Compulsory taxation powers were recommended so that Panchayati Raj Institutions could raise their own money and become financially capable.
The Committee proposed regular social audit by a district-level agency together with a committee of legislators.
The Committee recommended that elections should be conducted within
six months
if a Panchayati Raj body was superseded.

secs.t: Ashok Mehta Committee → fate and legacy; BRM vs Ashok Mehta

x: West Bengal
adopted the Ashok Mehta recommendations and strengthened its PRIs (Karnataka also followed).
The
Sixth Five Year Plan
, associated with the Janata Government’s 1978-1983 plan, gave Panchayati Raj a new lease of life but was dropped after 1980 and did not become an official Plan of India.
The Janata government fell before completing its term
, and consequently the Centre took no action on the recommendations.

secs.t: District planning committees → recommendations (Dantwala, Hanumantha Rao, G.V.K. Rao)

x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was set up in 1985 by the
Planning Commission
to review administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation.
The District Development Commissioner was proposed as the Zila Parishad's Chief Executive Officer and was to be in charge of all district development departments.
G.V.K. Rao examined the administrative set-up for rural development, whereas L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising Panchayati Raj Institutions as instruments of democracy.

secs.t: L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil Committees → constitutional status — L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986)

x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee was appointed in 1986 by the Rajiv Gandhi Government to prepare a concept paper on reviving Panchayati Raj Institutions.
The L.M. Singhvi Committee was associated with the title ‘
Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development
The Singhvi Committee supported the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy; it did not recommend its abolition.

secs.t: L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil Committees → constitutional status — P.K. Thungon (1988)

x: The Thungon Committee of 1988 dealt with constitutional recognition, a three-tier structure and a five-year term for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
The Thungon sub-committee proposed that supersession of a Panchayati Raj body should not exceed
six months
Thungon recommended placing a list of Panchayati Raj subjects in the Constitution; this was later reflected in the Eleventh Schedule.

secs.t: Bills and Amendments → year, government, fate (1989 to 1992)

x: Opponents feared that the 64th Bill would
centralise power and bypass the States
in matters relating to Panchayati Raj.
The
P.V. Narasimha Rao
Government during 1991–92 dropped the controversial portions and enacted the revised proposal as the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in July 1989 by the Rajiv Gandhi Government, sought constitutional status for Panchayats, and was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989 because it did not secure the special majority.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh Panchayati Raj Acts → year and provision

x: In 1985, N.T. Rama Rao abolished the hereditary village officer Patel-Patwari system and introduced the Mandal system.
The AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 brought in the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in Andhra Pradesh.
The 1986 reform under the NTR Government replaced block-level Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads, reflecting the mandal idea associated with the Ashok Mehta approach.

secs.t: PR committees → year, appointed by, subject (chronological order)

x: The committee was appointed by the Government of India during the Nehru era to review the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service.
Balwant Rai Mehta (1957), Ashok Mehta (1977-78), L.M. Singhvi (1986), Gadgil (1988):
d, b, a, c
, the APPSC 2025 keyed order.

secs.t: Committee → distinctive recommendation; correct pairs and odd one out — Recommendation → committee

x: The
G. Ramachandran Committee
of 1969 dealt with training centres.
Two tiers, a four-year term and party participation in panchayat elections are all Ashok Mehta recommendations.

secs.t: Committee → distinctive recommendation; correct pairs and odd one out — Committee → identifying recommendation

x: Balwant Rai Mehta proposed the District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad, but the Balwant Rai Mehta, First ARC, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao bodies are identified as cutting the Collector’s development role.

Balwant Rai Mehta recommended genuine transfer and resources; Ashok Mehta emphasised the district as the first point; G.V.K. Rao sought restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role; and L.M. Singhvi recommended constitutional status.

secs.t: Committee → distinctive recommendation; correct pairs and odd one out — Correct pairs and odd one out

x: Vishwa Raman dealt with PR Administration; Nyaya Panchayats was G.R. Rajagopalan (1962).
Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao were associated with Panchayati Raj inquiries.
The Administrative Reforms Commissions were associated with administrative reforms.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Panchayati Raj evolved from rural development schemes, particularly the Community Development Programme, towards constitutionalised local self-government under Part IX.
The distinctive intermediate-level institution in Andhra Pradesh is the
Mandal Praja Parishad
The Community Development Programme was
India's first major post-Independence rural development programme
and laid the groundwork for a third tier of government.
Andhra Pradesh implemented the three-tier Balwant Rai Mehta model on 1 November 1959 under Chief Minister N. Sanjiva Reddy's government.

The Ashok Mehta Committee was significant for being the first to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections for Panchayati Raj Institutions. ⚠ Sources differ: most prep texts: Ashok Mehta (1978) first sought constitutional status; APPSC 2018 key: L.M. Singhvi (1986).
The
L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil
Committees collectively contributed to the blueprint of the 73rd Amendment, including constitutional status, election and financial institutions, tenure and reservation.
The Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill was the first attempt to confer constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions.
The 1992 constitutional changes transformed Panchayati Raj from a largely policy-based arrangement into a constitutionally protected and justiciable system, creating obligations for the States.

rows.title: 73rd Amendment - Part IX, Eleventh Schedule, three-tier structure, Gram Sabha, reservations, State Election Commission
sub: Group-II M1-B-91: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act - Part IX, structure, Gram Sabha and the Eleventh Schedule
Group-II M1-B-92: 73rd Amendment - reservations, State Election Commission and State Finance Commission
Group-II M1-B-95: Implementation of the 73rd and 74th Amendments - achievements across states

secs.t: 73rd Amendment — Part, Schedule, dates and significance

x: Exam angle: A-R item "73rd is a landmark... because it brought PRIs under the justiciable part" - both true, R explains A.
The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX, comprising Articles 243 to 243O, and the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects.
Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government; the 73rd Amendment put it into effect through Part IX.

secs.t: FIRSTs and pioneer States in Panchayati Raj

x: Rajasthan was the first State to launch PRIs on 2 October 1959, while Andhra Pradesh was the second on 1 November 1959.
Madhya Pradesh
was the first State to implement the 73rd Amendment (MPPSC 2015 key).
Pradhans held unusual financial powers; therefore; .

secs.t: Compulsory vs voluntary provisions of Part IX

x: Exam angle: "is/are correct" sets mixing both columns (APPSC-G2 2025 answered "All of the above" for the mandatory list).
Reservation for backward classes
is left to the discretion of the States.
All four are compulsory under the text of Part IX: Gram Sabha (243A), three tiers (243B), SFC every five years (243I) and SEC (243K).

secs.t: Articles 243 to 243O → content

x: Exam angle: "Article → subject" matching; 243G is the Article the Eleventh Schedule hangs on.
Article 243A concerns the Gram Sabha, Article 243B the constitution of Panchayats, Article 243C their composition and chairpersons, and Article 243D reservations.
Article 243M concerns exempted areas, Article 243N permits existing laws to continue for up to one year, Article 243O bars court interference in electoral matters, and Article 243J concerns audit.

secs.t: Three tiers → intermediate-tier names by State

x: Article 243B provides for Panchayats at the
village, intermediate and district levels
Article 243B permits a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh to omit the intermediate level of Panchayats.
Anchalik Panchayat is the name used for the intermediate tier in Assam.
Mandal Praja Parishad is associated with Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Elections, age, tenure and dissolution — Articles 243C, 243E, 243F

x: The method of choosing a village chairperson is left to State law; the Constitution does not prescribe one uniform method.
Article 243F refers to disqualification under the law for elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
A Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.

secs.t: Gram Sabha — definition, powers, planning and PESA

x: Article 243A
deals with the powers and functions of the Gram Sabha, while Article 243(b) defines its composition.
PESA gives Gram Sabhas powers over minor forest produce, village markets and liquor, and protection of traditions and community resources; it does not give them control over the Union Budget.
PESA requires consultation with the Gram Sabha before
land acquisition
in Scheduled Areas.

secs.t: Areas exempted — Article 243M → States and regions

x: Article 243M excludes the hill council area of Darjeeling district from the application of Part IX.
The absence of SC reservation in Arunachal Pradesh does not mean that Part IX is wholly inapplicable there.
Article 243M(4)(b)
lets Parliament extend Part IX to Scheduled Areas with exceptions and modifications, which it did through PESA, 1996.

secs.t: Acts, committees, cases and bodies → year

x: PESA is stated to extend Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas in
ten States
, including Andhra Pradesh.
The
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees.

K. Krishna Murthy (2010) upheld backward-class reservation in local bodies under Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), holding that political backwardness is distinct from social and educational backwardness.
Part VI of
the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats.

secs.t: Women's reservation — Article 243D(4), 50% States and data

x: Bihar
was the first State mentioned as having raised reservation for women in local bodies to 50 per cent, in 2006.
The
Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats
are intended to promote substantive women’s leadership and counter token representation.
Of 24.41 lakh elected panchayat representatives, 12.14 lakh (49.75%) are women, well above the constitutional floor of one-third (33%).

secs.t: Eleventh Schedule — 29 subjects and how to identify them — Number and nature

x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects related to Panchayats.
The Eleventh Schedule provides a menu of subjects; it does not itself automatically transfer every subject to Panchayats.
Land improvement, minor irrigation and fisheries are Eleventh Schedule subjects.
Rural housing, drinking water and rural electrification are Eleventh Schedule subjects.

secs.t: Eleventh Schedule — 29 subjects and how to identify them — The 29 items

x: Exam angle: "18 functional items were placed with Panchayats" is FALSE (18 = Twelfth Schedule).
Fuel and fodder, rural roads and related infrastructure, and non-conventional energy are included in the Eleventh Schedule.
Poverty alleviation programme
is an Eleventh Schedule subject.
All four statements correctly identify education-related subjects included in the Eleventh Schedule.
Public distribution system and maintenance of community assets are Eleventh Schedule subjects.

secs.t: State Finance Commission and Union Finance Commission — Articles 243I, 243Y, 280 — State Finance Commission - Articles 243I and 243Y, constitution, functions

x: The Governor lays the State Finance Commission report before the State Legislature together with a memorandum explaining the action taken on its recommendations.
The first State Finance Commission was required to be constituted within
one year of 24 April 1993
, the date on which the 73rd Amendment came into force.
The State Finance Commission makes recommendations on fiscal distribution, assigned taxes, grants-in-aid and improvement of local finances.

secs.t: State Finance Commission and Union Finance Commission — Articles 243I, 243Y, 280 — Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) - Union Finance Commission and local bodies

x: Article 280(3)(bb) concerns panchayats and was inserted through the 73rd Amendment.
The Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for supplementing local-body resources, drawing on State Finance Commission recommendations.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — laws, PRI numbers and funds

x: The cited reorganisation proposes increasing the number of Zilla Parishads from 13 to 28.

secs.t: Devolution and model States — Panchayat Advancement Index, Kerala

x: The
Panchayat Advancement Index
is the newer composite, multi-domain index used to assess Panchayat performance against localised Sustainable Development Goals.
Kerala's People's Plan Campaign was launched in 1996.
The campaign devolved a large share of plan funds and encouraged planning from Gram Sabhas upwards.

secs.t: Schemes, e-tools and urban missions → year and fact

x: SabhaSaar is described as the first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes; it was piloted in Tripura on the Bhashini platform.
SVAMITVA was launched on
24 April 2020
, National Panchayati Raj Day, with the Survey of India and NICSI preparing Records of Rights through drone mapping.
Only a few large cities have issued municipal bonds because weak municipal balance sheets often prevent them from securing investment-grade ratings.

secs.t: National Panchayat Awards — categories and AP winners

x: The awards are judged on nine localised Sustainable Development Goal themes.
The
Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar
is the holistic category.
The awards include theme-wise and special categories and use the Panchayat Advancement Index for assessment.
Bokkasampalem in Srikalahasti, Tirupati, secured first position in the women-friendly panchayat category.
The Chittoor District Panchayat Raj Centre
, or Chittoor DPRC, was ranked first nationally.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, comprising Articles 243P to 243ZG, and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
Under the Vikas Kishanrao Gawali triple test (2021), total SC+ST+OBC reservation must not exceed 50 per cent, so the 34 per cent BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within that 50 per cent ceiling.
The Andhra Pradesh structure comprises Gram Panchayats, Mandal Parishads or Mandal Praja Parishads, and Zilla Parishads.

sub: Group-II M1-B-93: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act - Part IXA, types of urban bodies and the Twelfth Schedule
Group-II M1-B-94: 74th Amendment - ward committees, District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee

secs.t: Municipal government before the 74th — FIRSTs and milestones

x: The 1989 Municipalities Bill lapsed, while the Bill introduced by P. V. Narasimha Rao in September 1991 resulted in the 74th Amendment and Part IXA.
The first Municipal Corporation was set up at
Madras in 1688
(charter dated 30 December 1687; it began on 29 September 1688).
Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882
is called the Magna Carta of local self-government.

secs.t: 74th Amendment Act, 1992 — dates, Part IXA, compulsory vs voluntary — Enactment and commencement

x: The 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993; 24 April 1993 was the commencement date of the 73rd Amendment.
The 74th Amendment gave urban local bodies constitutional status and required States to establish a uniform municipal framework through conforming laws.
Local Government remains in the State List, and Article 243ZF required municipal laws to be brought into conformity within one year.

secs.t: 74th Amendment Act, 1992 — dates, Part IXA, compulsory vs voluntary — Compulsory vs voluntary

x: Exam angle: "came into force on" (1 June 1993) and "which is NOT a mandatory provision" type statements.
Exam angle: the four-option date trap - 24 Apr 1993 (73rd) vs
Article 243Q deals with types of municipalities, Article 243R with their composition, Article 243S with Ward Committees and Article 243T with reservation of seats.

secs.t: Articles 243P to 243ZG → content

x: Article 243P
contains the definitions for the purposes of Part IXA, while Article 243Q deals with the constitution of municipalities.
Article 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas.
Article 243ZF deals with the continuance of existing laws for a specified period, while Article 243ZG bars court interference in electoral matters relating to municipalities.

secs.t: Types of urban local bodies — Article 243Q, terms and ministries

x: Where municipal services are being provided by an industrial establishment, the Governor may specify the area as an industrial township and a municipality need not be constituted there.
The Governor may specify the type of urban area by public notification after considering population, density, revenue, non-agricultural employment and economic importance.

secs.t: Composition, age, term and elections of municipalities — Articles 243R to 243ZA

x: A municipal election must be held before expiry of the five-year term or, in the case of dissolution,
within six months of dissolution
, subject to the constitutional qualification relating to the remaining period.
Article 243ZA places the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections under the
State Election Commission
, the same constitutional authority associated with Article 243K.

secs.t: Wards committees and Area Sabhas — Article 243S and the Model Nagara Raj Bill

x: Article 243S makes Wards Committees mandatory in municipalities having a population of
three lakh or more
Wards Committees may cover one or more wards, while State law determines their composition and territorial area; the ward councillor sits on the relevant committee.
The Community Participation Law was a mandatory reform under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (
JNNURM

secs.t: Twelfth Schedule — 18 municipal functions

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 asked which one is a municipal Twelfth Schedule function - answer
cattle pounds
The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 municipal functional items.
Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.

secs.t: DPC and MPC — Articles 243ZD and 243ZE

x: An MPC is mandatory for a metropolitan area with a population of ten lakh or more, is provided under Article 243ZE, and such an area may span more than one district.

In Rajasthan the DPC is chaired by the
Zila Pramukh
, the head of the Zila Parishad (RPSC 2024 key).
The Pradhan heads the Panchayat Samiti at the block level in the Balwant Rai Mehta pattern (though in some States such as UP the term is used for the Gram Panchayat head).

As per the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, AP's 123 urban local bodies are
17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats

is the AP State Election Commissioner who notified ward-wise photo rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations and 29 municipalities/nagar panchayats).

Rajya Sabha members and Members of the Legislative Council
registered as voters in the concerned urban local body could vote in such mayoral polls.
The Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
All three statements reflect the criticism: ULBs spend less than 1 per cent of GDP, employ about 10 per cent of the public workforce, and are described as the 'stepchild' of federalism.

sub: Group-II M1-B-100: PESA Act 1996 and self-governance in the scheduled areas of Andhra Pradesh
Group-II S3-33: Constitutional provisions for Scheduled Tribes - Articles 244, 275, 338A; Fifth and Sixth Schedules

secs.t: Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas — definitions, criteria and data

x: Under Article 342 the President, after consultation with the Governor, notifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State or UT (the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950).
Both statements are true, and the concentration of Scheduled Tribes in contiguous areas explains why the Constitution provides area-based protection through the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.

secs.t: Articles → provisions (342, 338A, 244, 275, 243M)

x: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes requisitioned reports on Forest Rights Act implementation from the
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Parliament may amend the Fifth and Sixth Schedules
by an ordinary law
; such amendment is not required to follow the procedure under Article 368.
Article 243M
excludes Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas from the operation of Part IX relating to Panchayats.

secs.t: Fifth Schedule — Governor's powers, regulations and TAC

x: Regulations (Para 5):
regulations for peace and good government.
Exam angle: "Governor is NOT authorised to direct that an Act does not apply" is the false statement. Regulations are issued by the
Governor
. TAC size is
up to 20
Exam angle: TAC size "up to 20" (G2 2017 - answer key was left blank; the Constitution says not more than 20).

secs.t: Sixth Schedule — autonomous districts, regions and councils

x: The Governor may organise or reorganise autonomous districts and alter their areas, boundaries and names.

Legislative powers cover land, forests and social customs; judicial powers include village councils or courts; executive and financial powers include revenue and taxes; Article 275 provides grants-in-aid.
The application of Parliamentary and State legislation is subject to the prescribed authority: the Governor in Assam and the President in Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

secs.t: States → coverage under the Fifth Schedule, Sixth Schedule and PESA

x: Exam angle: G2 2025 statement set - the Sixth Schedule is NOT applied "wherever STs exceed 40%"; the key was "None" correct. GS 2019: Nagaland is not in the Sixth Schedule.
Tamil Nadu
is not among the ten Fifth Schedule States covered by PESA and is a State without Scheduled Areas.

secs.t: PESA Act 1996 — year, committee and objectives

x: Creation of autonomous regions is associated with the Sixth Schedule, not an objective of PESA.
PESA (24 December 1996) followed the
Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee
report (1995) and extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule Areas.

secs.t: PESA provisions — Gram Sabha powers, reservation and higher tiers — Gram Sabha

x: PESA recognises the habitation-level Gram Sabha, including units such as a para, majra or tola.
The presiding officer is
an ST member elected by the Gram Sabha
; the Sarpanch does not automatically preside in every case.
PESA requires consultation before land acquisition and resettlement, while a Gram Sabha recommendation is mandatory before prospecting licences or mining leases for minor minerals.

secs.t: PESA provisions — Gram Sabha powers, reservation and higher tiers — Reservation and higher tiers

x: The Zila Panchayat in Scheduled Areas may plan minor water bodies, control social-sector institutions and control Tribal Sub-Plans, along with other functions conferred by the State.
Under PESA, any provision of a State Panchayat law inconsistent with it ceases to operate one year from the date PESA received assent (24 December 1996), unless amended earlier.

secs.t: Acts and cases on tribal land, forests and mining — Acts and regulations

x: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises individual and community rights over forest land and ownership of minor forest produce.
Forest land may be diverted for public utilities only on the recommendation of the
Gram Sabha
OTFDs must prove three generations, taken as 75 years, of residence before 2005.
The AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation is
Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970

secs.t: Acts and cases on tribal land, forests and mining — Cases

x: In the 2013 Niyamgiri or Orissa Mining Corporation case, Gram Sabhas were to decide whether bauxite mining affected
religious and forest rights
Samatha (SC, 1997, an AP case) held that Scheduled Area land
cannot be leased to non-tribals or private companies, including for mining
, because such leasing violates the Fifth Schedule and the Land Transfer Regulation; the State itself was treated as a 'person'.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — Scheduled Areas, ITDAs, FRA and PESA Rules — Location and extent

x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district was carved from the erstwhile
Visakhapatnam
district.
Alluri Sitharama Raju district is tribal-majority and has
Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
(PVTGs).

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — Scheduled Areas, ITDAs, FRA and PESA Rules — ITDAs → district

x: The map was redrawn in 2025 with 28 districts, including new Polavaram and Markapuram, and the reorganisation created a need to realign land-transfer adjudicating authorities.
2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas are being strengthened, 19 model Gram Panchayats cover 43 Gram Sabhas, and the PESA Mahotsav was held in Visakhapatnam for the Act's 30th anniversary.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — Scheduled Areas, ITDAs, FRA and PESA Rules — AP FRA status (2024-25)

x: Scheduled Tribe farmers holding Recognition of Forest Rights (RoFR) are covered under
NTR Rythu Bharosa
The Tribal Medical College at Paderu opened in
with 50 seats.

secs.t: Fifth vs Sixth Schedule — comparison

x: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Union's executive power extends to giving directions to the State regarding Scheduled Areas.
The Governor may exclude or modify the application of laws in Fifth Schedule areas.
The Fifth Schedule is associated with the application of PESA, while PESA does not apply to areas governed by the Sixth Schedule.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The functioning of the Fifth Schedule has been criticised because Tribal Advisory Councils rarely meet and Governors rarely exercise their Fifth Schedule powers.
AP's Scheduled Areas correspond to the old Agency tracts, AP is among the ten Fifth Schedule States, and Araku is an ST Lok Sabha seat.
A post-Maoism policy discussion has emphasised the need to implement PESA in earnest rather than abandon its Gram Sabha-centred framework.
