rows.title: Panchayati Raj and urban bodies in Andhra Pradesh - structure, elections, finances, performance
sub: Group-II M1-B-97: Panchayati Raj in Andhra Pradesh - structure, elections, powers and finances
Group-II M1-B-98: Urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh - municipalities, corporations and their functioning

secs.t: Panchayati Raj — FIRSTs and committees

x: Balwant Rai Mehta is linked with the Panchayat Samiti–Zilla Parishad relationship; Ashok Mehta with the two-tier and party-participation model; G. V. K. Rao with the ‘grass without roots’ observation; and L. M. Singhvi with constitutional recognition and Gram Sabha.

All five features are associated with the Thungon Committee recommendations, including constitutional status, three tiers, the planning role of the Zilla Parishad, State Finance Commissions and a six-month maximum supersession period.

secs.t: AP Panchayat Raj laws → year and persons

x: The Ashok Mehta Committee proposed a two-tier system with a Mandal Panchayat covering
In 1986, during the N.T. Rama Rao Government, Panchayat Samithis were replaced by Mandal Praja Parishads and Zilla Parishads were renamed Zilla Praja Parishads.
Part II deals with Gram Panchayats, Part III with Mandal Parishads, Part IV with Zilla Parishads and Part VI with the Finance Commission.

secs.t: Three tiers — members, heads, elections and counts

x: MPTC members are directly elected, while the Mandal Parishad President is elected indirectly from among the MPTCs.
The Zilla Parishad Chairperson is elected indirectly from among the ZPTC members, not directly by all district voters.
Ward members and the Sarpanch are directly elected; the Gram Panchayat has a five-year term and the minimum contesting age is 21 years.

secs.t: Gram Panchayat functionaries → functions

x: Exam angle: "Who convenes / who implements / who is Marriage Officer" - the answer is the Secretary, not the Sarpanch.
Exam angle: APPSC 2018 asked which is an "essential function" - burial grounds.
Sanitation, drinking water, drains, street lighting, village roads and burial grounds are obligatory functions.
The
Panchayat Secretary
, the executive functionary of the GP, implements its resolutions (APPSC-GS 2019).

secs.t: State Election Commission — Articles, appointment, removal, AP SEC — Articles and functions

x: The State Election Commission conducts local-body elections, including Panchayat and municipal elections, but not elections to State Legislatures.
The Commission controls Panchayat electoral rolls and may direct their rearrangement and republication.

secs.t: State Election Commission — Articles, appointment, removal, AP SEC — Appointment and removal

x: Exam angle: statement pairs on "appointed by Governor for 5 years" + "status of HC judge" - both correct.
Both are correct: the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor for five years from assuming office and has the status of a High Court Judge, and can be removed only like one.

secs.t: State Election Commission — Articles, appointment, removal, AP SEC — AP SEC

x: The order concerned photo electoral rolls for
MPTC and ZPTC elections
, which are local-body elections.
After bifurcation, the Governor constituted the State Election Commission for the residuary State of AP on
30 January 2016
(APPSC-GS 2022 key).

secs.t: Local body elections in AP — reservation and polls

x: SC/ST reservation is provided in proportion to population, with seats allotted by rotation.
The last Gram Panchayat elections in Andhra Pradesh were conducted in four phases during February 2021.
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved
34 percent
reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies on 18 August 2026.

secs.t: Finances — State Finance Commission, FC grants, own revenue

x: The 14th and 15th Finance Commission grants prioritised
drinking water and sanitation
The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program is a challenge for revenue-generating projects under the
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan
of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
The programme requires the stated revenue thresholds, at least three years of remaining tenure and written Gram Sabha consent.

secs.t: AP municipal laws and Amendment Bills → year

x: The 33.33 per cent BC quota is implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965.
A companion Bill removed the two-child bar on contesting panchayat elections in November 2024.
The Third Amendment Bill, 2026 adds a Uniform Mutation Fee on title transfers recorded in municipal records.

secs.t: Urban bodies — grades, Mayor election and development authorities

x: A
Nagar Panchayat
is constituted for an area transitioning from rural to urban character under Article 243Q.
Urban Development Authorities are not subordinate to ULBs; their separate and autonomous functioning can fragment urban governance.
APCRDA relates to the Amaravati capital region and was established under the APCRDA Act, 2014; VMRDA relates to Visakhapatnam.
The three-level uniform mechanism extends across
Nagar Panchayats, municipalities, corporations and Urban Development Authorities

secs.t: Service delivery — Secretariats and e-governance projects

x: Ward Secretariats and the Volunteer system operate under the
Municipal Administration Department
as service-delivery mechanisms.
The 2024–25 outcome target was to improve the quality and accountability of urban services through Ward Secretariat and Volunteer Systems across all ULBs.
e-Panchayat is a Ministry of Panchayati Raj Mission Mode Project for digitising Panchayat planning, budgeting and service delivery through the e-Gram Swaraj portal.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Incomplete devolution of the three Fs—
Funds, Functions and Functionaries
—limits Panchayati Raj Institutions and leaves them mainly as implementing agencies.
Andhra Pradesh has reorganised its former 13 Zilla Praja Parishads into 28, while the MPP and ZPP terms end on 23 and 24 September 2026 respectively.
National Panchayati Raj Day is
24 April
, when the 73rd Amendment came into force; five AP panchayats won National Panchayat Awards in 2026.

rows.title: Public policy - meaning, types, policy cycle (formulation, implementation, evaluation), policy instruments
sub: Group-II S3-30: Public policy and the welfare state in India - evolution and approach

secs.t: Public policy — meaning, Indian bases and Lowi types

x: Public policy is a systematic state course of action addressing public issues, pursuing development goals and regulating behaviour; it bridges political intent and administrative action.
Distributive policies spread benefits to specific groups while their costs are generally borne by the wider public; farm input subsidies and PM-KISAN illustrate this type.

secs.t: Thinkers → definitions, models and concepts

x: Easton defined policy as the authoritative allocation of values for the whole society (a-2); Lasswell, founder of the policy sciences, as a projected programme of goals, values and practices (b-1); Anderson as a purposive course of action by an actor or set of actors dealing with a problem (c-3).
Herbert Simon’s bounded rationality and satisficing critique the
rational-comprehensive model
, which assumes complete information and full optimisation.

secs.t: Policy cycle — stages from agenda setting to termination

x: The principal sequence is agenda-setting, formulation, adoption, implementation and evaluation.
These activities are characteristic of policy
formulation
, when alternative courses of action are developed and assessed.
Termination or revision deals with ineffective policies and allows policy learning to feed back into agenda setting.
Implementation is not formal adoption; it involves planning, resource allocation, coordination and execution of the policy.

secs.t: Policy instruments → Indian illustration

x: Regulation works through licensing, standards and mandates (a-3).
Hood’s NATO framework consists of
Nodality, Authority, Treasure and Organisation

secs.t: Implementation — approaches, causes of failure and remedies

x: The top-down approach emphasises central direction and faithful execution, while the bottom-up approach recognises that front-line officials shape actual outcomes.
Michael Lipsky
developed the concept of street-level bureaucracy in 1980, referring to front-line officials who shape policy outcomes.
Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is cited as an example of multi-phase execution combined with performance evaluation.

secs.t: Acts, bodies and delivery reforms → year and provision — Evaluation bodies and budgets

x: DMEO is the apex M&E office under NITI Aayog; it evaluates Central schemes on its own initiative or at a ministry’s request, advises States and supports evidence-based policy.
The Draft National Health Research Policy 2026 uses the
ICMR Impact of Research and Innovation Scale
to assess research contributions to public policy and practice.

secs.t: Acts, bodies and delivery reforms → year and provision — Social legislation and rights-based entitlements

x: Social legislation protects vulnerable groups and establishes minimum floors for a dignified life.
Protective legislation prevents exploitation, regulatory legislation governs conduct and relations, and enabling legislation creates entitlements.
The RTE Act, 2009 provides free schooling for children aged
6–14 years
under Article 21A.
Civil society
played an important role in helping to win these rights-based entitlements.

secs.t: Acts, bodies and delivery reforms → year and provision — Delivery reforms

x: DBT began on 1 January 2013.
Section 17 of MGNREGA provides for social audit by the
Gram Sabha
Andhra Pradesh pioneered statewide NREGS social audits in 2006, and the independent Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency was established in 2009.

secs.t: Social policy → terms, welfare vs development and exam keys

x: General health services for all
are not classified as targeted social welfare services, whereas the other three serve vulnerable groups.

Social policy is the overall framework for social well-being; social justice removes inequalities; social welfare serves vulnerable sections; and social defence involves rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations.
The Mid-Day Meal, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and the Rural Health Mission are social development programmes.

secs.t: Welfare approach — Plan phases and welfare ministries → year

x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Ministry of Women and Child Development became separate ministries
during 2006–07.

State-led planned development characterised the 1950s–70s, welfare shifted towards development in the Sixth Plan, empowerment marked the Eighth–Ninth Plans, and rights-based laws emerged in the 2000s.
New welfarism is described as targeted and technology-driven, relying on DBT benefits rather than primarily on legal rights.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The index is intended to reinforce
evidence-based policymaking
by providing an analytical basis for decisions on electric mobility.
The Group of Ministers is framing the policy under Excise Minister Kollu Ravindra, and the 2024–26 policy expires on 30 September 2026.
The shift toward outcome-based governance is linked with Action Taken Reports (ATRs) and evaluations by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO).

rows.title: Actors in policy-making - executive, legislature, judiciary, bureaucracy, media, civil society, think tanks

secs.t: Executive — Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

x: The noted criticisms include delays, bureaucratic influence, overlapping mandates, political considerations and secrecy, even though the Cabinet and Cabinet Committees take key decisions.
The Cabinet Secretariat is headed by the Cabinet Secretary, works directly under the Prime Minister and administers the Transaction of Business Rules.
A is correct:
Ashok Kumar Lahiri
was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2026.

secs.t: Legislature — law-making, controls and options against the Court

x: Parliament is the chief law-making body, but the Cabinet determines the substance and timing of bills, while the bureaucracy generally drafts them.
Without a Rajya Sabha majority, a government may have to concede or negotiate, as illustrated by the rejection of the Prevention of Terrorism Bill, 2002, in the Rajya Sabha.
C is correct: referral of Bills to committees fell from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to
in the 17th Lok Sabha, showing falling committee scrutiny.

secs.t: Judiciary — PIL origin, activism and its critics

x: The 1979 case was filed on behalf of prisoners, not by them.
Upendra Baxi's typology includes ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears.
Ignoring police-reform orders illustrates the
legitimation risk
identified in the criticism of judicial activism.
Excessive judicial overreach is associated with
policy paralysis and backlog

secs.t: Cases, Acts and campaigns → law or guideline

x: Vishaka dealt with workplace sexual harassment, Prakash Singh with police reforms, and T.S.R. Subramanian with civil-services safeguards.
Prakash Singh concerned police reforms including the State Security Commission, DGP tenure, Police Establishment Board and Complaints Authority.
The MKSS movement led to the RTI Act, 2005; Right to Work/NAC advocacy was associated with MGNREGA, 2005; and the Right to Food campaign contributed to the National Food Security Act, 2013.

secs.t: Bureaucracy and political parties

x: The permanent executive includes personnel from All-India Services, State services, local bodies and public sector undertakings, assisting ministers in policy formulation and implementation.
The 33.33% BC quota in Andhra Pradesh urban local bodies was an NDA 2024 poll promise and was subsequently implemented through G.O. Rt.
Andhra Pradesh began publishing Action Taken Reports from 22 June 2026 against seven sectoral white papers, enabling public tracking of manifesto delivery.

secs.t: Media — agenda setting, image-building, free press and new media

x: Public awareness and media coverage
are identified as important drivers through which issues are pushed onto the policy agenda.
Media organisations are counted among
civil society
stakeholders involved in governance.
Media treatment helps explain the image formed about political personalities.
AI-driven foreign information manipulation can exploit social fault lines by using synthetic media and algorithmic polarisation.

secs.t: Civil society, stakeholders and think tanks → type

x: The State, Market and Civil Society are the three broad sets of governance stakeholders, and pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society.
NITI Aayog, along with DMEO, is classified as a Government think tank or expert body.
Policy labs, hackathons and idea competitions
are identified as newer channels for policy innovation and expert participation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Accountability concerns include delays by Governors and Speakers in deciding assent and Tenth Schedule matters, along with an RTI backlog and fewer committee referrals.
PIL is criticised when it is misused for publicity or political purposes rather than for a genuine public cause or protection of rights.
Sri Lanka's proposed 22nd Amendment would raise the retirement age of Supreme Court judges from 65 to 67, prompting debate concerning judicial independence.

rows.title: Governance and good governance - meaning, dimensions, World Bank/UNDP indicators

secs.t: Governance — definitions by body and FIRSTs

x: The World Bank defines governance as
the manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development
UNDP describes governance as the exercise of
economic, political and administrative authority
to manage a country's affairs at all levels.
B is correct: the
World Bank
first brought 'good governance' into development discourse through its 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa (APPSC-GS 2018 key).

secs.t: Good governance — UN/UNDP attributes, four pillars and tools

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a feature" - look for centralisation, secrecy, discretion or majoritarian rule as the odd one out.
Ethos means service, ethics means honesty and integrity, equity means empathy for weaker sections, and efficiency means speedy delivery using ICT.
People's participation
is identified as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance; other tools include RTI, Sevottam, Citizen Charters and e-governance.

secs.t: Second ARC reports → title and content

x: The Second ARC was set up in 2005.
All four subjects were covered in the 12th Report, “Citizen Centric Administration - The Heart of Governance,” published in 2009.

secs.t: World Bank WGI and DARPG Good Governance Index — dimensions

x: The WGI cover more than 200 countries since 1996 and include Government Effectiveness and Rule of Law among their six dimensions.
The
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
, or DARPG, is India's nodal department for the WGI.
India was described as having moderate government effectiveness and rule of law, while political stability was low compared with global averages.

secs.t: Other governance indices → publisher

x: The Public Affairs Index is published by the Public Affairs Centre, BRAP rankings by DPIIT, the SDG India Index by NITI Aayog, and the Good Governance Index by DARPG.
Gujarat
ranked first in the Investment Friendliness Index 2026 with a score of 56.6, followed by Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
The Responsible Nations Index is associated with
WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai

secs.t: DARPG tools and governance institutes — NCGG, CGG AP

x: The CGG is a governance-reform think tank that advises the government on administrative reforms, e-governance, research and training.
The Centre for Good Governance was established in collaboration with
DFID of the United Kingdom and the World Bank
B is correct: the CGG was set up in 2001 by the undivided AP government, with DFID (UK) and the World Bank (APPSC-GS 2021 and 2023 keys).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India showcased
CPGRAMS and the Samadhan Didi AI grievance chatbot
to Malaysia in August 2026.
Mana Mitra offers 500-plus services, received Rs 100 crore for RTGS in the 2026–27 Budget, and aims to reach 1,000 services.
WGI and V-Dem are contested because perception-based indices rely substantially on expert opinion, which can affect their objectivity and comparability.

x: Broadcasting or wider-dissemination
places government information in the public domain.
Critical flow
channels critical information to a targeted audience, such as corruption data sent to an ombudsman.
Comparative analysis = learning from best practices (a-ii); e-advocacy = online civil-society networks influencing decisions (b-iii); interactive service = two-way G2C services (c-i).

secs.t: Interaction types → examples (G2C, G2B, G2G, G2E)

x: G2C
means Government to Citizen interaction.
G2B means Government to Business interaction; MCA portal, GSTN and e-Procurement are examples.
G2G concerns inter-government interaction, while G2E concerns government services for its employees.

secs.t: National platforms → expansion and year

x: UMANG stands for
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
ERSS is the Emergency Response Support System, associated with the single emergency number 112.
UMANG is a single application providing multiple government services through web, SMS and IVR channels.
MyGov
is a citizen-engagement platform intended to promote participative governance.
Aadhaar was launched in 2009; the Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016 and amended in 2019.

secs.t: Awards and conferences → host, year, outcome

x: NAeG was instituted by DARPG (Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions).
The Visakhapatnam Declaration included extending the NeSDA framework to low-connectivity areas such as Ladakh and the North-East.
The 29th NCeG in Jaipur adopted the Jaipur Declaration on DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance.
The 2025 awards, conducted with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, introduced a first-ever dedicated category for
Gram Panchayats

secs.t: AP e-governance initiatives → year and purpose

x: The Real Time Governance Society, or
RTGS
, is associated with these technologies and the Command & Control Centre.
e-Pragati aims at
faceless, paperless and cashless governance
, with additional citizen services integrated into the platform.
B is correct: APSWAN (AP State Wide Area Network), from the NeGP era, is
the data backbone linking state, district and mandal offices

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A Singapore delegation reviewed
RTGS
in Andhra Pradesh.
E-governance is associated with citizen engagement, better service delivery, fewer face-to-face contacts and audit trails.
Andhra Pradesh declared 2026 the '
Technology-Driven Decision Making
Year'.

rows.title: Citizen-centric administration - Citizens' Charter, Sevottam, grievance redress (CPGRAMS), social audit

secs.t: Citizen-centric administration — origins and FIRSTs

x: Meghalaya
passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory in 2017.
L.M. Singhvi coined the term; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC that recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta.
The First Administrative Reforms Commission, associated with Morarji Desai and functioning during 1966–70, recommended Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for the States.

secs.t: Citizens' Charter — principles, elements and adoption in India

x: Exam angle: "main purpose of a Citizen's Charter" - time-bound service delivery and grievance redress.
All four are basic elements: service standards, service information, grievance redress arrangements and details of responsible officers.
Indian Citizens' Charters are generally non-justiciable and are not presently legally enforceable rights.
India adopted it in 1997; 1991 is the UK origin.

secs.t: Second ARC 12th report and Sevottam → terms and modules

x: The Citizens' Charter module publishes service standards; Public Grievance Redress receives, tracks and resolves complaints; Service Delivery Capability builds organisational capacity.
Veerappa Moily
chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission associated with the 12th report on Citizen Centric Administration.
The report recommended Sevottam, statutory Citizens' Charters, strong grievance redress, social audits, e-governance and right-to-public-services legislation.

secs.t: Right to Services Acts — features and order of enactment

x: The order is Punjab, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials.
Andhra Pradesh has laws providing for time-bound delivery of notified services, appeal and penalties for responsible officials in cases of delay.

secs.t: Grievance redress — CPGRAMS, GRAI and AP platforms

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2021 and 2018 both keyed
Spandana
as the AP grievance platform.
All four statements describe features associated with CPGRAMS: multilingual CPGRAMS 7.0, AI/ML-based IGMS with IIT Kanpur, access through 5.1 lakh CSCs and the “One Nation - One Portal” approach.
Spandana was associated with
the YSRCP
Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.

secs.t: Social audit, Lokpal and ombudsman — mechanisms compared

x: The Second ARC recommended institutionalising social audits in all major welfare schemes, extending the practice beyond MGNREGA alone.

CPGRAMS and State portals deal with service-delivery grievances; Lokpal and Lokayukta deal with corruption allegations against public functionaries; and the classic Ombudsman is an independent officer of the legislature.
Lokpal and Lokayukta are statutory institutions under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013; they are not non-statutory voluntary mediation mechanisms.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism of Citizens’ Charters is that they lack legal force, which can limit enforceability of their commitments.
The grievance-platform progression is Prajavani, followed by Meekosam and then Spandana.
The cited figure records more than 71,000 grievances pending on CPGRAMS in September 2025.

rows.title: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
sub: Group-II M1-B-55: Right to Information Act 2005 - features, information commissions, exemptions and amendments
Group-II M1-B-56: Working of the RTI regime - achievements, problems and the transparency debate

secs.t: RTI landmarks, FIRSTs and persons — Sweden 1766 to the 2005 Act

x: The MKSS jan sunwais on muster rolls and bills in Rajasthan started the RTI movement.
Tamil Nadu and Goa enacted laws in 1997, Rajasthan and Karnataka in 2000, Delhi in 2001, and Maharashtra and Assam in 2002.
Sections 13, 15, 16 and 24
were among the provisions that came into force immediately, along with Sections 4(1), 5 and 12.

secs.t: RTI landmarks, FIRSTs and persons — Sweden 1766 to the 2005 Act — Persons and bodies → role

x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 May 2005, the Rajya Sabha on 12 May 2005, assent was given on 15 June 2005, and the Act fully came into force on 12 October 2005.

secs.t: RTI landmarks, FIRSTs and persons — Sweden 1766 to the 2005 Act — Preamble and nature

x: The right to know has been judicially linked with Articles 19(1)(a) and 21.
The Act creates a statutory right.
The Preamble connects informed citizenship and transparency with containing corruption and ensuring accountability, subject to harmonisation with other public interests.

secs.t: RTI Act sections → content; terms → meaning

x: Section 2(h) defines public authority; Section 4 concerns proactive disclosure; Section 18 concerns complaints and inquiry; and Section 19 deals with appeals.
Section 22 gives the RTI Act overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923; it does not repeal that Act.
Section 5 concerns PIOs and APIOs; Section 9 concerns copyright belonging to a person other than the State; Sections 12 and 15 concern the CIC and SIC respectively.

secs.t: RTI Act sections → content; terms → meaning — Terms → meaning

x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
Information concerning a private body is covered when it is
accessible to a public authority under a law
Section 2(j) includes inspection, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information.

secs.t: Time limits — number game

x: Exam angle: "reply in 45 days" is the standard wrong pair (APPSC 2025 key: first appeal 30 days and life/liberty 48 hours correct).
The applicant first approaches the PIO, waits for the decision or expiry of the prescribed period, files the first appeal, and may thereafter file a second appeal before the Information Commission.

secs.t: Exemptions — Section 8(1) clauses, 8(2), 8(3), Sections 9 and 24

x: Section 8(1)(e) covers information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship.
Section 8(2) is the public-interest override, which applies even to OSA-covered information.
The IB, R&AW and CRPF are among the intelligence and security organisations covered by Section 24.
The Central Bureau of Investigation was added to the Second Schedule in 2011, subject to the statutory exceptions relating to corruption and human-rights violations.

secs.t: Public authority — bodies covered and not covered

x: The political parties did not comply with the CIC’s declaration; the Bill seeking exclusion lapsed, rather than successfully removing them.
The DAV College Trust decision in 2019 recognised that NGOs substantially financed by the Government can fall within the meaning of public authority under the RTI Act.
C is correct: the CIC declared INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP public authorities in June 2013; they did not comply and the matter is pending before the Supreme Court.

secs.t: Information Commissions — composition, appointment, term, removal (vs CVC)

x: Disagreement with a State Government decision is not a stated ground for removal.

secs.t: Information Commissions — composition, appointment, term, removal (vs CVC) — Nature and composition

x: For proved misbehaviour or incapacity, removal is by the Governor only after the Supreme Court conducts an inquiry on a reference made by the Governor.
D is correct: the
Chief Justice of the High Court
is not on the SIC selection committee (the trap in the G2 2025 key).
A is correct:
Wajahat Habibullah
was the first CIC when the Commission was set up in 2005.

secs.t: Information Commissions — composition, appointment, term, removal (vs CVC) — Eligibility and term

x: A sitting Member of Parliament cannot be appointed as a State Information Commissioner.
The original term was 5 years or age 65.
The Commission has a Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.

secs.t: Penalties on PIOs and compensation — Sections 20 and 19(8)(b)

x: Section 20 provides for a penalty of ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000, along with possible disciplinary action.
Penalty grounds include refusal to receive an application, delay, mala fide denial, knowingly incorrect or misleading information, destruction of information and obstruction.
Section 19(8)(b) enables the Commission to require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.

secs.t: Amendments → changes — RTI (Amendment) Act 2019 and DPDP Act 2023 — RTI (Amendment) Act 2019 - tenure and salaries

x: The criticism is that executive control over tenure and remuneration may weaken the institutional autonomy of the Information Commissions.
Originally, the CIC’s tenure was five years or until the age of 65 years, whichever was earlier, and there was no reappointment.
At the central level, the CIC’s salary was equated with that of the Chief Election Commissioner and an IC’s with that of an Election Commissioner.

secs.t: Amendments → changes — RTI (Amendment) Act 2019 and DPDP Act 2023 — DPDP Act 2023 and Section 8(1)(j)

x: Section 44(3) rewrote Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, dropping the earlier test concerning relationship to public activity, unwarranted invasion of privacy and the public-interest override.
The Attorney-General opined in January 2026 that the amendment did not dilute the RTI Act.

secs.t: Cases and rulings → issue decided

x: The CIC ordered disclosure of CBSE
answer-book procurement details
and rejected the plea based on the fiduciary exemption under Section 8(1)(e).

CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay recognised evaluated answer sheets as information; Girish Deshpande treated service records and tax returns as personal information; Subhash Chandra Agarwal covered the CJI’s office; and Zee Telefilms held that BCCI was not State under Article 12.
The Supreme Court held that the examining body does not hold the evaluated answer sheets in a fiduciary capacity.
The Delhi High Court treated the income-tax return details as personal information and found no larger public interest justifying disclosure to the estranged wife.

secs.t: Proactive disclosure and online RTI — Section 4, portals, AP inspection

x: Section 4 mandates proactive or
suo motu disclosure by public authorities
, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.
From 22 June 2026, the AP Secretariat published Action Taken Reports on seven sector white papers as an example of disclosure in the spirit of Section 4.
The portal at rtionline.gov.in enables filing of RTI applications and first appeals to central public authorities and provides online fee payment.

secs.t: Issues and debates — misuse, pendency, activists' safety — Achievements vs misuse

x: Exam angle: Assertion-Reason pairs of "purpose of the Act" with "misuse" or "limited impact" - usually both true.
The Act has helped break secrecy, improve accountability, reduce corruption and misuse of public funds, and strengthen participation and service delivery.
C is correct: clogging offices with indiscriminate demands is misuse by applicants.

secs.t: Issues and debates — misuse, pendency, activists' safety — Pendency, vacancies and the re-examination debate

x: The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for
confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
, along with a possible ministerial veto.
The Economic Survey associated the uniquely broad RTI regime with a possible chilling effect on
honest decision-making
and proposed re-examination of the framework.
RTI activists and whistle-blowers face harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks in connection with their disclosures and applications.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sweden enacted the first RTI law in 1766, Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997, and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.
The identified concerns include appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists.
Vajja Srinivasa Rao
was identified as the Chief Information Commissioner of the Andhra Pradesh Information Commission.

x: Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy is based on hierarchy, rules, impersonality, specialisation, merit and written files.
F. Morstein Marx identified
guardian, caste, patronage and merit
bureaucracies in The Administrative State.
DoPT controls the IAS cadre, the Ministry of Home Affairs controls the IPS cadre, and MoEFCC controls the Indian Forest Service cadre.

secs.t: Articles 308-323 — services and PSCs

x: Article 310
embodies the Doctrine of Pleasure.

x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”.
The 17th Civil Services Day took place at Vigyan Bhawan on 21 April 2025 with the stated theme, after the event was not held in 2024 because of elections.

secs.t: Neutrality and anonymity — conduct rules, cases and circulars

require political neutrality and integrity.
The section officer was dismissed under Rule 9 of the Andhra Pradesh Civil Services (CCA) Rules, 1991, through G.O. Ms.

secs.t: Committees on civil service reform → year and focus

x: The D.S. Kothari Committee was associated with the three-stage examination system; Satish Chandra reviewed that scheme and introduced the essay paper; Y.K. Alagh reviewed the CSE system; and P.C. Hota dealt with civil service reforms.
The committees belong respectively to 1974–76, 1989, 2000–01, 2004 and 2016, giving the order D.S. Kothari, Satish Chandra, Y.K. Alagh, P.C. Hota and B.S. Baswan.

secs.t: Second ARC — chairman, reports → titles, recommendations

x: The 2nd ARC was constituted on 31 August 2005 under M. Veerappa Moily.
The Fourth Report concerned Ethics in Governance; the Tenth, Refurbishing of Personnel Administration; the Eleventh, Promoting e-Governance; and the Fifteenth, State and District Administration.
The Commission recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition.

secs.t: Generalist vs specialist and capacity building — lateral entry, Mission Karmayogi

x: The generalist design is recognised as having served nation-building, but the contemporary debate supports dedicated scientific cadres and separate scientific service rules in appropriate fields.
The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building was launched in 2020 with the
iGOT Karmayogi
online platform.
The Global Digital Capacity Building Alliance was launched in New Delhi on 20 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Civil servants serve as policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers in public administration; therefore, all three statements are correct.

The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005, and India ratified it in 2011.

x: Exam angle: 17A (approval before investigation) and 19 (sanction before prosecution) are often swapped in statements.

Vineet Narain (1997) and Subramanian Swamy (2014)

secs.t: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 and the 2015 Bill — Enactment

x: A whistleblower includes any public servant or other person, including an NGO, who makes a public interest disclosure of specified wrongdoing to the Competent Authority.

secs.t: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 and the 2015 Bill — Protections, complaints and penalties

x: The term 'victimisation' is identified as a weakness because it is

in the framework.

May 2015
The Bill proposed restrictions on disclosures in Section 8(1)-type categories, including sovereignty, security and Cabinet papers, and lapsed with the 16th Lok Sabha in 2019.

Santhanam Committee
on Prevention of Corruption was constituted in 1962 and its recommendations contributed to stronger anti-bribery laws, eventually consolidated in the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

x: The Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 provides for confiscation and imprisonment up to seven years, not ten years.

secs.t: Lokayukta and citizens' oversight — FIRSTs, AP Act, social audit

x: The 2013 Act obliged every State to establish a Lokayukta within
one year
of its commencement; States then framed widely differing laws.
Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.
Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.

rows.title: Liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation - meaning, the 1991 reforms, sequencing

secs.t: LPG — terms → meaning; PSU categories

x: Liberalisation ends licences, quotas and controls.
A private stake exceeding 51 per cent transfers
ownership and management
of the public sector undertaking.
Disinvestment involves sale of part of the equity of a public sector undertaking to the public.
Nine PSUs were given Navratna status and greater autonomy in 1997 (NCERT-based sources give 1996).
The New PSE Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat, 2021, favours
strategic disinvestment

secs.t: Industrial policies and Acts → year and thrust (1948-1991)

x: The 1991 Industrial Policy Statement emphasised de-licensing, restructuring of MRTP provisions, foreign direct investment and autonomy for PSUs through Memoranda of Understanding.
The Licence Raj involved licensing for starting, closing or expanding firms, reservation for small-scale industries and price controls.
The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act was enacted in 1969, relaxed in 1980 and later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, administered by the CCI.

secs.t: 1991 crisis — persons, figures, stabilisation vs structural adjustment

x: The 1991 New Economic Policy was led politically by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and implemented under Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
Industrial de-licensing
is a structural-adjustment measure intended to improve efficiency.
The 1991 trade reforms initiated a move towards
a market-determined rupee
, with the market-determined exchange rate operating from 1993.

secs.t: 1991 reform measures — part of LPG or not

x: Industrial licensing was largely abolished, but it was retained for
alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence, and drugs
The reform material lists defence, atomic energy and railways among reserved areas, while the present position stated is limited to atomic energy and railway operations.
Import licensing was abolished except for hazardous or environmentally sensitive items

secs.t: Reform generations → content — sequencing debate

x: It lists the first-generation reforms of 1991-2000.
Average tariffs declined from about 125 per cent in the late 1980s to about 30 per cent by the early 2000s.
Reforms 2.0 are framed as reforms from 2014 onwards, including digital public infrastructure, Aadhaar, UPI, Jan Dhan and direct benefit transfer.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Washington Consensus was formulated by John Williamson in 1989.
Protection of property rights was one of the prescriptions associated with the Washington Consensus.
LENS (July 2026) describes LPG as ‘Reforms 1.0’ and argues for a third wave of reforms.

High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure
of the Constitution.

draft intended to provide a common framework for infrastructure regulators.

Regulators’ annual reports and accounts are laid before Parliament and examined by the
Departmentally Related Standing Committees
The FSDC
coordinates financial regulators
and helps address overlap among them.
The CCI penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance via data sharing.

institutional autonomy

x: Civil society organisations are described as the third sector, alongside government and the market, while functioning as development partners and democratic watchdogs.
Almond and Powell classify pressure groups as
institutional, associational, non-associational and anomic
Pressure groups are described as the '
Anonymous Empire
' because they influence public policy without directly seeking governmental office.

x: Societies are registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860; private trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882; public charitable trusts under State laws; and not-for-profit companies under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.
The policy seeks an enabling environment, easier resource mobilisation and partnership with government.
The policy favours
transparency, self-regulation and codes of conduct
rather than tight government control.

secs.t: FCRA — Act timeline, amendments, data and 2026 changes — Timeline and administration

x: The Ministry of Home Affairs administers FCRA, while FEMA, 1999 is administered by the Reserve Bank of India and the Enforcement Directorate.
The retrospective 2016 amendment followed the Delhi High Court's 2014 Vedanta-donations ruling and excluded Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms from the definition of foreign sources.
Contributions must first be received in the designated FCRA account at SBI, New Delhi.

secs.t: FCRA — Act timeline, amendments, data and 2026 changes — Registration, cancellation and data

x: Cancellation may arise from breach of the law or conditions, non-functioning, or administrative defaults such as non-filing of returns or delayed renewal.
The Public Health Foundation of India was placed under the FCRA prior-permission category in 2017 for
lobbying with parliamentarians

secs.t: FCRA — Act timeline, amendments, data and 2026 changes — 2026 changes

x: FCRA registration is valid for
five years
The Bill proposed an authority empowered to take over the assets of NGOs whose registration was cancelled or suspended.
Five categories (social, economic, educational, cultural, religious) with separate fees per category and per State/UT.

secs.t: SHGs and women's microfinance → bodies, year and features

x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh follows a quasi-wholesale model: it lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which lend onward to poor women and SHGs.
The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was piloted in 1992 and encourages banks to lend to SHGs of poor women.
DAY-NRLM is community-driven and develops SHG members as community resource persons.

secs.t: Pressure group techniques and terms → meaning

x: Lobbying means dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation and regulation.
Petitioning
involves submitting written demands or memoranda to authorities.
Litigation includes PILs and court cases, such as electoral cases filed by ADR.
Strikes, bandhs and dharnas are forms of direct action intended to disrupt normal activity and force public or governmental attention.

secs.t: Media — fourth estate, problems and Press Council of India

x: The misuse of
UAPA, IT Rules and defamation law
is identified as a concern affecting media freedom.
The Press Council can warn, admonish or censure newspapers and journalists and covers print media only.
The PCI is a statutory, quasi-judicial body under the Press Council Act, 1978 (first set up in 1966 under the 1965 Act).

secs.t: Changes in the role of civil society

x: The stated shift is from welfare delivery to
rights and empowerment
Civil society organisations have moved beyond service delivery to advocacy, policy formulation and watchdog functions; .

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — Amaravati agitation, AP pressure groups, fake-news task force

x: Farmers involved in land pooling in Amaravati protested from December 2019 against
the three-capitals plan
The AP NGOs' Association and farmers' associations, including rythu sanghams, are examples of pressure groups.
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet asked the police for a task force to address fake news and defamatory content on social media.

x: FCRA curbs and NGO funding regulations are specifically debated in relation to shrinking civic space.
A recognised criticism is that pressure groups may capture policy for narrow interests.
The opposition letters were written by
K.C. Venugopal and John Brittas
, seeking withdrawal of the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026.
The NEET paper-leak protests drew solidarity from
Sri Lanka
n civil society in July 2026.

rows.title: Globalisation and society - culture, migration, labour, inequality; the anti-globalisation critique

secs.t: Globalisation — meaning and cultural-change terms → meaning

x: Glocalisation means local adaptation, homogenisation means convergence, hybridisation means blending, and McDonaldisation means the spread of fast-food principles.
Assimilation
occurs when a minority culture is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its distinct identity.
McDonaldisation
refers to the spread of fast-food principles such as efficiency, calculability, predictability and control across society.

secs.t: Theorists and leaders → concepts, books and stands

x: Appadurai’s five scapes are ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes and ideoscapes. ‘
Politiscapes
’ is not included in this list.

The World Social Forum is associated with the slogan ‘Another world is possible’; the Seattle protests opposed the WTO Ministerial; Vandana Shiva advocates seed sovereignty; and Joseph Stiglitz criticised IMF policy conditions.
Mahendra Singh Tikait opposed the Dunkel Draft, GATT and WTO.

secs.t: Reports and surveys → publisher and data

x: MoSPI’s survey runs for a year from July 2026, is the first full survey since 2007–08, and the migrant share in PLFS 2020–21 was 28.9%.
The official view is that inequality matters less than it did in the early 2010s, while the comparability of data remains contested in the HCES 2023–24 debate.

secs.t: Migration and labour — Gulf remittances, government measures, informal workers

x: The
Ministry of External Affairs
signs Migration and Mobility Partnerships and runs Pre-Departure Orientation Training under the Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana.
Remittances and services exports offset pressures arising from the
trade deficit
and help keep the current account deficit stable.
The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Bill, 2025 replaced
MGNREGA

secs.t: Impact of globalisation → youth, farmers, women and artisans

x: ‘Mindless aping’ refers to the uncritical imitation of Western lifestyles, identified as a cultural risk accompanying global integration.
The concerns include cheap imports under WTO rules, while debt- and crop-failure-related farmer suicides were especially marked in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
Small farmers constitute about 98% of coffee growers and face global price swings as well as competition from Brazil and Vietnam.

secs.t: Anti-globalisation movements → event, year and place

x: The first World Social Forum was held in Porto Alegre, Brazil, in 2001.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism is that globalisation can widen disparities between rich and poor people and between nations, and can develop into ‘commercial imperialism’.
Gulf-dependent remittance households face uncertainty arising from
the 2026 West Asia war
The stated current-relevance references are the World Migration Report 2026, World Inequality Report 2026 and the MoSPI migration survey of July 2026.
A key criticism is that globalisation widens rich-poor and inter-nation gaps.

rows.title: Indian society - salient features, unity in diversity, continuity and change
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Indian society — salient features, bases of diversity and data

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2014 listed
excess population in villages, various religions, various castes
as main features of Indian social structure; poverty was the option left out.
Indian social life has historically been centred on
castes, ethnic groups and extended families
B.S. Guha's racial classification included Negrito, Proto-Australoid and other elements.

secs.t: Sociologists → statements and contributions

x: Andre Beteille
described traditional caste-based cumulative inequality giving way to dispersed, class-type inequality.
Louis Dumont
and D. Pocock founded Contributions to Indian Sociology in 1957.
Durkheim is associated with social facts, Weber with class-status-power, Marx with alienation, and Comte with positivism.
Verstehen, associated with Max Weber, means
interpretive understanding
of social action.

secs.t: Books → authors

x: Durkheim’s works appeared in the order Division of Labour (1893), Rules of Sociological Method (1895), Suicide (1897), and Elementary Forms of Religious Life (1912).
Marx linked class struggle with dialectical materialism, discussed alienation, and authored The Communist Manifesto (1848) and Das Kapital (1867).
Sociological imagination was coined by C. Wright Mills, network society by Manuel Castells, social facts by Durkheim, and verstehen by Weber.

secs.t: Concepts of change and terms → originator and meaning

x: McKim Marriott associated universalisation with the upward movement of local elements into the Great Tradition, illustrated by the integration of local Jagannath with Vishnu.

Robert Redfield originated the Great and Little Tradition; McKim Marriott proposed Universalisation and Parochialisation; M.N. Srinivas developed dominant caste; N.K. Bose is associated with the Hindu method of tribal absorption.

secs.t: Unity in diversity and national integration — bonds, threats, remedies

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2025 A-R. National integration has
political, economic, social, cultural and psychological
dimensions (keyed: A true, R false).
Shankaracharya is associated with sending priests from the south to temples in the north and vice versa, thereby strengthening cultural links.
Article 350-B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

secs.t: Continuity and change — forces of change → effect

x: The script remains undeciphered, and together with the urban collapse around 1900 BCE this limits the evidence.
Urbanisation and industrialisation produce nuclear households and make the family a consumption unit, not a production unit.
Digital citizenship is associated with technology and the
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All four were included among the mentioned classical-literature translations: Sangam works, a Telugu Silappathikaram, and the Odia works Charyapada and Madalapanji.
The report proposing a National Mission for Mother-Tongue-Based Multilingual Education was mentioned on

, 21 February 2026.

the safety-valve reorganisation of States

rows.title: Family - types, functions and changing structure in India
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Family — definitions and types

x: A
neo-local
family residence is established independently by the married couple.
In a duo-local arrangement, spouses stay with their respective natal families.
The
family of orientation
is the family into which a person is born, whereas the family of procreation is established after marriage.
Murdock's three features are common residence, economic co-operation and reproduction; political sovereignty is not one.

secs.t: Family functions → Murdock, Ogburn, Parsons

x: Murdock identified sexual, reproductive, economic and educational functions as four universal functions;
judicial function
is not included.
Parsons identified primary socialisation of children and stabilisation of the adult personality as the two irreducible functions of the family.
Dysfunction
refers to persistent failure of family functions, such as failure caused by abuse or alcoholism.

secs.t: Sociologists → statements on the joint family

x: Mukherjee found joint families over-represented in trade and higher occupations.
Karve emphasised functional unity and obligations more than co-residence; she also described the joint family as a residential unit holding common property.
Shah distinguished family from household.
The developmental cycle is A.M. Shah's; Uberoi studied media and the modern family.

secs.t: Matrilineal family systems → community and region

x: Among Tiyans, some Moplas and Bants, the tharawad consists of a woman, her siblings and her sisters’ children; the husband is not part of the unit.
Among the Garo, Machong is the matrilineage and the heiress’s husband, called
nokma
, heads the household.
The Nair tharavad followed Marumakkathayam (matrilineal inheritance), which was abolished by the
Joint Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975

secs.t: Acts, schools and cases on inheritance and family courts

x: Mitakshara is Vijnaneshwara’s commentary on the
Yajnavalkya Smriti
, composed in the Kalyani Chalukya court.
Mitakshara recognised coparcenary rights by birth and survivorship, whereas under Dayabhaga the right arose only on the father’s death.
*Vineeta Sharma* (2020) held that daughters’ coparcenary rights by birth apply irrespective of whether the father was alive in 2005.

secs.t: Data — households and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

x: More than half of all households were nuclear in 2011.
NFHS-5 reported urban and rural fertility rates of 1.6 and 2.1 respectively, while NFHS-6 reported an overall rate of 2.0.
NFHS-6, released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with IIPS Mumbai as nodal agency, covered 6.79 lakh households in 715 districts.

secs.t: Changes, issues and high-risk families

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2014 asked how T.K. Oommen distinguished urban families. Answer:
all of
mode of earning and value pattern, structure of authority, and urban milieu and social ecology.
Legislation and marital dissolution bring more separation, single parenting and divorce, and women's employment raises female-headed households.
Elderly care rests on filial piety, and nuclearisation and migration strain it, so alternative care is needed.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: N. Chandrababu Naidu urged a return to the joint family and incentives for having two or more children in the context of declining fertility.
Marxist sociologist
I.P. Desai
linked the emergence of nuclear households to capitalism.
Andhra Pradesh made its succession amendment in 1985, which was 20 years before the central amendment of 2005.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Forms of marriage — Vedic and customary terms → meaning

x: Niyoga permitted a wife to cohabit with a designated man for begetting a child when her husband was impotent or dead.
The Later Vedic period saw the emergence of child marriage, decline of Swayamvara, discouragement of widow remarriage and prohibition of marriage within the same gotra.
Anuloma referred to a higher-varna man marrying a lower-varna woman and was tolerated.

secs.t: Rules of mate selection — endogamy, exogamy, gotra, sapinda

x: Exam angle: the Delhi HC upheld
HMA Sec. 5(v)
(the sapinda bar).
The stated North Indian pattern is
caste endogamy, clan or gotra exogamy and village exogamy
The sasan rule bars marriage with members of the patri-family and with sapinda kin.
The Delhi High Court upheld
Section 5(v)
, which concerns the sapinda restriction, subject to the statutory framework regarding custom.

secs.t: Tribal ways of acquiring a mate → tribe

x: Compulsory registration under the Hindu Marriage Act
was not such a tribal form.
Capture marriage is associated with the
Naga, Ho, Bhil and Gond
communities.
Service/bride price with the groom working at the bride's home is cited for the Gonds; Nagas are cited for capture.
Atta Satta is a bride-exchange practice in Rajasthan, which was criticised by the Rajasthan High Court.

secs.t: Persons → contributions on marriage

x: Satyashodhak marriage, started by Savitribai Phule, used no dowry and no Brahmin priest.

secs.t: Marriage Acts → year and provisions

x: Self-respect marriages were institutionalised by Periyar and validated through
Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act
by a Tamil Nadu amendment in 1967.
A Kazi conducts Nikah, Anand Karaj takes place in a gurdwara, and a Marriage Officer solemnises a marriage under the Special Marriage Act.
The Bill makes polygamy cognizable and non-bailable, provides up to seven years' rigorous imprisonment, and exempts Sixth Schedule areas.

secs.t: Sections on bigamy and divorce — HMA, IPC/BNS, Muslim law

x: Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground, but the Supreme Court can use Article 142, and Naveen Kohli urged legislative recognition of the ground.
A Muslim wife may seek khula by mutual consent and may invoke the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939.
The Act, which followed Shayara Bano (2017), makes instant triple talaq void and illegal and gives the wife subsistence allowance and custody of minor children.

secs.t: Cases and judgments on marriage

x: The Supreme Court held instant triple talaq unconstitutional in
Shayara Bano
On 1 July 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA
overrides the personal-law puberty rule for all religions
In Supriyo (Oct 2023) the Supreme Court refused to read same-sex marriage into the SMA; CJI Chandrachud was in the minority.

secs.t: Child marriage — PCMA 2006, data and Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat

x: The Bill proposed raising women's minimum age to 21 and creating a Central Reporting Portal.
NFHS-6 reported that
of women aged 20–24 were married before 18; the rural figure was 23.3%.
Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat aims to cut child marriage by 10% by 2026 and eliminate it by 2030.

secs.t: Changing trends — inter-caste, live-in and same-sex unions

x: Only about 5% of marriages are inter-caste.
Uttarakhand's UCC makes registration of live-in relationships mandatory.
Companionate marriage, rising age at marriage, serial monogamy and increasing divorce are identified trends.
Nepal
was the first South Asian nation to register a same-sex marriage (APPSC 2025 PYQ).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated target is to cover all 21 NDA States by 2029.
Uttarakhand's UCC has been in force since January 2025.
The Andhra Pradesh adolescent-education programme covers child marriage in 9,675 schools.

rows.title: Kinship - descent, lineage, clan, kinship terminology; North-South Indian kinship contrast
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Kinship — definitions, types and degrees

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025. Ravindra-Seema's children are Krishna and Madhavi; Madhavi-Harish's daughter is Jyothi.
Krishna-Jyothi
(maternal uncle-niece) is consanguineous. Ravindra-Seema, Madhavi-Harish and Krishna-Harish are affinal.
Godparenthood, dharam bhai or behen relationships and rakhi ties are examples of ritual or fictive kinship.
Buddhist monks’ use of kin terms for fellow monks represents a spiritual family and is an example of fictive kinship.

secs.t: Descent rules and descent groups → meaning

x: Patrilineal descent is found among the
Kondhs, Santhals and Bhils
, while Khasi, Garo and Nair are examples of matrilineal communities.
A
lineage
is a unilineal descent group whose members trace descent from a known ancestor and which is exogamous.
Gotra is an exogamous Hindu clan, and the same-gotra bar dates from
the Later Vedic period

secs.t: Kinship terminology and usages → meaning

x: A classificatory term uses one word for several categories of kin, such as different kinds of uncle.
Kinship terms may be classified by structure or use, and Kapadia connected them with marriage and inheritance rules.
Couvade is the practice in which the husband imitates or observes his wife’s pregnancy-related taboos.

secs.t: Scholars → books and contributions on kinship

x: L. H. Morgan
proposed the classificatory-descriptive distinction in Systems of Consanguinity and Affinity (1871).
Kolenda's 1968 work built on Karve, not Dumont.

secs.t: North-South kinship contrast — Karve's zones, Dumont

x: North Indian kinship is characterised by gotra and village exogamy and sasan or sapinda marriage prohibitions.
Marriage with the elder sister's daughter, FZD or MBD is a South Indian preference (symmetry).
In the South there is continuity between natal and marital families; the break is a North Indian feature.
Dumont associated the South with immediate exchange, closely clustered kin and greater freedom for women.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Cross-cousin and uncle-niece marriage are features of the South Indian kinship pattern and are common in Andhra Pradesh, where the practice is known as Telugu menarikam.
Kinship rules shape marriage choice, inheritance patterns and the form of households.
Karve is regarded as the ‘Mother of Indian Kinship Studies’ because she was the first to map Indian kinship systematically.

rows.title: Caste - features, theories of origin, varna-jati distinction
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Caste — etymology, varna vs jati and numbers

x: The term caste is derived from the Portuguese
casta
, meaning race or breed.
Jati consists of numerous local and regional groups, not exactly four groups.
Each varna is subdivided into jatis
The 1931 Census recorded 4,147 castes.

secs.t: Scholars → definitions of caste

x: S.V. Ketkar emphasised membership by birth and the prohibition on marrying outside the caste.
Risley described caste in terms of families sharing a common name, claiming descent from a mythical ancestor and following the same hereditary calling.
Bouglé named hereditary specialisation, hierarchy and repulsion.

secs.t: Theories and periods of origin of caste

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2007 asked when caste "began" as a new social organisation (after the Vedic period / Mauryan / Gupta / after Gupta). The printed key is garbled in your bank. Your notes date the crystallisation to the
Later Vedic
age.

Risley gave the racial theory, Nesfield the occupational theory (hereditary occupations became guilds, then castes), Abbé Dubois the Brahminical/political theory (a device of Brahmins to keep superiority), and Sarat Chandra Roy the cultural theory (restrictions on commensality and intermarriage).

secs.t: Features of caste — Ghurye's six and other lists

x: Ghurye identified lack of
free choice of occupation
, not free choice of occupation, as a feature of caste.
G.S. Ghurye’s Caste and Race in India was published in 1932.
Caste has a vertical dimension expressed through ranking and a horizontal dimension expressed through grouping into separate communities.
Universal inter-caste commensality
is contrary to the commensal taboos associated with caste.

secs.t: Scholars → books and ideas on hierarchy and the tribe-caste continuum

x: Louis Dumont
analysed caste through the opposition of purity and impurity in Homo Hierarchicus, published in 1966.
McKim Marriott explained caste interaction and ranking through the exchange of coded substances, including food, water and services.

Bailey is associated with the tribe-caste continuum; Sinha with secondary state formation; Bose with *The Hindu Method of Tribal Absorption*; and Ghurye with the description of tribes as ‘backward Hindus’.

secs.t: Jajmani system — regional equivalents

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2020 matched the pairs above (answer 1-3-4-2).
The Jajmani system was a socio-economic and ritual arrangement in which the landholding jajman received hereditary services from kamin castes.
Adade is the regional equivalent in Karnataka.
The Ayagar or Ayagadu system was the Andhra village service arrangement.

secs.t: Caste among non-Hindus — SC Order → year

x: The tradition referred to here places the arrival of St Thomas in India in 52 AD.
Approximately
74 percent
of Indian Christians are stated to identify with lower castes.
Mazhabi Sikhs
are identified as the largest Scheduled Caste component among the Sikh groups mentioned.
The 1950 Order initially covered Hindus, Sikhs were included in 1956, and Buddhists were included in 1990.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Census 2027 is noted for the proposed enumeration of caste.
The study found that most Indians descend from two ancestral populations.
The Census is specifically described as shaping colonial understandings of caste.
The Satavahanas organised the eighteen professions; the Kakatiya era is called the ‘Age of Shudras’; and Brahmins were classified as Vaidiki or Niyogi.

Non-Brahmin mobilisation

The economic categories include food-gatherers and hunters, shifting cultivators, settled agriculturists, artisans, pastoralists and industrial labour.

Nomadic tribes do not have permanent settlements; pastoralists, hunters and entertainers are among the groups included in this description.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Ethnicity — definitions, types and data

x: An ethnic group consists of people who identify with one another through common language or dialect, history, society, culture or nation.
India’s linguistic diversity includes more than 19,500 returned languages and dialects, 121 languages, 270 mother tongues and 22 Scheduled Languages.
The conflict approach views groups as interest groups competing unequally, with South Africa and Sri Lankan Tamils cited as examples.

x: Rajni Kothari and Christophe Jaffrelot are associated with instrumentalist discussions, while Barth and Anderson are associated with constructivist perspectives.
Arnold Rose describes a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language that sees itself, and is seen by others, as different, with negative connotations.
Giddens identifies disadvantage, group solidarity and physical or social isolation as features associated with minorities;
constitutional sovereignty
is not included.

secs.t: Ethnic groups, languages and minorities → regions

x: The Nyishi (largest tribe of Arunachal) hold the Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival; the Apatani of Ziro valley grow wet rice without animals or machines; the Idu Mishmi observe the 'iyu-ena' taboo on killing tigers; the Tangkhul Naga of Manipur make Longpi pottery.
Khasi and Garo are official languages of Meghalaya alongside English, but neither is included in the Eighth Schedule.

secs.t: Ethnic movements → outfits, leaders and demands

x: Exam angle: code names of operations (Blue Star, APPSC 2025) and "ULFA belongs to" (Assam).

The Naga movement sought independence / Greater Nagalim; the Bodo movement moved from Udayachal to a Bodoland state; ULFA (April 1979) sought a sovereign Assam for ethnic Assamese; the Khalistan movement sought a separate Sikh state.

secs.t: Ethnic conflicts → places

x: The Manipur conflict has involved the Meitei demand for Scheduled Tribe status and the Kuki demand for separate administration, with the conflict continuing since May 2023.
The Tripura conflict developed between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers after demographic change.

The Sixth Schedule, under
Article 244(2)
, provides autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

is associated with secessionist pressures connected with Naga aspirations.
The shutdowns affected 12 of Manipur’s 16 districts.

rows.title: Processes of social change - sanskritisation, westernisation, modernisation, secularisation
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Social change — factors and sources

x: Modern education, legislation, behaviour-change communication and social movements are all identified as sources or illustrations of social change.
Inclusive growth was the goal of the Eleventh Plan (the Seventh Plan is linked with technology-led modernisation).
Seasonal migration of nomads is a routine, recurring cycle and does not alter social structure, so it is not a source of social change (APPSC 2019).

secs.t: Theories of social change → proponents

x: Spengler wrote about the decline of the West, Toynbee proposed challenge and response, Sorokin distinguished sensate and ideational cultures, and Pareto explained the circulation of elites.

The British school (Elliot Smith, Perry) saw Egypt as the source of culture; the German-Austrian school (Graebner, Schmidt) developed culture circles; the American school (Boas, Wissler) developed culture areas.

secs.t: M.N. Srinivas → concepts and statements

x: Reference groups may include Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and the locally dominant caste.
M.N. Srinivas
associated Westernisation with changes produced by more than 150 years of British rule.
Srinivas identified technology, institutions, ideology and values as levels at which the effects of British rule produced Westernisation.
Srinivas observed that urbanisation and education can alter authority patterns within families without necessarily ending the
joint family

secs.t: Other scholars → statements

x: Lerner's sequence is urbanisation, followed by literacy, media exposure and participation.
Singer showed that tradition and modernity can coexist, using Madras temple culture as an example.
Max Weber used the expression “disenchantment of the world” in relation to secularisation.

secs.t: Books → authors

x: W.F. Ogburn
propounded the concept of cultural lag in Social Change, published in 1922.
Lerner wrote The Passing of Traditional Society (1958).

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: Assimilation
occurs when a minority merges fully into the wider society and loses its distinct identity.
Ogburn held that material culture, particularly technology, changes faster, while beliefs, norms and other non-material elements lag behind.
De-sanskritisation involves rejecting Sanskritic norms and asserting one's own identity, as illustrated by the non-Brahmin or Dravidian movement.

secs.t: Comparisons, lag factors and indicators

x: The example illustrates
cultural lag
because technological change is faster than the adjustment of social norms.
Constitutional secularism is associated here with Articles 25 to 28, concerning freedom of religion and the state's relationship with religious practice.
Sociological secularisation and constitutional secularism are distinct, and constitutional secularism does not require the exclusive removal of religion from public life.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sanskritisation may provide mobility to a caste but leaves the hierarchy intact; the Westernisation-modernisation debate concerns value-neutrality.
The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan uses
community outreach and street plays
as tools of behavioural change.
Srinivas preferred to treat Westernisation as ethically neutral, whereas modernisation is commonly value-loaded through the idea of progress.

, illustrating that stratification is not confined to Hindus.

x: Functionalism is associated with Davis and Moore; the conflict approach with Marx; the multi-dimensional approach with Weber; and the ideological caste approach with Dumont.
Davis and Moore argued that unequal rewards help attract scarce talent to positions considered functionally important.

A dominant caste combines
numerical strength, sizeable arable land and fairly high ritual rank

is associated with Andre Beteille.

x: Horizontal mobility
means a change of position without movement up or down the social hierarchy, such as moving between similar clerical jobs.
Sanskritisation is the process by which lower castes imitate the rituals and lifestyle of higher castes to seek upward social mobility.

Vertical mobility is movement up or down; horizontal mobility is movement at the same level; inter-generational mobility occurs between parents and children; structural mobility results from occupational restructuring.

secs.t: Caste vs class — comparison and change

x: Caste is generally characterised as a closed system, whereas class is an open system.
Conflicts are now about power, not ritual status.

secs.t: Casteism — definitions and caste vs casteism

x: Casteism is the evil form of the caste system involving discrimination and prejudice based on caste, along with concentration of power, money and prestige in a few castes.
Caste is a social structure involving hereditary and endogamous identity, whereas casteism is an attitude and practice involving partisan loyalty and the use of caste for gain.

secs.t: Thinkers and reformers → statements and contributions

x: Kaka Kalelkar described casteism as “
an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty
” that ignores justice, fair play and universal brotherhood.

division of labourers
.” He argued that it splits the working class and blocks collective bargaining.
AP reformer
Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu
organised Saha Pankti Bhojanam as an initiative promoting inter-caste dining.

secs.t: Books → authors
Causes and manifestations of casteism

Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala
are identified as States where empowered Dalits show both more inter-caste unions and more honour killings.

rows.title: Communalism - meaning, causes, forms and growth in India
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Communalism — meaning, distinction and FIRSTs

x: In India, communalism is commonly understood as religious differences between groups that generate tension and rioting, often when one group promotes its interests at the expense of others.
Religious fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal, emphasising a return to fundamentals and literal scripture.
Both statements are true, and the mobilisation of one community against others explains why communalism necessarily has an “us versus them” or relational character.

secs.t: Scholars and leaders → definitions, statements and roles

x: Exam angle: definition → scholar matching (asked in APPSC-G2 2025).
T.K. Oommen identified six dimensions ranging from assimilationist to secessionist, while Asghar Ali Engineer is a leading scholar of communalism and communal harmony.

Syed Ahmad Khan is associated with the ideological basis of the Two-Nation Theory, Iqbal with the proposal for a consolidated Muslim state, Jinnah with the Fourteen Points, and Ramsay MacDonald with the Communal Award.

secs.t: Types and stages — Oommen's six dimensions, Bipan Chandra's three stages

x: Assimilationist communalism involves the absorption of smaller religious groups into a larger one, as illustrated by claims that STs, Jains, Sikhs and Buddhists are Hindus.
Extreme communalism treats community interests as mutually antagonistic and is expressed through fear, hatred and violence; .
After the 1937 elections, the Muslim League adopted extreme communalism based on
fear, hatred and violence

secs.t: Causes of communalism — factor → cause

x: The recording of caste and religion in the first census of
is identified as a historical or colonial factor contributing to communalism.
The Arya Samaj promoted Shuddhi and Sangathan, while Muslim organisations promoted Tabligh and Tanzim in the 1920s.
Separate electorates are historical or colonial; vote-bank politics is political; poverty is economic; and delayed justice is legal-administrative.

rows.title: Human rights - concept, generations of rights, UDHR, ICCPR and ICESCR; UN human rights machinery

secs.t: Human rights — concept and Karel Vasak's three generations

x: Human rights are inherent and inalienable, rest on human dignity and are universal across cultures.
Karel Vasak (1977) proposed three generations mapped to liberty, equality and fraternity.
First-generation rights are civil and political; second-generation rights are economic, social and cultural; third-generation rights are collective rights such as peace and development.

secs.t: UDHR, 1948 — adoption, features, rights included and not included

x: The UDHR was adopted by the UNGA on 10 December 1948 (Human Rights Day) and Eleanor Roosevelt chaired its drafting.
A
right to universal basic income
is not included.
The UDHR is not a treaty and is not legally binding as a treaty.
The UDHR protects privacy under Article 12 and the ICCPR protects it under Article 17.

secs.t: International Bill of Human Rights — ICCPR, ICESCR, protocols → year

x: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.
The ICESCR covers work, social security, health and education, with these rights realised progressively.
The ICCPR First OP (1966) allows individual complaints and the Second OP (1989) concerns abolition of the death penalty.

x: India ratified CERD in 1968 and CEDAW in 1993, signed but did not ratify CAT in 1997, and acceded to CRC in 1992.

The UN General Assembly recognised the
right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment
as a universal human right on 28 July 2022.

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2018 asked the Asia-Pacific seat count (
