secs.t: Appointment, term, resignation and removal → NHRC vs SHRC — Appointed by

x: Exam angle: "appointed by" = President.
The six-member committee is the Prime Minister (chair), Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses and the Union Home Minister.
The CM chairs the committee (with the Speaker, State Home Minister and LoP in the Assembly), and bicameral States add the Council's Chairman and LoP.

secs.t: Appointment, term, resignation and removal → NHRC vs SHRC — Consultation

x: Appointment of a sitting Supreme Court Judge or a sitting High Court Chief Justice requires consultation with the
Chief Justice of India
Insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity, unsound mind and conviction for moral turpitude are grounds of removal by the President.
Since 2006 the SHRC Chairperson resigns in writing to the Governor, and since 2019 the term is 3 years or 70, whichever is earlier.

secs.t: Acts and amendments → year and change

x: Exam angle: "Member is not eligible for re-appointment" is the WRONG statement; after office, chairperson/members are ineligible for further government employment.

Before 2019 a member could be reappointed for only one more five-year term; the 2019 amendment removed this five-year limit, so members remain eligible for reappointment (subject to the 3-year/70 age term).
The term became 3 years or 70, SHRC Chairperson eligibility was widened to HC Judges, and three commission heads were added to the four deemed members.

secs.t: Functions and powers → detail

x: The Commission’s civil-court powers include summoning persons, examining them on oath, requiring documents, and requisitioning public records.
In 1997, the Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the
Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Custodial deaths are to be reported to the NHRC within
24 hours
; post-mortem videography and independent investigation are also associated safeguards.
NHRC guidelines and PUCL v. Maharashtra (2014) require reporting and a magisterial inquiry in cases of encounter deaths.

secs.t: Jurisdiction and limitations → NHRC vs SHRC — Division of functions

x: An SHRC deals with subjects in the State List and Concurrent List.
The Central Government may confer the human-rights functions of a Union Territory on an SHRC.
The arrangement prevents simultaneous inquiry by the SHRC, NHRC or another statutory commission into the same pending matter.

secs.t: Jurisdiction and limitations → NHRC vs SHRC — Limitations

x: In armed-forces cases, the NHRC may
seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations
In armed-forces cases, the Central Government must inform the NHRC of the action taken within
three months
Sub judice matters are not taken up by the Human Rights Commission while they are pending before a court.
The expression includes the naval, military and air forces, as well as any other armed forces of the Union.

secs.t: Reports, Paris Principles and GANHRI → terms

x: The SHRC submits its annual report to the State Government, which lays it before the State Legislature along with a memorandum of action taken.
The NHRC annual report is laid before each House of Parliament along with
a memorandum of action taken
The Paris Principles, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993, set standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission → establishment and cases

x: In the Gade Sai Krishna case, the NHRC directed the Andhra Pradesh SHRC, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary to report.
The NHRC sought reports from the AP DGP, Chief Secretary and SHRC
within a week
in connection with the alleged custodial death of Gade Sai Krishna.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Activist
Harish Iyer
resigned from the NHRC's LGBTQI+ core group, alleging non-consultation on the Bill.
The criticism refers to the NHRC's non-binding advice, the one-year bar and limitations concerning complaints involving the armed forces.
Optional creation, advisory powers and vacancies are weaknesses of SHRCs, and SHRCs in the highest-GDP States receive only 80 paise per capita.

rows.title: Custodial violence, encounter deaths, prison reforms, death penalty debate

secs.t: Cases on custodial violence, police and encounters → principle

x: Nilabati Behera concerns compensation, Joginder Kumar concerns justified arrest and informing relatives, D.K. Basu concerns arrest safeguards, and Arnesh Kumar restricts automatic arrest for offences up to seven years.
D.K. Basu required safeguards such as an arrest memo, identification of officers, informing kin and medical examination.
PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.

secs.t: Guidelines and directives → points

x: Prakash Singh (2006) issued
seven

directives: State Security Commission, DGP from a UPSC panel with a 2-year tenure, 2-year tenure for field officers, separation of investigation from law and order, Police Establishment Board, National Security Commission and Police Complaints Authorities.
The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations and requires mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.

secs.t: Death penalty and mercy → cases and Articles

x: Jagmohan Singh (1973) upheld the death penalty (a–ii); Bachan Singh (1980) laid down 'rarest of rare', life the rule and death the exception (b–iii); Machhi Singh (1983) set categories of rarest cases and the aggravating-mitigating balance (c–i).

All three statements reflect the safeguards recognised in Shatrughan Chauhan (2014): unexplained delay may support commutation, pre-rejection solitary confinement is illegal, and 14 days should separate rejection from execution.

secs.t: Acts, Sections and constitutional entries → provision

x: CrPC Section 176(1A) made judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths; the corresponding BNSS provision is Section 196.
BNSS Section 218 requires Government sanction before courts take cognisance against public servants in the relevant circumstances, which may delay prosecution.
BNSS Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, reduced to one-third for first-time offenders, subject to the statutory conditions.

secs.t: Committees, Law Commission reports and conventions → year and focus

x: The proposed way forward includes ratifying UNCAT, passing a standalone anti-torture law and adopting the PEACE model of interviewing.

The Mulla Committee focused on comprehensive jail reforms, the Krishna Iyer Committee on women prisoners and women in police, and the Justice Amitava Roy Committee on overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial.

secs.t: Data — custodial deaths and prison statistics

x: The reported data recorded 2,253 police-custody deaths and only three convictions during 1999–2023.
Bihar
records the most police-custody deaths, followed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
Undertrials constituted approximately 73%, 9,028 had been held over five years and there were 34 women’s prisons.
National occupancy was 112.7% (a decade low); Delhi had the highest occupancy at 194.6%, followed by Meghalaya at 163.5%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: NCRB Prison Statistics 2024 reported prison occupancy at 112.7%, with undertrials constituting 73% of the prison population.
The NHRC sought reports in June 2026, and subsequently the Supreme Court gave the SIT seven-day custody of suspended CI Nagaraju.
Retributive justice emphasises punishment or retaliation for wrongdoing, whereas reformative justice focuses on rehabilitation and reform of the offender.

rows.title: Women's rights - constitutional provisions and the legal framework
sub: Group-II S3-11: Women in Indian society - status through history, patriarchy and the women's movement
Group-II S3-37: Constitutional and legal provisions for women - Articles 15(3), 39, 42, 51A(e), 243D; key legislations

secs.t: Gender terms, customs and status → meaning — Core concepts

x: Amartya Sen
coined the term ‘missing women’ to refer to the consequences of discrimination against women, including intra-household discrimination.
Niyoga did not mean prohibition of widow remarriage; it involved a childless widow or wife bearing a son by the husband’s brother or kinsman.
The practice was banned by the Madras Act of 1947 and, in Andhra Pradesh, by the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988.

secs.t: Gender terms, customs and status → meaning — Status by period

x: The status of women declined in the later Vedic and medieval periods, when practices such as purdah became prominent.
The GDI makes a female-to-male comparison in
health, education and command over resources
The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the
Gender Inequality Index
, not the GDI.

secs.t: Thinkers, reformers and leaders → contributions and statements — Thinkers

x: Bina Agarwal is associated with land rights and authored A Field of One’s Own.

secs.t: Thinkers, reformers and leaders → contributions and statements — Social reformers → reform

x: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj; Vidyasagar was associated with the Widow Remarriage Act; the Phules founded the Satyashodhak Samaj; and Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj.

Rammohan Roy is linked with the abolition of Sati (1829); the Phules set up a Home for the Prevention of Infanticide (1863); Kandukuri Veeresalingam brought widow remarriage and women's education to Telugu society; and Pandita Ramabai ran a widows' home at Pune.

secs.t: Thinkers, reformers and leaders → contributions and statements — Statements on women's status and progress → leader

x: This observation is associated with
Swami Vivekananda
The statement was made by
Mahatma Gandhi

Ambedkar measured a community's progress by the progress of its women (APPSC-G2 2025); Nehru said a nation's condition can be told from the status of its women (APPSC 2019); Vivekananda used the one-wing image; Gandhi called the 'weaker sex' label a libel.

secs.t: Books and reports → author

r: Committee on the Status of Women in India

secs.t: Women's movement and organisations → year and founders

x: In the 1973 Chipko movement, women of Chamoli hugged trees to protect them.
The Anti-Arrack Movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta in Nellore among women participating in literacy campaigns.
The movement began at Dubagunta in 1992, led to the arrack ban in 1993, and was followed by prohibition in 1995.

secs.t: Constitutional provisions and women's reservation → Article and quota

x: Articles 14, 15(1) and 16(2) respectively provide equality, prohibit sex discrimination and prohibit such discrimination in public employment.
Article 243D provides for at least one-third reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats.
Women constitute
about 46%
of Panchayati Raj Institution representatives nationally.
The 33% quota came into effect in the
Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry
Assemblies on 17 April 2026.

secs.t: International commitments → year

x: The UN General Assembly adopted CEDAW in 1979.
India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993.
The Beijing Platform for Action covers areas such as violence, economy and decision-making.
The International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women were held in Mexico City in 1975.
SDG 5, adopted in 2015, concerns
gender equality

secs.t: National policies → goals

x: The Eighth Plan marked a shift in policy emphasis from development of women to empowerment of women.
The policy objectives included advancement and empowerment, equal access to health, education and employment, ending discrimination and violence, and gender mainstreaming.
The 1987 Act addressed Sati and its glorification, while 2001 marked both the National Policy and the Year of Empowerment of Women.

secs.t: Laws on women → year and provision

x: The years are 1961 for the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1986 for the Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1987 for the Commission of Sati Act and 2006 for the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.
The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act dates to 1956, the Dowry Prohibition Act to 1961, the PCPNDT Act to 1994 and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act to 2019.

secs.t: Personal laws → Acts and amendments

x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate.
The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a civil marriage framework irrespective of religion.
The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.
Andhra Pradesh
made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment.

secs.t: Landmark judgements on women's rights → issue and outcome

x: Vineeta Sharma
(2020) recognised that a daughter is a coparcener by birth, whether or not the father was alive on 9 September 2005.
The Shah Bano judgment recognised the entitlement of a divorced Muslim woman to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC and also urged the adoption of a Uniform Civil Code.
The petition was filed by the
Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan
, associated with Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz.

secs.t: Reproductive rights laws → provisions

x: Sex selection is prohibited and cannot be permitted merely through the surrogate’s consent.
Abortion of a surrogate foetus is not prohibited outright.
Sex-selective ART is prohibited under the ART Act, 2021.
The Act prohibits disclosure of the woman’s identity.
The PCPNDT Act bans
sex selection and prenatal sex determination

secs.t: Work, pay and maternity laws → provisions — Equal pay

x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 addressed equal pay for equal work and prohibited gender bias in recruitment and promotion.
The Code subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act (with the Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Payment of Bonus Acts) and bans gender discrimination including against transgender persons.
The OSH Code, 2020 permits women to work during these hours with their consent and subject to safety safeguards.

secs.t: Work, pay and maternity laws → provisions — Maternity Benefit Act 1961 vs Amendment Act 2017

x: The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to
26 weeks
for women with fewer than two surviving children (at most 8 weeks before delivery); from the third child it stays 12 weeks.
The 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid maternity leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.
The 2017 position provides
12 weeks
of maternity benefit for the third child onwards.

secs.t: Institutions for women's justice → composition, functions and FIRSTs

x: The NCW is statutory, derives its authority from the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
The first women's court was set up in
West Bengal
, at Malda in 2013 (APPSC 2019).
The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary.

secs.t: Data — sex ratio, indices and LFPR

x: The sex ratio was 991 in NFHS-4 and increased to 1020 in NFHS-5.
Son preference, female foeticide or infanticide, dowry and neglect of girls are stated causes of a low sex ratio.
Haryana and Punjab are identified as the most male-skewed region, whereas Kerala and the North-East, including Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Mizoram, have the best sex-ratio balance.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Nirbhay Raho works through
Panchayati Raj Institutions
(PRIs).
The Bill aimed to redistribute Lok Sabha seats to speed up the quota, which still waits for Census and delimitation.
APSES 2024–25 identifies all three—women's participation in the labour force, institution building and crime against women—as gaps under SDG 5.
The expression ‘proxy’ women heads refers to situations in which elected women representatives are effectively controlled by others in local governance.

rows.title: Laws for women - Dowry Prohibition Act, Domestic Violence Act 2005, POSH Act 2013, Maternity Benefit Amendment
sub: Group-II S3-23: Dowry, domestic violence, sexual harassment and trafficking

secs.t: Women-specific Acts → year (timeline)

x: The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment.
The Indecent Representation law covers denigrating depiction and, as of 2025, monitoring extends to digital and AI-generated content.
The law originally started as the
Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act
, commonly abbreviated as SITA, and was later renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.

secs.t: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 → sections and penalties — Commencement and definition

x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage.
Dowry death is covered by BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B.
The 1986 changes introduced dowry death under IPC Section 304B and the presumption under Evidence Act Section 113B.

secs.t: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 → sections and penalties — Section → offence / penalty

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - the Act came into force on
1 July 1961
S.3 fixes five years as the minimum (not less than 5 years) plus a fine of not less than Rs 15,000 or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs
within seven years
of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.

secs.t: Domestic Violence Act, 2005 → definition, authorities, reliefs

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2015 - the PWDVA came into force on
26 October 2006
The Act is a
civil law
protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
Multiple reliefs may be sought in one case, including residence, protection, monetary relief, temporary custody and compensation; disposal is contemplated within 60 days.

secs.t: POSH Act, 2013 → committees and time limits

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2018 - the "Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal Act 2013" deals with
sexual harassment of women at the workplace
An employer who does not set up the Internal Committee, display the policy, run awareness programmes or act on reports can be fined up to
. ₹10,000, ₹15,000 and ₹25,000 are wrong; ₹15,000 is the minimum fine under s.3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

secs.t: Cases → Supreme Court directives (Vishaka, Laxmi)

x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least
₹3 lakh
The directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India provide
free treatment
for acid-attack victims in addition to compensation.
The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted.

secs.t: BNS sections → offences against women (IPC → BNS from 1 July 2024)

x: Rape is covered by Sections 63-64, trafficking by Section 143, selling or buying minors for prostitution by Sections 98-99, and acid attack by Section 124.
BNSS Section 144 provides for maintenance of wives
regardless of religion
; it corresponds to old CrPC Section 125.
BNS Section 124 provides a minimum punishment of ten years extending to life imprisonment for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.

secs.t: Trafficking → terms, tiers and forms

x: GLOTIP 2016 highlighted that traffickers and victims often come from the same national or ethnic background.

Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 does not fully meet them but is making significant efforts; Tier 2 Watch List is the watch-list category; and Tier 3 represents countries not making significant efforts.
The forms include sex trafficking, forced/bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and organ removal.

secs.t: Institutions and schemes → role

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - the MHA IT initiative for real-time crime/trafficking information and inter-state coordination is
Cri-MAC
743 Fast Track Special Courts were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, and 3,39,644 cases had been disposed of by 31 July 2025.
Cri-MAC
is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → implementation data

x: Protection Officers:
DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs.
Service Providers:
55 NGOs.
POSH in AP (AP SES 2025-26):
26 LCs and 10,437 ICs.
Women Helpline 181:
3 lakh+
calls in AP.
AP Shakti Sadans:
26 Shakti Sadans
, sheltering
women.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The compulsory Internal Complaints Committee report is linked to compliance under the POSH Act, 2013.
Poor enforcement, faulty First Information Reports, and presenting dowry-death cases as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.
The debate includes misuse claims as well as heavy under-reporting, not only conviction rates.

rows.title: Crimes against women - trafficking, honour crimes, acid attacks; Criminal Law Amendments 2013 and 2018
sub: Group-II S3-21: Crime against women - types, magnitude, causes and NCRB data
Group-II S3-22: Legal and institutional response to crimes against women

secs.t: Crimes against women — classification and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2019 - first women's court =
West Bengal
The
Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956
is an SLL head.
Cruelty by husband or relatives and kidnapping or abduction of women are IPC/BNS heads.
Foeticide, sati and eve-teasing are classified as social violence.
The first all-women police station was established at Kozhikode in Kerala in 1973.

secs.t: Causes → effects

x: Marital rape is not captured well in NCRB data because such incidents are substantially under-reported and remain insufficiently visible in official reporting systems.
The cited weaknesses are that women constitute only 11.7% of the police, rape conviction rates are low, and pendency in courts for crimes against women is over 90%.

secs.t: NCRB data → national crime figures — NCRB and Crime in India 2024

x: Telangana
had the highest crime rate against women in 2023, whereas Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of cases.

The 2024 report recorded 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes, incorporated BNS data for the first time alongside IPC data, was released in May 2026, and reported Odisha as having the highest violent-crime rate.
The rape conviction rate was 22.7% in 2023, down from approximately

secs.t: NCRB data → national crime figures — Crime heads ranked by share (2023 break-up)

x: The descending order is cruelty by husband or relatives at 29.8%, kidnapping and abduction at 19.8%, and assault with intent to outrage modesty at 18.7%.
Cruelty by husband or relatives
was the dominant head in NCRB 2024, at about 42% of crimes against women; it was also the top head in 2023 (29.8%).

secs.t: NFHS and Census data → dowry, child marriage, violence, sex ratio

x: NFHS-5 reported that
of ever-married women had faced spousal violence.
NFHS-5 reported that
of women aged 18–49 had faced physical violence.
The Child Sex Ratio was 918 in India and 944 in Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011.
India's Child Sex Ratio declined from 927 in 2001 to 918 in 2011.

secs.t: Criminal Law Amendments 2013 and 2018, BNS 2023 → provisions — Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ("Nirbhaya Act")

x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, while keeping the minimum punishment at seven years (it was raised to ten years in 2018).
Acid attack (326A) is now BNS 124(1), sexual harassment (354A) is BNS 75, stalking (354D) is BNS 78, and death for repeat rapists (376E) is BNS 71.

secs.t: Criminal Law Amendments 2013 and 2018, BNS 2023 → provisions — Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018

x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the
Kathua and Unnao cases
and was associated with the fast-track court response.
The 2018 amendment barred anticipatory bail in cases involving rape of a girl
below 16 years
Section 69 of the BNS addresses sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud.

secs.t: Trafficking and foeticide laws → Protocol, Acts, Bills

x: The PCPNDT Act permits diagnostic procedures for detecting
genetic abnormalities
, while prohibiting sex selection and prenatal sex determination.
The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.
Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.

secs.t: Cases and committees → outcomes (honour crimes, Nirbhaya, Verma)

x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, which respectively protect equality, prohibit discrimination, protect freedoms and safeguard life and personal liberty.
The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for
heinous crimes
, subject to the statutory process.

secs.t: Institutional mechanisms → key fact and funding

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2019 - OSCs are set up with grants from the
Nirbhaya Fund
. ERSS for women's safety =
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 to address the declining
Child Sex Ratio
and related discrimination against girls.
AHTUs are district-level task forces funded by the Ministry of Home Affairs for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution.

secs.t: IT initiatives → purpose (ITSSO, NDSO, CCTNS, Cri-MAC, Safe City)

x: ITSSO tracks investigation timelines; NDSO is the database of convicted sexual offenders; CCTNS links police stations; Cri-MAC enables real-time crime information sharing.
NDSO, established by the NCRB in 2018, is a police-only national database of convicted sexual offenders.
Safe City Projects use CCTV and artificial intelligence-based public-safety measures for women in eight major cities.

secs.t: Fast track and special courts → FTSC scheme

x: The FTSC scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund for cases involving rape and offences under POCSO.
The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 inserted Section 376E IPC, allowing death or life imprisonment for repeat rape offenders.
87,754 disposals against 80,320 registrations is a disposal rate of
about 109%
, meaning FTSCs disposed of more cases than were newly registered.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → Disha Bill, schemes and campaigns

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2022 - the SOS app is
Disha
. APPSC-GS 2018 - Chittoor's campaign is
Abhayam
; the Ongole pick-up scheme is
Abhay
The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to
the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case
The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → crime data and newer measures

x: Trishul committees are described as state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women’s Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets.
APSES 2024–25 aims for one of the lowest crime rates and provides for special courts for atrocity cases.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Disha model is associated with a 21-day verdict, the Nirbhaya Act with a two-month probe, Shakti Teams with the current Andhra Pradesh policing model, and SHe-Box 2.0 with the workplace-harassment complaint portal.
The measures included Trishul committees, a police response time of 30 minutes, and an emphasis on improving conviction rates.

rows.title: Women's political participation - 73rd/74th Amendment reservation, 106th Amendment; gender indices (GII, GGGI)
sub: Group-II M1-B-101: Women and weaker sections in local governance - reservation and its social outcomes

secs.t: FIRSTs — first women in posts, at the polls and in panchayats

x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
Pratibha Patil was the first woman President, Meira Kumar the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister, and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor.

secs.t: Women's Reservation Bill → year → fate

x: Articles 84 and 173 relate to qualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, respectively, and thereby permit women to contest elections when the qualifications are met.
The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.

secs.t: 106th Amendment and 131st Amendment Bill → Articles → provisions — Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 — Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam

x: The amendment provides reservation of one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including one-third within the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
Article 330A is the Lok Sabha quota, 332A the State Assemblies quota, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly quota, and 334A deals with commencement, duration and rotation.

secs.t: 106th Amendment and 131st Amendment Bill → Articles → provisions — Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 — defeated attempt to fast-track the quota

x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368.

secs.t: 73rd/74th Amendments → Articles → women's reservation

x: Article 243T(3)
provides for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats in Municipalities for women.
SC/ST reservation is proportionate to population, and chairperson offices are arranged under State law and rotation.
Article 243D(5) links the duration of SC/ST reservation in Panchayats to the period specified under
Article 334

secs.t: Data — women in local bodies, States at 50% and AP

x: Exam angle: "one-third at which level?" is answered by PRIs. "How many seats in AP?" is answered by
one-half
. 243D(3) is the Article for women's seats.
Andhra Pradesh provides
50 per cent
reservation for women in local bodies.
Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006.

secs.t: Initiatives and institutions → purpose (MoPR, ECI, NCW, SHGs)

x: Women's turnout first exceeded men's in 2019, did so again in 2024, and women voters are among the targets of the ECI's SVEEP programme.
The Abhiyan provides leadership, legal-awareness and gender-justice training, including modules on gender-based violence, for Women Elected Representatives.
Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to be established at least one per district, promote safe spaces and gender-responsive governance, and align with SHGs.

secs.t: Studies, terms and legal shield — women and SC/ST panchayat leaders

x: Chattopadhyay and Duflo used the
random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan
to study the effects of women’s political leadership.
“Sarpanch-pati” denotes proxy representation in which a male relative exercises the office formally held by an elected woman.
The relevant legal safeguards identified are
the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

secs.t: Gender indices → publisher → dimensions; India's rank

x: Exam angle: publisher-index matching; India's rank in a named year; which dimension is in which index.
GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.
The reproductive health dimension of GII includes
maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
India's GII position is pulled down especially by
low female labour-force participation and low political representation

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Local bodies have a one-third floor, half reservation operates in 19 States and Union Territories, and legislative reservation is linked to post-delimitation operation.
The existing experience of local-body quotas is described as the working model for the
106th Amendment
concerning women’s representation in legislatures.
The criticisms include delay of the women’s quota until post-Census delimitation, proxy representation, and the absence of an OBC-women sub-quota.

rows.title: Women's welfare schemes - Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Mission Shakti, PMMVY, Ujjwala

secs.t: MWCD umbrella missions → components

x: From 1 April 2022, MWCD schemes were organised under
three
umbrella missions: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya, and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0.
Mission Poshan 2.0 comprises Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
Mission Vatsalya is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2021-22 to 2025-26 (₹10,916 crore).

secs.t: Mission Shakti → sub-schemes → components

x: Exam angle: "Which is a sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?" Swadhar and Ujjawala no longer exist under their own names.
Samarthya includes Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY, SANKALP-Hub for Empowerment of Women and Gap Funding for Economic Empowerment.
Nari Adalat provides an alternative grievance-redressal mechanism for petty cases, including harassment and denial of entitlements.

secs.t: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao — launch, ministries, objectives, districts

x: The scheme is fully centrally funded, began in 100 districts with low Child Sex Ratio, and has subsequently expanded to all districts.
The scheme focuses on Child Sex Ratio, prevention of gender-biased sex selection, and the survival, protection and education of girls.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is included under the
Sambal
vertical, which deals with women’s safety.

secs.t: Schemes → year → target group (girl child, adolescent girls, shelter and livelihood) — Girl child and adolescent girls

x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 2015 under BBBP as a small-savings account scheme for girls below 10 years, primarily supporting education and marriage expenses.
Balika Samriddhi Yojana provides a post-birth grant and annual scholarships to girls from families living below the poverty line.
Dhanalakshmi was introduced in 2008 as a conditional cash-transfer scheme linked to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and delaying marriage beyond 18 years.

secs.t: Schemes → year → target group (girl child, adolescent girls, shelter and livelihood) — Shelter, livelihood and income (older schemes and successors)

x: Swadhar Greh is meant for
women in difficult circumstances
and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.
STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.
The Working Women Hostel scheme, introduced during 1972–73 for working women, is now known as
Sakhi Niwas

secs.t: Maternal schemes → year → benefit

x: IGMSY was the pilot maternity-benefit scheme; PMMVY provides partial wage-loss compensation; PMSMA provides monthly antenatal check-ups; and JSY supports institutional delivery.
IGMSY was introduced in 2010 as a pilot conditional maternity-benefit scheme and later served as the forerunner of PMMVY.
PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on
the ninth day of every month

secs.t: Economic empowerment and Ujjwala → ministry → key facts

x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh lends to intermediary NGOs and micro-finance institutions, which in turn provide micro-credit to poor women.
Under DAY-NRLM, an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh annually is termed a
Lakhpati Didi
The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is offered through the Ministry of Finance and India Post, has a two-year tenure, permits deposits from ₹1,000 to ₹2 lakh, and carries 7.5% interest.

secs.t: Economic empowerment and Ujjwala → ministry → key facts — Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana — free LPG for BPL women

x: Women hold over 55% of PM Jan Dhan accounts, about 70% of MUDRA loans go to women, and female LFPR is near 37%.
PMUY is under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, was launched on 1 May 2016 at Ballia, and provides LPG connections to women of BPL households.

secs.t: AP women's welfare schemes and delivery network

x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 annually to eligible mothers, with a 75 per cent attendance condition, and was described as a restructured form of Amma Vodi.
YSR Cheyutha, introduced in 2020, provides ₹18,750 annually to BC, SC, ST and minority women in the 45–60 age group.
YSR Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa was introduced in 2022 and provides marriage assistance to poor brides belonging to SC, ST, BC and minority communities.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: NCRB put the rape conviction rate at 27.2% in 2018 and 27.8% in 2019, prompting demands for more fast-track courts and stronger standards.
The stated demands include extending fast-track courts and establishing national minimum standards for One Stop Centres and shelters.
Talliki Vandanam is described as a conditional cash transfer, while Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is approximately 1.7.

rows.title: SC/ST rights - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 164, 244, 330, 332, 335; abolition of untouchability
sub: Group-II S3-16: Untouchability and caste-based atrocities; the legal response
Group-II S3-31: Constitutional provisions for Scheduled Castes - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 330, 332, 335, 338

secs.t: Untouchability and Scheduled Castes — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — Article 17 — provision

x: The Constitution does not define ‘untouchability’.
Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.

secs.t: Untouchability and Scheduled Castes — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — Terms → meaning

x: The Mysore HC read 'untouchability' as the historically developed practice, not its literal meaning.
Untouchability involves both the stigma of ritual pollution attached to people and the practices adopted by the rest of society to protect itself from that supposed pollution.
Manual scavenging is described as the “
worst surviving symbol of untouchability

secs.t: Untouchability and Scheduled Castes — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — FIRSTs

x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, given statutory shape in the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first official SC list followed in 1936, after which 'Scheduled Castes' replaced the earlier 'Depressed Classes' in official usage.
The first list was issued through the
Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950

secs.t: Articles → subject (SC/ST rights, Part XVI) — Article-subject matching (incl. STs)

x: Article 275(1)
provides grants-in-aid for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas, including funds associated with the Tribal Sub-Plan.
Articles 243D and 243T
provide for reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State
to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation

secs.t: Articles → subject (SC/ST rights, Part XVI) — Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes

x: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes.

secs.t: Articles → subject (SC/ST rights, Part XVI) — Traps

x: Exam angle: straight "which Article" questions (Art. 46 asked three times; Art. 17 twice).
Exam angle: "educational and economic interests of SCs/STs" =
Art. 46
(G2/GS 2018, 2019); "untouchability abolished" =
Art. 17

secs.t: Articles 341, 342 and 330, 332, 334 — SC lists and reserved seats

x: Exam angle: CDX AP History (p.424) credits "Article 344" with adding castes to the list - that is wrong; Art. 344 is the Official Language Commission. The power is
Art. 341
(and 342 for STs).
The Supreme Court struck down Bihar's 2015 notification in
July 2024
, reaffirming that a State cannot alter the Scheduled Caste list.

secs.t: Amendments and cases → provision (reservation and sub-classification) — Amendments → purpose

x: Exam angle: G2 2024 asked which amendment allows relaxation of qualifying marks in promotions - the correct answer is the
82nd
; the key circulated for that paper says 89th, which is the NCSC-NCST bifurcation amendment.
The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.

secs.t: Amendments and cases → provision (reservation and sub-classification) — Milestones and cases

x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A).
Andhra Pradesh

became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute, through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 (Punjab had done so earlier, in 1975, only by an executive circular).

secs.t: Amendments and cases → provision (reservation and sub-classification) — AP categorisation and aftermath

x: The Commission recommended four groups: A comprising Relli and others, B Madiga, C Mala and D Adi-Andhra.
Telangana
became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.

secs.t: Commissions → role (NCSC, NCST and others)

x: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission examines SC status for Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam; its term was extended to 10 June 2026.
The 89th Constitutional Amendment created the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A, and it began functioning from
19 February 2004
The joint commission became constitutional in 1990, and the 89th Amendment (2003) split it into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under new Article 338A.

secs.t: Acts and schemes against untouchability and manual scavenging — Laws enforcing Article 17

x: The PoA Act was enacted in 1989 and the Rules were framed in 1995; the framework includes special courts and State and district vigilance and monitoring committees, with a 60-day limit for police investigation.
The 2013 Act prohibits manual scavenging, unsafe cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and requires identification and rehabilitation.

secs.t: Acts and schemes against untouchability and manual scavenging — PCR offences

x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
SRMS began in 2007, was revised in 2013 and 2021, provided one-time cash assistance of ₹40,000, and was subsumed in NAMASTE.
All four statements correctly describe NAMASTE: its two ministries, zero sanitation deaths goal, allocation of ₹349.70 crore, and the stated stipend and health coverage.

secs.t: Persons → statements and contributions

x: B.R. Ambedkar
ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
Bhagya Reddy Varma established
Jagan Mitra Mandali
in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.
The Adi Hindu Social Service League was originally founded as
Manya Sangham
in 1911 and was renamed later.
Bezwada Wilson, associated with the Safai Karmachari Andolan, received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2016.

secs.t: Movements and incidents → place and year — Movements

x: Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore in 1924–25 and was organised by T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon, with K. Kelappan also associated with it.
The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
The Safai Karmachari Andolan campaigns against
manual scavenging
and is associated with Bezwada Wilson.

secs.t: Movements and incidents → place and year — Major incidents → state

x: Tsundur occurred in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh on 6 August 1991, where Dalits were massacred by dominant-caste villagers.
The Karamchedu incident of 1985, in which Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords, sparked the independent Dalit movement.
In the Hathras case, the Supreme Court entrusted monitoring to the Allahabad High Court.

secs.t: Books and papers → authors

x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.
Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam was modelled on Kalidasa’s
Meghaduta
Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, Annihilation of Caste by B.R. Ambedkar, Gulamgiri by Jyotiba Phule and Jatimimamsa by Sree Narayana Guru.

secs.t: Data — SC population, seats and enforcement

x: Census 2011 records 1,241 caste groups notified as Scheduled Castes across States/UTs.
In Andhra Pradesh,
the SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population
Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema
recorded the highest SC population share at 24.85%.
The Scheduled Caste literacy rate in Andhra Pradesh is given as

secs.t: Caste atrocities — causes and social boycott

x: Religious causes
are not included in the stated list.
All four factors—caste hierarchy, upper-caste dominance, rising Dalit activism and political interference—are identified as contributing factors.
The 2017 NCRB crime head covered persons forced to leave their residence or facing social boycott.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Madiga Dandora movement and the 2000 Andhra Pradesh Act initiated the sub-classification debate within the Scheduled Castes, which culminated in the Davinder Singh judgment of 2024.
A major criticism is that untouchability is not constitutionally defined, allowing newer indirect forms to potentially escape effective penal consequences.
The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and stated that any change would require a holistic empirical review.

rows.title: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and amendments; Civil Rights Protection Act 1955
sub: Group-II S3-32: Statutory provisions for SCs - PoA Act 1989, Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955

secs.t: PCR Act 1955 and PoA Act 1989 — definitions, terms and FIRSTs

x: Since 1 July 2024, references to the IPC and CrPC in the Act are read as references to the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
The Act was enacted in 1989, commenced in 1990, amended in 2015, Section 18A was inserted in 2018, and its application extended to Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.
The 2015 amendment defined economic boycott and social boycott and made them offences amounting to atrocities under the Act.

secs.t: Sections → offence / provision (PCR and PoA) — PCR Act — sections

x: Section 3 deals with religious disabilities, including barring entry to or worship in public places of worship.
Section 15A provides for State duties such as legal aid, special courts, surveys of untouchability-prone areas, awareness measures and related implementation duties.
(both MPPSC 2019 key facts): Section 5 covers refusal of admission to hospitals, dispensaries and educational institutions, and Section 12 raises a presumption when the victim is an SC member.

secs.t: Sections → offence / provision (PCR and PoA) — PCR offences and punishment

x: Exam angle: Untouchability (Offences) Act "extends to the whole of India"; MPPSC accepted both "cognizable and triable summarily" and "cognizable and non-compoundable".
For a first offence, the stated punishment is imprisonment of one to six months and a fine of ₹100 to ₹500.
Under Section 15, offences under the PCR Act are cognizable and may be tried summarily; they are also non-compoundable (MPPSC 2019 accepted both descriptions).

secs.t: Sections → offence / provision (PCR and PoA) — PoA Act — sections

x: Section 4 punishes wilful neglect of duty by public servants.
An appeal, including an appeal against a bail order, lies to the High Court within
90 days
Section 18 bars anticipatory bail (CrPC Sec. 438, now Sec. 482 BNSS) and Section 19 denies probation to convicts.

secs.t: Sections → offence / provision (PCR and PoA) — PoA — other key provisions

x: Special Courts are set up in each district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants.
States must ensure legal aid, travel and maintenance for victims and witnesses, and identification of atrocity-prone areas.

secs.t: Rules, machinery and implementing bodies

x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional machinery: State-level chairmanship by the Chief Minister, district-level chairmanship by the Collector, a Secretary-level nodal officer, and Protection Cells under an IG or ADGP.
The relief under the PoA Rules was fixed in 2016 at
Rs 85,000 to Rs 8.25 lakh
, paid under a centrally sponsored scheme shared 50:50.

secs.t: Amendments and cases → outcome (2015, 2018, Mahajan, Chauhan) — PoA Amendment Act, 2015

x: Tonsuring, forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass and dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi are recognised acts under the amended framework.
The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.
A new chapter on the
rights of victims and witnesses
was introduced by the 2015 amendment.

secs.t: Amendments and cases → outcome (2015, 2018, Mahajan, Chauhan) — Dilution and restoration

x: In
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
, decided on 20 March 2018, the Supreme Court issued directions concerning preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest.
The 2018 Amendment Act inserted
Section 18A
The power to grant relief or quash proceedings is available where no prima facie case exists; statement 3 reverses this condition.

secs.t: Amendments and cases → outcome (2015, 2018, Mahajan, Chauhan) — Case / law → outcome

x: Exam angle: G2 2024 - the case "alleged to have diluted" the Act =
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan
The correct sequence is Mahajan judgment in March 2018, recall in October 2019, Prithvi Raj Chauhan in February 2020 and Kiran in 2025.
The Supreme Court cancelled the High Court's anticipatory bail, held that Section 18 applies where a prima facie case exists and stated that a mini-trial is impermissible at the bail stage.

secs.t: Manual scavenging — Acts, cases and schemes

x: The 1993 Act prohibited employing manual scavengers and constructing dry latrines.
Local authorities are required to conduct surveys and build sanitary latrines within
three years
NAMASTE formalises sewer and septic-tank workers, subsumed the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers, and aims at zero sanitation fatalities.
Offences under the 2013 Act are
cognizable and non-bailable
; a first contravention attracts up to 1 year or Rs 50,000, and hazardous sewer cleaning up to 2 years or Rs 2 lakh.

secs.t: Data — NCRB and Andhra Pradesh enforcement — National data

x: Crimes against Scheduled Tribes declined by 23.1%, crimes against Scheduled Castes by 3.6%, and Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar were the leading States mentioned for crimes against Scheduled Castes.
The 26-month duration, compared with the 60-day limit, illustrates chronic pendency and delay in investigation.

secs.t: Data — NCRB and Andhra Pradesh enforcement — Andhra Pradesh

x: Andhra Pradesh has 14 Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Laxmipet in Srikakulam.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The task force report proposed higher relief, counselling, State relief cells, and transmission of FIRs and charge-sheets to the authorities within 24 hours.
The debate includes allegations of misuse, concerns regarding low convictions, and criticism that counter-FIRs may intimidate complainants.
The Sukanya Shantha decision held that
Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma
, expanding the understanding of untouchability beyond narrow physical exclusion.

rows.title: Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation
sub: Group-II S3-35: Constitutional and statutory provisions for Backward Classes - Articles 15(4), 16(4), 338B; commissions

secs.t: Reservation — definitions, Articles and FIRSTs — Definition

x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
Indra Sawhney held that backward classes under Article 16(4) are identified mainly by
caste and social backwardness
, not by economic criteria alone.
SEBC means
Socially and Educationally Backward Classes

secs.t: Reservation — definitions, Articles and FIRSTs — Articles → content

x: Exam angle: "which article was added to overcome Champakam Dorairajan" → 15(4).
Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and recommend remedial measures.
Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment to overcome
P.A. Inamdar (2005)
, which had barred quotas in private unaided institutions; it excludes minority institutions and is the basis of the CEI Act, 2006.

secs.t: Commissions → year → findings

x: Exam angle: "commission on reservation in government employment" =
Mandal
B. The Kalelkar Commission itself used low
caste

status (with lack of education and poor representation in government service, trade and industry) as criteria; it was the Central Government that refused to accept caste as the criterion, so the report was not implemented.

secs.t: Commissions → year → findings — Justice G. Rohini Commission - sub-categorisation of OBCs

x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
The creamy-layer criteria were framed through
the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee
The Commission, set up in October 2017 and given 14 extensions, submitted its report to the President on
31 July 2023
(some sources say October 2023); the report is not yet public.

secs.t: Cases → rulings

x: Indra Sawhney accepted caste as a possible main criterion, prescribed the general 50 per cent ceiling and excluded the creamy layer.
The 11 March 2026 verdict held that parental salary alone cannot determine creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts.
The creamy-layer principle for excluding socially advanced OBCs was introduced through the
Indra Sawhney
decision.

secs.t: Amendments → Article → content

x: Exam angle: match amendment to clause.
The
77th Constitutional Amendment Act
, 1995 inserted Article 16(4A) to provide reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, in response to the Indra Sawhney judgment.
The 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A), the 81st dealt with backlog vacancies, the 82nd inserted the proviso to Article 335, and the 85th provided consequential seniority.

secs.t: Acts and orders on the central OBC quota

x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.

secs.t: Creamy layer and EWS — criteria and income limits

x: The income ceiling was revised to
₹8 lakh per annum
in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
Andhra Pradesh aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central creamy-layer threshold of ₹8 lakh.
The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.

secs.t: AP BC groups → quota

x: BC-D consists of other classes.

secs.t: AP commissions, cases and GOs on BC quota — History

x: The
Anantharaman Commission
was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.

secs.t: AP commissions, cases and GOs on BC quota — Kapus

x: The quota began at 20 per cent in 1984, rose to 34 per cent for the specified elections, and was later reduced to 24.15 per cent under the cited Government Orders.
All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A criticism noted in the reservation debate is that approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts remain vacant.
BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand
are identified as live reservation issues in Andhra Pradesh.
On 12 September 2026, the Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to add a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.

rows.title: Scheduled Tribes - Forest Rights Act 2006, Fifth and Sixth Schedules, TSP, Eklavya schools
sub: Group-II S3-8: Tribal problems and tribal development approaches - isolation, assimilation, integration
Group-II S3-34: Statutory provisions for STs - Forest Rights Act 2006, PESA Act 1996
Group-II S3-41: Welfare programmes for SCs and STs - scholarships, hostels, special component plan, TSP

secs.t: Scheduled Tribes — definition, identification and FIRSTs

x: The stated sequence is proposal by the State, examination by the Registrar General of India and NCST, consideration by the Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).
ST status is religiously neutral
(RPSC 2010 key): it does not depend on the religion professed.
Bharia of Madhya Pradesh
was the first PVTG mentioned as receiving habitat rights; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
Birsa Munda is popularly known as
Dharti Aaba
Although RoFR can expand to “Right of First Refusal” in another usage, the Andhra Pradesh usage here is “
Recognition of Forest Rights

secs.t: Tribal problems → causes and effects

x: All three statements correctly identify problems associated with tribal communities: loss of habitat, educational and linguistic disadvantages, malnutrition, forced labour and displacement.
The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.
The stated concerns of the Koya and Kondh communities include land rights, inadequate compensation and displacement without proper rehabilitation.

secs.t: Tribal revolts → year → leader → issue

x: Santhal Hul was led by Sidhu and Kanhu (a-ii); Birsa's Ulgulan by Birsa Munda, Dharti Aaba (b-iv); the Rampa rebellion by Alluri Sitarama Raju (c-i); the Srikakulam Girijan movement by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam (d-iii).
The correct sequence is Santhal Hul (1855–56), Birsa’s Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa rebellion (1922–24), and Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967–70).

secs.t: Persons → approaches and statements on tribes

x: Isolation seeks to keep tribes apart for cultural protection; assimilation seeks their absorption as ‘backward Hindus’; integration combines development with retention of identity.
The isolation approach is associated with
early Verrier Elwin
and sought to keep tribes apart to protect their culture.
Assimilation views tribes as ‘backward Hindus’ to be absorbed and is associated with G.S. Ghurye and N.K. Bose, including Bose’s Hindu method of tribal absorption.

secs.t: Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development — five principles

x: The first principle is to develop tribal people along their own genius, respecting their distinct capacities and culture.
The first three statements are Panchsheel principles.

secs.t: Institutions → year → role

x: NSTFDC was set up in 2001 by splitting the SC/ST corporation, is a not-for-profit (Section 8) company and runs the Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana.
NCST functions from 19 February 2004 under Article 338A, inserted by the 89th Amendment, 2003, and has civil-court powers.
The GCC purchases minor forest produce at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers.
The APSCCFC provides self-employment support, including rehabilitation of Jogin women under the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis Act, 1989.

secs.t: Sub-plans — TSP to DAPST

x: The Tribal Sub-Plan originated in 1972 and was adopted in the Fifth Plan; the Special Component Plan became SCSP and later DAPSC; DAPST is the present ST-focused form.
All three are objectives of TADP/ITDA: agricultural improvement, fruit-bearing plantations and other income-generating activities in tribal areas.
The monitoring shift occurred in January 2017, online monitoring covers 41 ministries, and Andhra Pradesh enacted a 2013 law binding proportional allocation.

secs.t: Schemes → year → key facts — Area and habitation programmes

x: PM-JANMAN focuses on houses, roads, water, Mobile Medical Units and hostels;
industrial mining leases
are not among the stated focus areas.
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan has an outlay of
Rs 79,156 crore
The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission is run by TRIFED and focuses on buying Minor Forest Produce at MSP, value addition and GI tags.

secs.t: Schemes → year → key facts — SC/ST economic empowerment

x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016 under the Ministry of Finance and targets at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch for a greenfield enterprise.
Stand-Up India provides loans ranging from
Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore

secs.t: Schemes → year → key facts — SC welfare - DACE, SHRESHTA, NAMASTE

x: SHRESHTA places bright SC students in top residential schools through the National Testing Agency’s NETS test.
NAMASTE, launched in 2022, seeks to end manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks and promote mechanised sanitation.
NAMASTE involves the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, is implemented by NSKFDC and has an allocation of Rs 349.70 crore.

secs.t: Education schemes — EMRS, hostels, scholarships

x: The tribal residential schools in Andhra Pradesh are run by the Andhra Pradesh Tribal Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (
APTWREIS
), known as Gurukulam.
The SC Post-Matric Scholarship is the largest central SC scheme with 60:40 cost sharing, while the specified ST scholarships are classified as stated.
The ST pre-matric scholarship covers Classes IX and X; the post-matric scholarship applies thereafter.

secs.t: Forest Rights Act 2006 — provisions — Basics

x: The Act’s full title concerns recognition of forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional
Forest Dwellers
, and its stated objective was to undo historical injustice to forest dwellers.
Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before
13 December 2005
for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.

secs.t: Forest Rights Act 2006 — provisions — Rights and ceiling

x: The Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce, community forest resource management and PVTG habitat rights.
Habitation and self-cultivation
are individual rights.
Forest land may be diverted for public utilities such as schools and dispensaries on Gram Sabha recommendation, with the stated limit of up to one hectare per project.

secs.t: Acts, cases and linkages — forest, wildlife and land law

x: Exam angle: the right to fell and transport
bamboo
comes from the
FRA
, not the IFA amendment.
MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete; this position was repeatedly upheld by the Supreme Court.
Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable

secs.t: Fifth Schedule, PESA and AP land laws — PESA States

x: In PESA areas, at least 50 per cent of seats go to Scheduled Tribes and all chairpersons are Scheduled Tribes.
The strengthening measures include an election manual, an MFP training manual and model Gram Panchayats.
AP is among the 10 PESA States, and 9 of the 10 have framed rules while Odisha has only draft rules.
AP has 2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas under the AP PESA Rules 2011.

secs.t: Fifth Schedule, PESA and AP land laws — AP land regulations and cases

x: The Samatha judgment held that land in Scheduled Areas cannot be transferred or leased to non-tribals or private companies, including private mining companies.
The case arose against the background of mining leases in the
Visakhapatnam Agency
, where the AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation was enforced.
Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas can prevent alienation and restore illegally alienated land belonging to Scheduled Tribes.

secs.t: Data — FRA titles, VDVKs, loans and AP indicators

x: More than 47,900 CFR/CFRR claims were rejected.
About
23.92 lakh individual and 1.22 lakh community titles
had been distributed, covering 233.48 lakh acres.
The tribal maternal mortality ratio and infant mortality ratio are both above the State average.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Parasnath Hills have both Jain pilgrimage significance and Santhal religious significance, and the dispute is discussed in relation to Articles 25, 26, 29, the Fifth Schedule and Article 244.
Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan aims at
20 lakh grassroots change leaders across 1 lakh tribal villages in 30 States and Union Territories
The issues concern funding for CFR management, alleged disregard of FRA in Agasthyamalai eviction orders, and the wider development-versus-consent debate.

rows.title: Child rights - Articles 21A, 24, 39(e)(f); UNCRC; Right to Education Act 2009
sub: Group-II S3-39: Provisions for children - Article 21A, RTE Act, JJ Act, POCSO, child labour law

secs.t: Articles and amendments on children — number game

x: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A, revised Article 45 regarding early childhood care up to six years, and added the parental duty in Article 51A(k).
Article 45
was substituted by the 86th Amendment to provide for early childhood care and education until children attain six years of age.
The sequence is Unni Krishnan (1993), the Constitution Amendment Bill (July 1997), the 86th Amendment (December 2002), and Pramati (2014).

secs.t: Cases → issue decided on child rights

x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
(2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.
Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act, while Bachpan Bachao Andolan addressed trafficking, circus children and FIRs concerning missing children.

secs.t: UNCRC 1989 → numbers, rights, principles and protocols

x: The four core principles include non-discrimination, best interests of the child, life-survival-development, and respect for the child’s views.
India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005, but is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol.
The sequence is 1989 adoption of the UNCRC, 1992 Indian accession, 2000 adoption of two Optional Protocols, and 2011 adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol.

secs.t: RTE Act 2009 → sections, dates and numbers — Basics

x: Exam angle: statement pairs - "6-14 years" and "enacted under Art. 21A" are both correct (APPSC answer: both).
Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
The RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A, covers children aged 6-14 (elementary education, Classes 1-8, in a neighbourhood school) and came into force on 1 April 2010.

secs.t: RTE Act 2009 → sections, dates and numbers — Teachers and numbers

x: The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the
National Council for Teacher Education
(NCTE).
The original no-detention provision extended up to Class VIII, while the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after regular examinations and a re-examination opportunity.

secs.t: RTE Act features — included vs not included

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2017 asked the odd one out - "Central government has sole responsibility for funds" is NOT a feature.

All four are features of the RTE Act: it prohibits screening and capitation fee, physical punishment, mental harassment and private tuition by teachers, and provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children.

secs.t: Bodies and Acts → composition, powers and mandate

x: NCPCR and SCPCRs review, monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act.
The specified monitoring mandate includes the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009.
HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, while the adoption route under the Juvenile Justice Act is open to all religions.

secs.t: Policies, schemes and campaigns → year and features

x: The Centre-State sharing pattern is
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan was launched in 2001 and was followed by Samagra Shiksha in 2018.
Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into an integrated school education framework.
The National Policy for Children, adopted in April 2013, treats every person below 18 as a child.

secs.t: Helplines and portals → purpose

x: TrackChild handles tracking of missing and found children, Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting, and CARINGS relates to child adoption information and guidance.
e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights.
CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline and is now integrated with ERSS-112.

secs.t: Child indicators — data

x: The NFHS-5 figures stated are an infant mortality rate of 35.2, an under-five mortality rate of 41.9 and a total fertility rate of 2.0.
The figures refer to working children aged 5–14 years.
The child sex ratio (0-6) was 914 in Census 2011.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The DPDP Act, 2023 defines a child as a person below 18 years and requires verifiable parental consent for processing the child's data.
POCSO defines a child as below 18 years, child labour law uses the below-14 threshold stated here, and RTE covers children aged 6–14 years.
All three are identified areas of criticism and debate: the age of consent, arbitrariness in the JJ transfer system and vacant RTE quota seats.

rows.title: Juvenile Justice Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment 2016
sub: Group-II S3-24: Child abuse - forms, causes, consequences and the legal framework
Group-II S3-25: Child labour - magnitude, causes, legislation and rehabilitation

secs.t: Child abuse and child labour — forms, causes and effects

x: Child labour is recognised as a form of abuse; India is described as having the largest number of child labourers in the world, with debt bondage extending across generations.
Lack of affectionate relationships is a cause, while deviant behaviour such as drug abuse and stealing is a consequence.
Brick kilns, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals and tea stalls are all identified sectors or settings associated with child labour.

secs.t: Data — abuse, crimes, child marriage and child labour — Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD)

x: Kidnapping and abduction
were reported as the largest categories of crimes against children in 2024.
NCRB 2021 data reported that
of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child.
The study found that
two out of three
children faced physical abuse.
The study concluded that
boys were as much at risk as girls

secs.t: Data — abuse, crimes, child marriage and child labour — Child marriage

x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14.

secs.t: Juvenile Justice Acts → year and provisions — Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

x: A heinous offence is defined by a minimum punishment of
seven years or more
The Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 was the first uniform law and prescribed an age of 16 years for boys and 18 years for girls.
The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by
the Delhi gang rape case of 2012

secs.t: Juvenile Justice Acts → year and provisions — 2021 Amendment

x: The Board comprises a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class serving as Principal Magistrate and two social workers, with at least one woman among the social workers.
The Juvenile Justice Board handles children in conflict with law, whereas the Children's Court, a Sessions Court, tries cases transferred to it.
The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.

secs.t: POCSO Act 2012 → sections, punishments and amendments — Full name, enforcement, age definition

x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the
Ministry of Women and Child Development
POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child and applies in a gender-neutral manner.
The IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.

secs.t: POCSO Act 2012 → sections, punishments and amendments — Offences and procedure

x: POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography.
Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting, Sections 29–30 place the burden of proof on the accused, and Section 22 deals with false complaints, subject to the good-faith exception.
POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.

secs.t: POCSO Act 2012 → sections, punishments and amendments — Amendments

x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years.
POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012, and the 2019 amendment set a minimum of 10 years (extendable to life) for penetrative sexual assault.

secs.t: Age of consent — evolution, committees and courts

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2022 - the MP High Court asked the Centre to lower the age of consent to 16 because
social-media exposure brings earlier puberty
The 2012 Standing Committee supported 18 years, the 2023 Law Commission warned against lowering it, and the Supreme Court suggested a Romeo-Juliet clause in January 2026.

secs.t: Child labour laws and committees → year and provisions

x: Exam angle: the year 1986. The "adolescent" category came only in 2016.
The Gurupadswamy Committee identified
poverty
as the root cause of child labour and recommended banning hazardous work while regulating the rest.
The amendment made offences cognizable, prescribed imprisonment and fines, and provided for a Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund.
The 2016 amendment created the adolescent category (14-18), banned only from hazardous occupations and processes; children below 14 are banned from all occupations.

secs.t: Constitution, policy and institutions → role

x: Mission Vatsalya covers former child-protection services as well as CWCs, JJBs and DCPUs.
Article 39(e) concerns protection of tender age from abuse, while Article 39(f) concerns protection against exploitation and moral and material abandonment.
The widened concept includes sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal.
The widened definition covers the specified forms of trafficking
irrespective of consent

secs.t: Portals, helplines, operations and schemes → purpose

x: The cybercrime portal cybercrime.gov.in is used for CSAM and other online abuse, under the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and the Ministry of Home Affairs.
PENCIL is the online portal for effective enforcement of
the amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
PENCiL
(Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment on 26 September 2017.

secs.t: International conventions, days and cases

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2003 key "All of the above": the Constitution, the SC judgment of 10 Dec 1996 and the UN Charter.
The 2011 Bachpan Bachao Andolan case emphasised stricter enforcement and the rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers.
ILO Convention No. 138 concerns the Minimum Age for Employment, whereas Convention No. 182 concerns the Worst Forms of Child Labour.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — JJBs, CWCs, operations and rescues

x: Andhra Pradesh had Boards in the erstwhile 13 districts, undertook selection for bodies in the 13 new districts, and its Juvenile Welfare Department also runs the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
Operation Chinnari-Thalli includes Sexual Offender Sheets, zero pendency in POCSO cases and chargesheets within 60 days.
The
Women & Child Safety Wing
conducts “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programmes in schools and hostels.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Per the APPSC 2022 key, the parliamentary standing committee on home affairs was taken to have recommended lowering the age, for applying POCSO, from 18 to 16.
The cited criticisms are that the transfer system can erode rehabilitation and that POCSO can criminalise consensual adolescent relationships.
In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court flagged misuse of POCSO in consensual adolescent relationships and urged
a “Romeo-Juliet” clause
