rows.title: Child welfare - ICDS, POSHAN Abhiyaan, mid-day meal (PM POSHAN), child marriage, malnutrition
sub: Group-II S3-43: Welfare programmes for women and children - ICDS, POSHAN, Mission Shakti, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

secs.t: ICDS and Anganwadi → services and functionaries

x: Exam angle: "Anganwadi worker is a functionary of which scheme?" → ICDS; count and names of the six services.
Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the Anganwadi Centre, whereas immunisation, health check-up and referral services are delivered through the health system.
Cash maternity benefit
is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.
All four statements correctly describe the Anganwadi Worker, Anganwadi Helper and the joint AWW-ASHAs role in HBYC home visits.

secs.t: Nutrition missions → launch, funding and targets

x: One Nation One Anganwadi enables migrant families to continue receiving benefits for children below six years and pregnant or lactating women after migration to another State.
Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 merges Anganwadi Services/SNP, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
POSHAN Abhiyaan targets stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight.
POSHAN Abhiyaan envisages a Suposhit Bharat and a Jan Andolan, with the stated goal of reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.

secs.t: Nutrition campaigns, tools and early childhood care → terms — Campaigns and tools

x: Poshan Tracker data represents a census of children enrolled or covered at Anganwadi centres, while NFHS data is survey-based; therefore, the two are not strictly comparable.

Poshan Tracker relates to real-time monitoring, Poshan Vatika to nutrition gardens, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi to ECCE and play-based pedagogy, and Poshan Pakhwada to brain development in the first six years.

secs.t: Nutrition campaigns, tools and early childhood care → terms — Weeks and fortnights - ministry

x: The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.
Andhra Pradesh has 1,030 Hub Anganwadi Centres associated with ITC and Pratham.
Bal Vatika was brought under
PM POSHAN
as part of the school nutrition framework.
Article 45
provides for ECCE for children up to six years.

secs.t: Mid-day meal to PM POSHAN → origin, norms and features — Origin and renaming

x: The scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 as the
National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
(NP-NSPE).
PM POSHAN is a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented under the
National Food Security Act, 2013
PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools and provides one hot cooked meal.

secs.t: Mid-day meal to PM POSHAN → origin, norms and features — Aims and features

x: All four statements describe features of PM POSHAN: mandatory district-level social audits, school nutrition gardens, additional nutrition in specified districts, and participation of FPOs and SHGs.
In Andhra Pradesh, the Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal was extended to Intermediate Classes XI-XII in 2024-25, covering 27.97 lakh students and providing five eggs, three chikkis and ragi java per week.

secs.t: Maternal and girl-child schemes → launch, ministry and benefit — Maternal health schemes

x: Exam angle: PMSMA launch year (2016, G2-GS 2022); JSY sits under NHM, while PMMVY sits under MWCD.
JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns with free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.

secs.t: Maternal and girl-child schemes → launch, ministry and benefit — Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)

x: BBBP is implemented under
Sambal
, the safety component of Mission Shakti.
Balika Samriddhi provides a birth grant and scholarships; Dhanalakshmi is a conditional cash-transfer pilot; BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign; Sukanya Samriddhi matures at 21 years.
MWCD is nodal (with Health and Education) and BBBP aims to reverse the falling Child Sex Ratio.

secs.t: Child marriage → Act, data and models

x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
West Bengal, Bihar and Tripura
were identified among the States with the highest child-marriage levels in the cited NFHS-5 data.
Under PCMA 2006 a child marriage is voidable at the option of the minor party, not automatically void.

secs.t: Child protection → Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES, Palna

x: Under
Mission Vatsalya
, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.
Mission Vatsalya was introduced in 2021–22 for child protection and the promotion of a happy childhood, in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
PM CARES for Children was launched in 2021 for children who lost parents or specified guardians to COVID-19 and provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at 23, along with education and health support.

secs.t: Women's credit, livelihood and welfare schemes → year and objective

x: DAY-NRLM
, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
Swavalambini was associated with 2022 and promoted entrepreneurship among women students in the North-East through MSDE and NITI Aayog.
PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA age limits apply
to all citizens irrespective of religion
The criticism is that the schemes still emphasise survival rather than complete child development, while last-mile gaps persist in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
Tithi Bhojan began in Gujarat, and PMMVY is identified as the only cash maternity benefit written into the National Food Security Act.

rows.title: Rights of persons with disabilities - RPwD Act 2016, UNCRPD, accessibility (Sugamya Bharat)
sub: Group-II S3-38: Provisions for persons with disabilities - RPwD Act 2016 and accessibility measures

secs.t: Constitutional basis, UNCRPD and days → Article and year

x: The UNCRPD was adopted on 13 December 2006, India ratified it in October 2007, the RPwD Act was enacted in 2016, and it came into force on 19 April 2017.
The proposal for a national minimum disability pension of Rs 8,000 per month has been linked with
Article 41
, which refers to public assistance in cases of disablement.

secs.t: RPwD Act 2016 → provisions and number game

x: Section 2(s) covers long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full participation in society.
The Act increased specified disabilities from 7 to 21, includes conditions such as autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease, and permits the Central Government to add more disabilities.

secs.t: Institutions → basis and mandate

x: The Inclusive India initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, associated with the National Trust, seeks to bring persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream.
The
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
is the statutory authority under the RPwD Act, 2016, responsible for monitoring implementation and taking up complaints.
The National Trust Act, 1999 covers autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities and provides for welfare and legal guardianship.

secs.t: Schemes and campaigns for PwDs → purpose — Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan)

x: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on
3 December 2015
as a flagship initiative for universal accessibility.
The three verticals are accessibility in the
built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem
The Sugamya Bharat App functions as a crowdsourcing platform through which accessibility gaps can be reported.
Accessible booths and Braille-enabled EVMs are measures for accessible elections.

secs.t: Schemes and campaigns for PwDs → purpose — Welfare schemes

x: UDID provides a single national disability identity and certificate.
The
ADIP
scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.
SIPDA provides grant-in-aid for implementing the RPwD Act.
Monthly disability pension is not one of the six scholarship components.

secs.t: Schemes and campaigns for PwDs → purpose — Entrepreneurship and livelihood

x: Divya Kala Shakti showcases the artistic talent of persons with disabilities and is associated with the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal provides UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for employment opportunities.
ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise established in 1972 and manufactures aids and artificial limbs.

secs.t: Disability rights cases and rulings → issue

x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned deplaning and dignity; Vikash Kumar recognised a scribe as reasonable accommodation; Rajive Raturi concerned mandatory accessibility standards.
Jeeja Ghosh concerned the deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy by an airline, raising the right to dignity and resulting in compensation.
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC
(2021) recognised the availability of a scribe as reasonable accommodation even without benchmark disability.

secs.t: Inclusive education and AP disability welfare

x: Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities.
From 18 March 2026, free APSRTC bus travel is available in the specified categories to persons with
40 percent
or more disability.
The Corporation supplies aids and appliances and runs economic-rehabilitation schemes for persons with disabilities and senior citizens.

secs.t: Disability data → Census 2011, Census 2027, AP figures

x: India’s Census 2011 figure was 2.21 percent, whereas the approximate global estimate was about 16 percent; the difference suggests under-reporting in India.
Movement disability
was the largest among the cited categories at 20.3 percent, followed by hearing at 18.9 percent and seeing at 18.8 percent.
The figures are orthopaedic 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.90 lakh, visual 2.03 lakh, multiple 1.96 lakh and mental 1.02 lakh.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court directed attention to prison accessibility and revision of prison manuals in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
The Supreme Court recognised digital access as part of Article 21 while citing the
United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
The 1995 Act recognised seven disabilities, the 2016 Act recognises 21, and the Census 2027 categories are criticised as narrower than the Act’s 21 categories.

rows.title: Rights of the elderly - Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007, schemes

secs.t: National policies → year, ministry and focus

x: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 defines an older person as an individual aged
60 years or above
Compulsory military service for older persons
is not part of NPOP 1999.
All three statements reflect the focus of the National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011.
NPHCE was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in

secs.t: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 → provisions and Sections

x: Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
permits the Tribunal to declare such a property transfer void when the promised care is not provided.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was enacted in 2007; NPOP was issued in 1999; NPHCE began in 2010–11; and NPSC dates to 2011.

secs.t: Elderly schemes and helpline → ministry and benefit

x: The scheme provides aids such as walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids and dentures to BPL senior citizens.
The four components of AVYAY are the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line.
Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana, introduced in April 2021, was renamed from the
National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
Elder Line is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment with State emergency response centres and technical support from
Tata Trusts and NSE Foundation

secs.t: Elder abuse, international frameworks and days → year

x: HelpAge India
runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.
Such victims may approach
the Revenue Divisional Officer
(RDO).
The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers the period
World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on
15 June
The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing dates to 2002.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposed floor is specifically intended to be indexed to inflation.
Weekly geriatric OPDs function in 1,684 PHCs and daily geriatric OPDs in 177 CHCs in Andhra Pradesh.
Himachal Pradesh
enacted the Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001, the first such State law.

rows.title: Population problem, ageing and problems of the elderly
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-107

secs.t: Population terms and growth phases → meaning

x: The correct sequence is decline during 1911–1921, the Great Divide in 1921, population explosion during 1961–1971, and high but slowing growth during 1981–2011.
The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.
The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.

secs.t: Population data → Census, TFR and age structure

x: Decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.7%, not 27.7%.
Bihar
recorded the highest total fertility rate in NFHS-5, at 3.0.
SRS 2024 reported India’s TFR at 1.9, rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
SRS 2024 gives the working-age population share as 66.4% and the children’s share as 24%.

secs.t: Effects of population growth and control debates → factor and effect

x: About
9.7 million
new working-age people enter each year, and a large workforce pays off only if employed.
All four statements reflect the environmental case for population control and the counter-debate concerning the possible demographic and fiscal disadvantage of southern States.
The draft policy moves from population control to management, offers Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removes the two-child norm for local elections.

secs.t: Problems of the elderly and family change → issue and data

x: Ageing does not eliminate health expenditure; persons aged 80 and above face chronic disease, insurance may have age caps, and the elderly account for about 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
Ageism and abuse
are recognised social problems faced by elderly persons; loneliness and feminisation of ageing are also important concerns.
Care within joint families is weakening, while over 55% of the elderly live in nuclear households, highlighting changing family support arrangements.

secs.t: Policies and schemes for the elderly → year and FIRSTs

x: Kerala
is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.
Under AVYAY, the SAGE component provides equity support of up to
₹1 crore
for senior-care start-ups.
NPHCE was launched in
, after the National Policy on Older Persons of 1999 and before the National Policy on Senior Citizens of 2011.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh’s population is stated as 495.77 lakh, accounting for 4.09% of India’s population and placing it 10th.

India introduced the first national family planning programme in 1952, Kerala was first with the senior-citizens institutional framework, and Andhra Pradesh is associated with the draft Population Management Policy.

rows.title: Transgender persons - NALSA judgment, Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019
sub: Group-II S3-40: Provisions for the elderly and transgender persons

secs.t: Transgender identity — definitions and terms

x: The 2019 definition includes trans men and women, intersex variations, genderqueer persons and specified socio-cultural identities including kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.
The transgender community has sought horizontal reservation, which would cut across the SC, ST, OBC and General categories.

secs.t: Cases and Bills → year, mover, holding

x: Both statements are true, and the direction to extend reservation in education and employment explains the treatment of transgender persons as socially and educationally backward.
The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by
Tiruchi Siva
of the DMK.
In August 2026, the Centre assured the Supreme Court that identity cards issued before the 2026 Act would remain valid.

secs.t: Acts and Rules → provisions: 2019 Act vs 2026 Amendment

x: Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation.
The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under
the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
The Transgender Persons Rules, 2020 prescribe the application procedure through the national portal for obtaining the certificate of identity.

secs.t: Bodies → composition and role: NCTP, NHRC

x: The Council has governmental, expert and community representation and performs advisory and monitoring functions.
The 2026 amendment provides for one State or Union Territory representative each from the North, South, East, West and North-East, by rotation.
The NHRC Advisory 2.0 recommended Census categories for
intersex persons, trans men and trans women

secs.t: Schemes → ministry, components, benefits — SMILE scheme

x: SMILE stands for
Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
The transgender component includes scholarships, PM-DAKSH skilling and a PM-JAY-linked health package.
Garima Greh provides
shelter homes for transgender persons
The National Portal for Transgender Persons provides online applications for a certificate and identity card.
Invalidity and old-age pensions are included in
Concurrent List Entry 24

secs.t: Schemes → ministry, components, benefits — AP - NTR Bharosa Pension

x: NTR Bharosa provides
per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.
The cited rates are Rs 6,000 for persons with disabilities, Rs 10,000 for chronic diseases, Rs 15,000 for fully disabled persons and Rs 4,000 for transgender persons.

secs.t: Persons → contributions and FIRSTs

x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.
Joyita Mondal
of West Bengal became India’s first transgender judge in a Lok Adalat in 2017.
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific region to address the
United Nations General Assembly

secs.t: States, AP and Census data

x: Karnataka
became the first State to provide one per cent reservation for transgender persons in all government jobs in July 2021.
Kerala
was the first State to formulate a transgender policy, in 2015.
Census 2011 counted approximately
4.88 lakh
transgender persons in India.
Tamil Nadu set up the Transgender Welfare Board in 2008.

secs.t: Reservation debate and criticism

x: The issue resurfaced through a Mumbai protest against
Maharashtra
’s reply to the Bombay High Court in June 2023.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.
NHRC Advisory 2.0 included admission by self-identified gender, a ban on non-consensual intersex surgery on children and more Garima Grehs.
RVY was launched at Nellore.

rows.title: Minority rights - Articles 29 and 30, National Commission for Minorities, Sachar Committee, schemes
sub: Group-II S3-36: Constitutional and statutory provisions for minorities - Articles 29, 30; National Commission for Minorities
Group-II S3-42: Welfare programmes for BCs and minorities - education, skill and credit schemes

secs.t: Minority — meaning, notified communities, FIRST/last — Meaning

x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in
Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B
, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
The Act does not define minority; under
Section 2(c)
a minority is any community notified by the Central Government.

secs.t: Minority — meaning, notified communities, FIRST/last — Unit for minority status

x: Exam angle: G2 2017 - minority status is decided by the State's demography (true); "minority rights are
absolute
" is the untrue statement (APP's "absolute right" wording for Art. 30 should not be used in MCQs).
In T.M.A. Pai Foundation, the
State
was treated as the unit for determining minority status, rather than the whole of India.

secs.t: Minority — meaning, notified communities, FIRST/last — Notified minority communities

x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.
The first five communities were notified in 1993 and Jains were added in 2014.
Jains
were added on 27 January 2014, increasing the number of nationally notified minority communities from five to six.
The six nationally notified minority communities together account for approximately 19 percent of India's population.

secs.t: Articles → provisions: 29, 30, 347, 350, 350A, 350B — Articles 29 and 30

x: Article 30(2)
provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
The
44th Amendment
, which removed the right to property, added Article 30(1A) so that removal of that right does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions and compensation is ensured on acquisition.

secs.t: Articles → provisions: 29, 30, 347, 350, 350A, 350B — Linguistic minority Articles

x: The 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956, linked to the reorganisation of States, inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is styled the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (office set up in 1957).

Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

secs.t: Cases → year and holding

x: In re Kerala Education Bill held the Article 30 right is not absolute and the State may impose reasonable conditions (regulating standards); St. Stephen's (1992) let an aided minority college prefer its own community up to about 50%; T.M.A. Pai (2002) made the State the unit for minority status; P.A. Inamdar (2005) barred State reservation quotas in unaided institutions, minority or non-minority.

secs.t: Commissions and bodies → status, composition, powers — National Commission for Minorities - evolution

x: Exam angle: G1 2022 - "set up under the NCM Act 1992" is correct; the claim that the Ministry of Welfare notified five communities was the rejected statement.
The milestones are correctly matched as 1978–non-statutory Commission, 1992–statutory NCM Act, 1993–first statutory Commission and 1995–addition of Vice-Chairperson.
The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 2006, and Haj management was added to its responsibilities from
October 2016

secs.t: Commissions and bodies → status, composition, powers — NCM - composition and appointment

x: The Commission has seven members: a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
Harjit Singh Grewal
was appointed NCM Chairperson in July 2026.

secs.t: Commissions and bodies → status, composition, powers — NCM - functions and powers

x: The Commission may summon witnesses and call for records while conducting an inquiry.

secs.t: Commissions and bodies → status, composition, powers — Other bodies

x: The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures;
conducting elections to minority educational institutions
is not one of its stated functions.
The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers.

secs.t: Committees and commissions → chair, findings

x: The Sachar Committee was chaired by Rajinder Sachar, the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities by Justice Ranganath Misra, and the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee by Amitabh Kundu.
The Sachar Committee was the
Prime Minister’s High Level Committee on the social, economic and educational status of Muslims

secs.t: Regimes compared → year, members, controls

secs.t: Funding pattern and terms → meaning

x: VB-G RAM G stands for Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).
PM-KISAN, PM Vishwakarma, DILRMP and SEED are Central Sector examples, while the Urban Challenge Fund is also Centrally Sponsored.
The general pattern is 60:40, changing to 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 100 per cent Central funding for Union Territories without legislatures.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major debate concerns whether funding should follow a normative allocation formula or remain demand-driven.
States now bear the unemployment allowance.
The CAG audit found that the planned convergence was not achieved.
On the AP side, Amaravati is a
HRIDAY
city.

rows.title: Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - infrastructure, industry, energy, digital

secs.t: Industry and MSME schemes → features

x: Startup India provides a three-year tax holiday, permits self-certification under nine labour and environment laws, and provides for winding up in 90 days.
MUDRA loans are collateral-free up to
₹10 lakh

(APPSC 2022 key), i.e. across all three slabs: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000-5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5-10 lakh). ₹50,000 and ₹5 lakh are only the upper limits of Shishu and Kishor; ₹1 crore is far beyond MUDRA's range.

secs.t: Infrastructure programmes → objective

x: PM Gati Shakti, launched in October 2021, is a GIS-based National Master Plan for integrated multimodal connectivity planning across ministries.
DFCs are built by DFCCIL; NHAI builds Bharatmala highways.
The stated figures are 657 running UDAN routes, expansion to 120 new destinations, and Indian logistics costs of about 13–14 percent of GDP.

secs.t: Energy programmes → objective and ministry

x: UJALA is associated with the
Ministry of Power
and promotes LED bulbs and energy-efficient appliances through EESL.
PAHAL transfers LPG subsidy directly to bank accounts and is associated with the
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
The Scheme for New and Novel Uses of Hydrogen funds startup pilots and is implemented by NISE and BIRAC.

secs.t: Digital programmes → purpose

x: ONDC is an open network for digital commerce promoted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (
DPIIT
BharatNet, 5G, UPI, Aadhaar, DigiYatra and FASTag form the identified DPI backbone.
Fabs, display and ATMP incentives belong to the India Semiconductor Mission; IndiaAI covers compute, datasets and AI innovation.

secs.t: Data → infrastructure, energy and digital figures

x: Renewable capacity grew from about 40 GW in 2015 to about 260 GW in 2025.

secs.t: Scheme → implementing ministry and nodal agency

x: SIDBI is associated with MUDRA refinance and the Fund of Funds for Startups; IREDA is the renewable-energy financing arm; and NHAI is associated with Bharatmala highways.
NICDC is associated with
industrial corridors and smart industrial cities under DPIIT
EESL implements UJALA and REC is the nodal agency for DDUGJY and Saubhagya, while KVIC is associated with PMEGP and Solar Charkha.

secs.t: Scheme → launch year (quick revision)

x: Make in India was launched in 2014, Digital India in 2015, Startup India in 2016 and Atmanirbhar Bharat in 2020.
Atmanirbhar Bharat was launched in May 2020, not May 2019.
PAHAL was launched in November 2014 and rolled out nationwide in January 2015.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
PM Surya Ghar drive
in Andhra Pradesh is identified as a current-relevance issue.
High logistics costs, low R&D spending and the continuing need for support to DISCOM finances are all identified challenges.
The Andhra Pradesh angle includes three industrial corridors, VCIC’s association with the Asian Development Bank, and a top-four rank in rooftop solar.

rows.title: Important policies and programmes of the Government of Andhra Pradesh - welfare and social security
sub: Group-II S3-45: Welfare programmes of the Government of Andhra Pradesh - social security and welfare schemes

secs.t: Welfare packages → pillars and old name → new name

x: Exam angle: scheme → benefit matching, and old name → new name.
Navaratnalu was the nine-pillar welfare framework associated with the period
Navaratnalu was the previous government’s welfare package and was funded from revenue expenditure.
The Aarogyasri scheme, introduced in 2007 as Rajiv Aarogyasri and renamed Dr YSR Aarogyasri in 2019, is now known as
Dr NTR Vaidya Seva

secs.t: Super Six and sector schemes → beneficiary and benefit

x: Talliki Vandanam is intended to reduce the cost of schooling and raise the
Gross Enrolment Ratio
Stree Shakti provides free bus travel for women and transgender persons having Andhra Pradesh domicile.
Stree Shakti was launched on 15 August 2025, was later extended to PwD, and women's share of bus travel rose from 40% to 65%.
The earlier
Deepam, launched in 1999
, provided LPG connections, whereas Deepam-2 provides three free LPG cylinders a year.
Thalliki Vandanam provides
per year to mothers of school-going children.
YSR Vahana Mitra provided ₹10,000 annually to self-owned auto or taxi drivers, while the current Auto Driver Sevalo provides ₹15,000 annually to owners of self-owned autos.
Talliki Vandanam replaced
Jagananna Amma Vodi
(launched January 2020), which credited ₹15,000 a year to the mother/recognised guardian of a poor child sent to school or college (APPSC 2023).

secs.t: Social security pensions → amount, age and categories

x: Exam angle: the ₹3,000 → ₹4,000 revision and the 60/18 age limits.
Arya Vysya, Brahmin, Kapu, EBC, Kamma, Reddy and Kshatriya communities received the same ₹3,000 to ₹4,000 enhancement.
NTR Bharosa Pension covers elderly persons, widows, single women, weavers, fishermen and artisans; it is not a universal pension for all formal-sector employees above 18 years.
NTR Bharosa Pension provides monthly pensions ranging from
to eligible beneficiaries.

secs.t: NTR Bharosa → data, spending and delivery — Beneficiaries

x: SERP
is the nodal agency for NTR Bharosa pensions.
The 16th Finance Commission found Andhra Pradesh to have the highest
per-capita social security pension spending
among States.
NTR Bharosa pension expenditure was estimated at
₹27,719 crore

secs.t: NTR Bharosa → data, spending and delivery — Delivery and recent changes

x: The Chief Minister stated that
the family
should be the unit for welfare, including family mapping before sanctioning new pensions.
Pension distribution is automated using
Aadhaar-based biometric authentication
, intended to eliminate ghost beneficiaries.
Andhra Pradesh supplements the central NSAP pension amount with funds from the State government.
There were 63.12 lakh pensions, monthly expenditure was ₹2,744 crore, and payments used biometric Aadhaar-based authentication.

secs.t: Health schemes → coverage and indicators

x: The model announced in May 2025 proposed annual coverage up to ₹25 lakh for about 1.65 crore poor and middle-class families and was announced by Y. Satya Kumar Yadav.
The 104 service operates mobile medical units providing fixed-day village health services, whereas 108 provides emergency ambulance services.
The Universal Health Policy provides free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh for every citizen, while poor persons receive treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
Dr NTR Vaidya Seva gives cashless care to 1.43 crore families for 3,257 procedures and is linked with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

secs.t: Women and child schemes → purpose

x: YSR Sampoorna Poshana provides supplementary nutrition to
pregnant and lactating women and children aged 6–72 months
through Anganwadis.
YSR Cheyutha gave ₹18,750 a year to BC/SC/ST/minority women aged 45-60, linking them to livestock units and Pasu Kisan Credit Cards.
One Stop Centre
s provide police, medical, legal, counselling and shelter support to women facing violence under one roof.

secs.t: Women and child schemes → purpose — Nutrition and anganwadis

x: Sampoorna Poshana/Poshana Plus provides
richer take-home rations through Anganwadi Centres
In 2024–25, Sampoorna Poshana was delivered as
Bala Sanjeevani
in plain areas.
Aasara provided ₹633.74 crore by DBT to 69,597 SHG members in 2024–25.
The name Cheyutha first belonged to a 1998 TDP scheme for handicapped persons; it was later used for YSR Cheyutha.
SERP works with 84.47 lakh rural women, while MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh urban SHGs.

secs.t: Women and child schemes → purpose — Women's safety

x: The Disha Bill, 2019 proposed completion of
investigation within 7 days and trial within 14 days
, making the total period 21 days.
The Disha Bill proposed amendments to
the Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure
for dealing with sexual offences against women.
OSCs are part of MWCD's Mission Shakti with Shakti Sadan, and are backed by Women Helpline 181.

secs.t: Community-specific welfare → beneficiary

x: Chandranna Pelli Kanuka covered SC, ST, BC, minorities and disabled persons; YSR Kalyanamasthu covered the same broad groups; Shaadi Tohfa was for Muslims; Dulhan was for Muslim brides and began in April 2015.
The monthly assistance is ₹5,000–10,000, the annual expenditure is ₹180 crore, Urdu is the second official language, and Haj and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance is provided.

secs.t: Food, housing, sanitation and water → targets and data — Food security

x: The proposal was to provide 5 kg of rice for every family member, with the family treated as the unit for distribution.
Door delivery of ration through mobile dispensing units began in 2021.
Anna Canteens provide subsidised meals primarily for the urban poor.
Anna Canteens provide a meal priced at ₹5.

secs.t: Food, housing, sanitation and water → targets and data — Housing

x: The stated Housing for All target was 7.60 lakh houses by 2026, using convergence between PMAY-U and PMAY-G and tracking through CFMS.
The AP State Housing Corporation, also referred to as APHCL, runs the Weaker Section Housing Programme with the motto “Housing for All”.
The policy provides house sites of
3 cents in rural areas and 2 cents in urban areas
for every eligible homeless household by 2029.

secs.t: Food, housing, sanitation and water → targets and data — Sanitation and water

x: CLAP focuses on door-to-door collection of segregated garbage and sanitation activities across Andhra Pradesh.
Waste-to-energy units, compost units and Material Recovery Facilities are associated with CLAP outcomes.
CLAP recorded 96.07% waste segregation at source, processing of 6,890 tonnes daily and 104 functioning STPs.
CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021, not on 15 August 2025.

secs.t: Delivery machinery, FIRSTs and poverty goals

x: e-Seva was introduced in 2001, followed by MeeSeva as a single-window service, and Village/Ward Secretariats were introduced in 2019.
Direct Benefit Transfer through the JAM trinity helps
reduce ghost beneficiaries and middlemen
in welfare delivery.
Swarna Andhra @2047 aims to end extreme poverty by 2030 and attain high-income status by 2047.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that new welfarism prioritises DBT and tangible transfers over public goods and places pressure on State finances.
Kerala’s pension amount is ₹2,000 per month and its delivery is shifting towards DBT; Andhra Pradesh is identified as having the highest per-head social-pension spending among States.
The Opposition alleged that the Super Six programme had been only partly delivered and that pensions had been cut.

rows.title: Important policies and programmes of the Government of Andhra Pradesh - agriculture, industry, IT and infrastructure

secs.t: Swarna Andhra@2047 — vision frame, goals and summit

x: Swarna Andhra@2047 provides the framework for
the 2024–29 policies and industrial corridors
in Andhra Pradesh.
The net-zero target is 2047 and is associated with the Integrated Clean Energy Policy and APSES 2024–25.
The five panels are energy and fuel-cost optimisation; DeepTech; space and defence manufacturing; BioValley; and agri-tech, water and blue economy.

secs.t: Agriculture schemes → year → benefit

x: YSR Jala Kala gives free borewells to small and marginal farmers, and e-Crop digitally books the crop on every field each season (basis for insurance, input subsidy and procurement).
PMFBY coverage in Andhra Pradesh rose with extreme-weather losses, and the specified farmer premium rates apply; the scheme has been voluntary for all farmers since Kharif 2020.

secs.t: Policies → G.O. → department → goal — "(4.0) 2024-29" policy suite

x: The Industrial Development Policy targets large investment and higher project categories; the MSME policy carries the One Family, One Entrepreneur approach; the Food Processing Policy promotes value addition and cold chains; and the Electronics Manufacturing Policy has the stated production, investment and employment targets.
The Industrial Development Policy 4.0 was issued as G.O.Ms.68 by the Industries & Commerce (P&I) Department.

secs.t: Policies → G.O. → department → goal — Startups and IT

x: Exam angle: acronym expansion (LIFT), issuing department, and which policy carries which slogan.
In August 2026, the Cabinet cleared the draft AP PPP Policy-2026 with VGF of ₹1,500 crore and the draft AP Omnibus Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026.
The policy covers solar, wind, hybrid energy, pumped storage, green hydrogen and ammonia, biofuels, storage and EV charging.

secs.t: Terms and project classes → meaning

x: A large project has fixed capital investment exceeding ₹501 crore and up to ₹1,000 crore.

secs.t: Acts and Cabinet drafts → year → provision

x: APCRDA was established under the
APCRDA Act, 2014
The Aqua Authority regulates aqua farms, aquaculture seed and aquaculture feed under the AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020.

secs.t: Agencies and portals → function

x: BhuSeva assigns a unique
Bhudhaar number
to each land parcel as part of its integrated land-records system.
AP FiberNet is a fibre grid launched in 2017 to provide
low-cost broadband, television and telephone
services to homes and offices.
Real Time Governance
operates through a command centre at the Secretariat for real-time monitoring of services and grievances.

secs.t: Places and projects → district → feature — Industrial hubs and nodes

x: 12 new projects were approved in August 2024, taking the total to 20, with Orvakal and Kopparthy identified for Andhra Pradesh.
Kopparthy is associated with
an electronics manufacturing cluster and an NICP node
in YSR Kadapa district.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid Amaravati's foundation stone on 22 October 2015; the capital region is run by APCRDA under the APCRDA Act, 2014.

secs.t: Places and projects → district → feature — Irrigation and ports

x: The Polavaram Project is located on the
Godavari River
All four statements are correct regarding Polavaram’s legal status, progress, target year and 2024–25 budget provision.
Ramayapatnam is a greenfield port on the
south coast of Andhra Pradesh
The reduction in Machilipatnam port limits from 64 km to 15 km was made under the
Indian Ports Act, 2025

secs.t: Data and ranks — investment, power, budget

x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in 2016 jointly with Telangana, and in 2017 and 2019.
The SIPB is chaired by the
Chief Minister
; in 2024-25 it approved 8 projects worth ₹2,45,275 crore with 65,541 jobs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The industrial initiatives signify Rayalaseema’s transformation from a drought-prone region into an industrial hub.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 2,61,393 MSMEs set up in 2024–25 and ranked sixth in exports.
The Cabinet cleared the drafts of the PPP Policy-2026 and Omnibus EoDB Act 2026.
The PanIIT Summit 2026 is scheduled at Vijayawada on 3 October 2026 to shape a DeepTech roadmap for Swarna Andhra@2047.
